name: Sharefun Studio
significance: Chinese animation studio known for producing Scissor Seven (2018–present), the first Chinese animated series on Netflix. Uses TVPaint animation software. Known for small-team, auteur-driven production under creator He Xiaofeng.

name: Bagdasarian Productions
significance: American entertainment company founded by Ross Bagdasarian Sr., creator of Alvin and the Chipmunks. Revived by his son Ross Bagdasarian Jr. and Janice Karman in 1977. Produced all Chipmunks media including the 1983 animated series (with Ruby-Spears), The Chipmunk Adventure (1987), the CGI/live-action film series (2007-2015), and ALVINNN!!! and The Chipmunks (2015-2023).

name: Classic Media
significance: American entertainment company that acquired and managed a vast library of classic animated properties including the Rankin/Bass catalog, Lassie, Casper the Friendly Ghost, and others. Produced new content based on legacy properties. Acquired by DreamWorks Animation in 2012 and subsequently absorbed into NBCUniversal.

name: Silvertoons
significance: American freelance animation studio (Silvertoons, Inc.) founded in 1992 by British-born character designer Stephen Silver. Silver is best known as the lead character designer for animated series including Kim Possible (2002-2007), Danny Phantom (2004-2007), and Clerks: The Animated Series (2000). Has provided character design services for Disney Television Animation, Sony Feature Animation, and Nickelodeon Animation. Also operates the Silver Drawing Academy for character design education. Silver is the author of The Silver Way, one of the best-selling books on character design. Served on the Animation Guild executive board.

name: Yash Raj Films
significance: One of India's largest and most prestigious film production and distribution companies, founded by Yash Chopra in 1970. Partnered with Walt Disney Pictures for Roadside Romeo (2008), India's first major CGI animated feature co-production with a Hollywood studio. Primarily a live-action studio known for Bollywood blockbusters.

name: Kobayashi Shokai
significance: Early Japanese film production and distribution company active in the silent film era. Produced Jun'ichi Kōuchi's Namakura Gatana (1917), the oldest surviving Japanese animated film. One of the pioneering companies in Japanese cinema during the Taishō era.

name: Palermo Estudio / Raindogs Cine
significance: Uruguayan animation studio (Palermo Estudio) based in Montevideo. Directed by Alfredo Soderguit. Produced Anina (2013), Uruguay's notable animated feature. Co-produced Lila's Book (2017) with Colombia's Fosfenos Media, contributing to visual design and story development. Soderguit also collaborated as scriptwriter with Federico Ivanier. Active in the growing Latin American animation scene, participating in Ibero-American co-productions.

name: Sunrise Productions
significance: South African computer animation studio founded in 1998 by Phil Cunningham and Jacqui Cunningham. Originally launched in Zimbabwe before establishing primary operations in Cape Town (Noordhoek). Best known for producing the Jungle Beat franchise, a dialogue-free animated series about animals in an African jungle that has aired in 180+ countries and amassed over 5 billion YouTube views with 10+ million subscribers. Created Africa's first-ever animated feature film. Also a world leader in sports mascot creation and branding, partnering with Juventus FC, Welsh Rugby Union, English RFU, and South African Rugby (Springboks). Produced Jungle Beat: The Movie (2020), a Mauritian-South African co-production, and The David Movie (with Slingshot USA/Angel Studios).

name: Domerica
significance: Japanese animation studio based in Tokyo. Notable productions include The World Ends with You: The Animation (2021, based on Square Enix game), Seven Knights Revolution: Hero Successor (2021), Romantic Killer (2022, Netflix), Touken Ranbu Kai: Kyoden Moyuru Honnōji (2024), Fermat Kitchen (2025), and Gnosia (2025). Also contributed additional animation for Persona 5 Royal cutscenes. Works frequently with game IP adaptations.

name: Asahi Production
significance: Prolific Japanese animation studio (旭プロダクション) established June 1, 1973, in Nerima, Tokyo. Initially a specialized shooting studio and PR video company, subcontracting for Tokyo Movie Shinsha (now TMS Entertainment) and Sunrise. Over 50+ years, evolved into one of anime's most widely-credited support studios, providing photography, finish animation, in-between animation, 2D/3D CGI, and production assistance for hundreds of anime. Clients include Sunrise, Madhouse, David Production, SILVER LINK., Diomedea, and TMS Entertainment. Contributed to major franchises including Doraemon, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Mobile Suit Gundam: Iron-Blooded Orphans, Gintama, Sailor Moon Crystal, and Blade Runner: Black Out 2022. 165 employees. Subsidiaries include XuYang Donghua and Shiroishi Studio.

name: The Nacelle Company
significance: American diversified media company founded in 2017 by Brian Volk-Weiss, headquartered in Los Angeles. Originally spun off from New Wave Entertainment's Comedy Dynamics division. Known for documentary series The Toys That Made Us, The Movies That Made Us (Netflix), Down to Earth with Zac Efron (Emmy-winning, Netflix), and Behind the Attraction (Disney+). Expanded into animation with the NacelleVerse shared universe, acquiring 1980s–90s toy IP rights including Biker Mice from Mars, Wild West C.O.W.-Boys of Moo Mesa, and RoboForce. Launched RoboForce: The Animated Series (2025). Also operates NacelleBooks publishing and Nacelle Consumer Products divisions.

name: Digital Frontier
significance: Japanese CG animation studio (デジタル・フロンティア) that began producing CG works in 1994 as a division of TYO Image Enterprise. Became an independent company (Digital Frontier Inc.) in 2000. One of Japan's premier CG/3D animation studios. Notable works include the Appleseed CG films, CG for the live-action Death Note films, Kingsglaive: Final Fantasy XV (CG production), Infini-T Force (full production), and Mirai (CG). Created iconic character reveal trailers for Super Smash Bros. for Wii U and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, including the 'World of Light' cutscenes. Parent company changed from TYO Inc. to Fields Corporation in 2010. Subsidiaries in Malaysia and Taiwan.

name: Kokusai Eiga-sha
significance: Also known as MIC (Movie International Company), founded in 1974 by associates of Nikkatsu films. Best known for producing the J9 Series trilogy (Braiger, Baxingar, Sasuraiger) and other mecha anime of the early 1980s including Space Warrior Baldios. The studio went bankrupt in the mid-1980s. Notable for commissioning early scores by Joe Hisaishi (Sasuraiger) and for producing anime with distinctive genre-blending approaches.

name: Cookie Jar Entertainment
significance: Canadian animation production and distribution company. Formerly known as CINAR Corporation (rebranded 2004). Produced and distributed numerous children's animated series including MetaJets (co-production with Sunwoo Entertainment), Johnny Test, and many others. Acquired by DHX Media (now WildBrain) in 2012.

name: Quad
significance: Japanese animation studio (株式会社JFK), officially known as JFK Co., Ltd., founded May 1, 2018 by Naoto Awano and former members of AIC and Production IMS. Based in Nerima, Tokyo (relocated from Suginami in 2023). Notable productions include Miss Kuroitsu From the Monster Development Department (2022), My Life as Inukai-san's Dog (2023), I'm the Evil Lord of an Intergalactic Empire! (2025, for TV Asahi's ANiMAZiNG!!! block), and I'm Living with an Otaku NEET Kunoichi!? (2025, 24 episodes + 2 OVAs). A newer but increasingly productive entrant in the anime industry.

name: E&G Films
significance: Japanese animation studio (also known as Easy Film/イージー・フイルム) originally established in 1971 as E&G World Pro by ex-Toei animator Shiro Murata. Renamed E&G Films in 1988 after absorbing photography studio Lucky More (who provided photography services for Grave of the Fireflies). Best known for Invincible King Tri-Zenon (2000), one of the first fully digital TV anime productions on TBS. The studio worked on several co-productions with major broadcasters.

name: Yumeta Company
significance: Japanese animation studio (株式会社ゆめ太カンパニー, Yumeta Co., Ltd.) originally founded March 5, 1986 as Shizuoka Animation Co., Ltd. by former Tama Production animator Satoshi Yamaguchi. Renamed Yumeta Company in October 1990. Became a TYO subsidiary in 2005 alongside Hal Film Maker and Doga Kobo. In July 2009, absorbed Hal Film Maker to form TYO Animations Inc. Acquired by Memory Tech Holdings' Graphinica in December 2017 and reverted to Yumeta Company name. Based in Kiyose, Tokyo. Primarily operates as a subcontracting and production assistance studio, providing key animation, in-between animation, finishing, and coloring services for major anime productions including Dragon Ball Super, One Piece, Boruto, and Naruto Shippuden.

name: Hampa Studio
significance: Valencia-based Spanish animation studio founded in 1997, established as an independent production company in 2006. One of the largest animation companies in Spain with 150+ employees. Known for Cry Babies and My Talking Tom. Received Goya awards, EFA nominations (Best European Animated Film), Annie Award nominations. Co-producer on the Serbian sci-fi series 2142.

name: The World of 2142
significance: Serbian animation production company, main producer of the ambitious sci-fi animated series 2142 (8 x 45'), a Serbian-Spanish co-production with Hampa Studio. The series blends class wars, augmented reality, and end-of-the-world myths in a dystopian setting aimed at young adults and adults. Presented at Cartoon Forum 2025 where it was among the five most-watched projects. Written by Mina Sablic Papajic, Kristina Djukovic, Nedeljko Kovacic, and Pavle Zelic. Features 3D computer animation. Led by producer Mladjen Merdovic.

name: The Answer Studio
significance: Japanese animation studio (アンサー・スタジオ) founded June 2004 by Motoyoshi Tokunaga from 35 former Walt Disney Animation Japan staff members after Disney closed its Tokyo studio. Carries forward the animation heritage of Disney's Japanese operations (which had produced work on Gargoyles, Aladdin TV series, The Tigger Movie, 101 Dalmatians II, and other Disney projects since 1984 as Pacific Animation/Walt Disney Animation Japan). Notable productions include Golgo 13 (2008 TV series), Transformers: Animated (key animation), Flag (2006, pioneering internet-distributed mecha anime directed by Ryōsuke Takahashi), Tower of God Season 2, and Anne Shirley (2025). Active subcontractor for major studios.

name: Chuse Animation
significance: Chinese 3D animation studio (初色动画 / formally Beijing Chuse Meike Animation Technology Co., Ltd., 北京初色美刻动画科技有限公司) founded October 15, 2014 by Wu Wenpeng. Headquartered in Beijing's Chaoyang district. Specializes in sci-fi CG donghua. Known for productions including Sihai Jingqi (四海鲸骑), Galaxy Heart (银河之心), Black Gate (黑门), and The Knight (夜的命名术). Part of the growing Chinese 3D animation industry producing web novel adaptations for Bilibili.

name: Riki Group
significance: Major Russian animation studio and media holding company, founded in 2003 in Saint Petersburg by Ilya Popov and team. Creators of the internationally successful Smeshariki (KikoRiki) franchise, which has aired in 100+ countries, been translated into 50+ languages, and accumulated a daily audience of 50 million viewers. The company includes Petersburg Animation Studio, Aeroplane Production Center, Marmalade Media (licensing), 4Screens (YouTube content), and a publishing house. Also produces BabyRiki, The Fixies, PinCode, and Tina & Tony. Multiple feature films including Kikoriki: Team Invincible and Kikoriki: Déjà Vu.

name: miHoYo Anime
significance: Internal animation division of miHoYo Co., Ltd. (trading globally as HoYoverse/Cognosphere), the Chinese video game development company founded February 13, 2012 by Cai Haoyu, Liu Wei, and Luo Yuhao — three Shanghai Jiao Tong University students with a shared passion for anime culture. Produces animated shorts, promotional videos, and narrative cinematics for the company's game franchises (Honkai Impact 3rd, Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, Zenless Zone Zero). Collaborates with external animation studios including ufotable, Studio TRIGGER, Fantasier Animation, and RED DOG CULTURE HOUSE. Also co-produced full anime series adaptations. HoYoverse's global presence includes offices in Singapore, Montreal, Los Angeles, Tokyo, and Seoul.

name: Nyan Pollution-ω-
significance: Japanese anime studio (にゃんぽりゅーしょん-ω-) that produced the short-form anime Does It Count If You Lose Your Virginity to an Android? (2026), an adaptation of Yakiniku Teishoku's 4-koma manga published by Ichijinsha. The series aired from January 2026, directed by NEKO-B. A small, newer studio in the Japanese anime industry.

name: Planet Entertainment
significance: Japanese animation studio, originally known as Planet before being renamed Planet Entertainment. Specialized in adaptations of Leiji Matsumoto properties. Produced all three entries in The Galaxy Railways franchise (2003-2007) and other Matsumoto-related projects. A niche studio closely associated with one of anime's legendary creators.

name: Studio Junio
significance: Japanese animation studio (スタジオ・ジュニオ) founded by Junio Ikeda. Active from the 1970s through the 1990s. Produced the anime adaptations of Osamu Tezuka's works including Bagi, the Monster of Mighty Nature (1984 TV special). Also provided animation production services for various other anime productions. Known for maintaining close ties to the Tezuka school of animation.

name: UTV Motion Pictures
significance: Indian film production and distribution company founded in 1990 by Ronnie Screwvala in Mumbai. Acquired by The Walt Disney Company India in 2012. In animation, UTV produced and distributed several Indian animated films including Roadside Romeo (2008, a co-production with Yash Raj Films and Disney — India's first fully CGI animated feature) and co-produced the Arjun: The Warrior Prince (2012) animated film. Also funded animated television content for Indian audiences. Now fully integrated into Walt Disney Company India.

name: Soundac, Inc.
significance: American animation and production company formed in 1951 by Bobby Nicholson in Buffalo, New York. Originally a sound and film production house, relocated to the Greater Miami area in 1955. Notable for producing Colonel Bleep (1957), widely considered the first color animated TV series. The studio's Miami offices famously included a heated pool and patio. Produced various animated commercials, TV content, and industrial films throughout the 1950s and 1960s.

name: Detour Filmproduction
significance: American film production company founded in 1990 by writer/director Richard Linklater in Austin, Texas. Not primarily an animation studio — produces Linklater's live-action and rotoscope films including Before Sunrise (1995), Before Sunset (2004), Boyhood (2014), and the groundbreaking rotoscope-animated films Waking Life (2001) and A Scanner Darkly (2006). The rotoscope films, where live-action footage is traced over frame-by-frame to create an animated look, represent some of the most artistically significant uses of animation in American independent cinema.

name: Warner Independent Pictures
significance: American specialty film distribution label of Warner Bros., founded in 2003 to distribute independent and art-house films. In animation, distributed A Scanner Darkly (2006), Richard Linklater's rotoscoped adaptation of Philip K. Dick's novel starring Keanu Reeves — a landmark in rotoscope animation technique. Warner Independent Pictures was shut down in 2008 as Warner Bros. consolidated its distribution operations during the financial crisis.

name: Vodka Capital
significance: Spanish animation and entertainment company founded in 2008 by Víctor M. López (ex-CEO of Zinkia/Pocoyo), Steven J. Posner, David Cantolla (creator of Pocoyo), and Juan Perea. Focused on developing, financing, and managing cross-platform kids entertainment brands with international potential. Best known for Jelly Jamm (52×11 min, 3D animated series co-produced with RTVE and Bandai, broadcast in 150+ countries) and Bugsted (transmedia format co-produced with Televisa). In 2014, five former Vodka Capital executives partnered with Mexico's Ánima Estudios to form Ánima Kitchent in Madrid, effectively succeeding Vodka Capital's operations.

name: Thousand Words
significance: American production company involved in animated content distribution and production. Limited independent documentation available. The company appears to have been a minor or short-lived entity in the US animation and entertainment industry.

name: Studio Unicorn
significance: Japanese animation studio (スタジオ・ユニコーン) providing animation production assistance for anime television series. Handles key animation, in-between, and finishing work as a subcontractor for larger studios. Part of Tokyo's dense network of animation support studios.

name: Studio GARDEN
significance: Chinese animation studio (花园文化, Garden Culture) founded in 2015. Led by Wang Xin. Specializes in high-quality 2D animated feature films and TV series, combining traditional 2D techniques with 3D assist. Creates both original IP content and adaptations from literature, comics, and original stories. Dedicated to producing top-tier Chinese 2D animated feature films. All production handled by in-house teams. Part of China's growing premium animation production sector.

name: Goldcrest Films
significance: Independent British film production, distribution, post-production, and finance company founded in 1977 by Canadian Jake Eberts. Helped revive the British film industry in the 1980s, financing critically acclaimed films including Chariots of Fire (1981, Oscar winner), Gandhi (1982, Oscar winner), The Killing Fields (1984), and A Room with a View (1986). In animation, backed Don Bluth Entertainment and financed All Dogs Go to Heaven (1989). Nearly bankrupted by the failures of Revolution and Absolute Beginners (1985-86), sold to Brent Walker in 1987. Later resurrected as a premier post-production and sales company operating from London and New York.

name: Young Toys
significance: South Korean toy manufacturer and entertainment company (영실업) founded in 1980. Initially imported and manufactured toys for foreign companies (G.I. Joe, Power Rangers). Transformed in the 2000s by creating original IP: Tobot (transforming car-robot, 2010), which became a massive domestic hit surpassing Lego in Korean market share, generating ₩76 billion in sales. Also created Biklonz, GeoMecha, Monkart, and other brands. Tobot exported to Singapore, Thailand, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia. Acquired by Mirae-n in September 2020. Now 135+ employees. Co-produces animated series with Retrobot Animation Studios. Headquartered in Seoul.

name: Hiro Media
significance: Japanese production company (Hiro Media Associates) founded by Hiromasa Shibazaki in the mid-1980s. Active during the early Original Video Animation (OVA) boom in Japan. Produced and planned a series of direct-to-video anime, associated art books, and a monthly anime magazine. Productions include M.D. Geist (1986 OVA), California Crisis: Gun Salvo (OVA), The Humanoid (OVA), Dream Dimension Hunter Fandora (OVA), Roots Search (OVA), and Circuit Angel (OVA). Known for low-to-mid-budget OVAs that gained cult followings, particularly in the Western anime fan community.

name: Retrobot
significance: South Korean 3D CGI animation studio founded in 2008 by Lee Dahl. Based in Korea, Retrobot quickly became one of the most successful animation houses in the country after signing a co-production deal with toy maker Young Toys for the TV series Tobot (2010), which posted high ratings and was exported to many countries, especially Southeast Asia. Also produced Biklonz and Tobot Athlon. Tobot Movie: Attack of Robot Force (2017) was the studio's first theatrical release. Currently producing PotenDogs. Provides production services for series, features, and game cinematics.

name: Televisa
significance: Mexican telecommunications and broadcasting conglomerate founded January 8, 1973, through the merger of Telesistema Mexicano (est. 1955) and Televisión Independiente de México. Name derived from 'Television via Satellite.' One of the biggest TV companies in Mexico and Latin America. Operates Las Estrellas, Nu9ve, Foro TV, and Canal 5. Televisa Animation Studios is one of the oldest animation divisions in Latin America. In 2022, sold content assets to Univision Communications to form TelevisaUnivision. Relevance to animation: produced animated content including co-productions with international studios, and broadcast anime in Latin America for decades.

name: Seoul Movie
significance: Seoul-based South Korean animation studio owned by TMS Entertainment (Japan). Established in January 1990, incorporated January 10, 1994. Served as TMS's Korean production arm, providing animation services for both Japanese and Western productions. Previously known alongside 'Geumgang Planning' (predecessor of Iconix). Produced Restor Special Rescue Team (also broadcast on NHK's BS channel in Japan), Taengoo and Woollashon, and provided animation support for TMS co-productions. Went bankrupt in July 2008. Spiritual successor Soul Creative launched August 15, 2008 from former staff.

name: Woodblock
significance: Berlin-based animation studio founded in 2013 by six friends who studied at Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg's Institute of Animation in Ludwigsburg. Now a 50-strong studio with teams in Berlin, Ludwigsburg, and Los Angeles. Creates design, film, and immersive projects rooted in the animation medium. One of the only independent studios producing visuals for Las Vegas' Sphere (including ILLENIUM ODYSSEY). Has worked with Disney, Netflix, Apple, Nike, Adidas, and Greenpeace. Notable original works include Loom (award-winning short), Bye Bear, and The Shark in the Park. Expanding into ambitious sci-fi and horror-fantasy series including Space Probe.

name: Nippon Columbia
significance: Japanese record label founded October 1, 1910 as Nipponophone Co., Ltd. — one of Japan's oldest music companies. Renamed to Nippon Columbia in 1946, briefly Columbia Music Entertainment (2002–2010), then back to Nippon Columbia. Affiliated with the UK's Columbia Graphophone Company from 1931. As an anime production committee participant and music producer, involved in hundreds of anime productions providing music production services, including Action Heroine Cheer Fruits, Banished from the Hero's Party, Brave Witches, Combatants Will Be Dispatched!, and many others. Also operates the DENON label. Headquartered in Minato-ku, Tokyo. Still active.

name: Production Wave
significance: Japanese animation studio (プロダクションウェイブ) founded in 2003. Provides production assistance and subcontracting services for anime productions, handling in-between animation, coloring, and finishing tasks. Credits include production cooperation on California Crisis: Gun Salvo (OVA), in-between animation for Call Me Tonight (OVA), production assistance for Dancougar (eps 19, 24), and work on Fairy Princess Minky Momo OVA and various other anime. Part of Japan's extensive animation subcontracting network.

name: Spring House Entertainment
significance: Taiwanese animation studio (春水堂科技娛樂股份有限公司, Spring House Entertainment Inc.) founded in February 2000 by Micho Chang, a former television and music video director. Created the animated character A-kuei, a ten-year-old boy living in the fictional town of Springfall. Since January 17, 2008, operates as a subsidiary of Chunghwa Telecom Company, Ltd. Based in Taipei, Taiwan. Productions include the Akuei to Gacchinpo animated series and its sequel Tenkomori.

name: 视觉暂留 (Persistence of Vision)
significance: Chinese animation studio (视觉暂留, literally 'Persistence of Vision'). Part of China's growing independent animation scene. The studio name references the optical phenomenon fundamental to how animation works — the brain's retention of images creating the illusion of movement.

name: TED World
significance: South Korean animation production company based in Anyang, Gyeonggi Province. Produces original animated content for both domestic and international markets. Known for the Capsule Boy animated TV series, which gained popularity in both China and South Korea. Following the success of Season 1, TED World launched Season 2 and a theatrical version of Capsule Boy. The company focuses on creating family-friendly animation content with international distribution potential.

name: Tencent Video
significance: Leading online video streaming platform in China, launched April 2011 by Tencent. One of China's most popular streaming services with 117+ million subscribers. Major investor in and commissioner of Chinese animation (donghua) and anime productions. Tencent Penguin Pictures (est. 2015) is its production unit; G.CMay Animation & Film is its animation subsidiary. Productions include The King's Avatar, Grandmaster of Demonic Cultivation, and many other donghua. The Cartoon Channel has 200+ million viewers, making it China's #1 platform for teen/YA animation. Expanding internationally with partnerships for global distribution.

name: Big Bocca Productions
significance: American production company owned by Richard McWilliam, CEO of Upper Deck Company. Co-produced the animated series Huntik: Secrets & Seekers (2009–2012, 52 episodes) with Italy's Rainbow S.p.A. and Rai Fiction. Huntik was an action-adventure series created by Iginio Straffi (creator of Winx Club) featuring historical locations and European mythology. Big Bocca handled US scriptwriting and voice recording while Rainbow produced animation in Italy. The series aired on The CW4Kids in the US and Disney XD in Europe.

name: Primrose Productions
significance: British animation production company founded in 1953 by Louis Hagen Jr., the son of the financier of The Adventures of Prince Achmed. Primarily established to produce silhouette animation films by the legendary Lotte Reiniger, the pioneer of silhouette animation who created the world's first feature-length animated film (Prince Achmed, 1926). Primrose Productions produced over a dozen short silhouette films based on Grimms' Fairy Tales for the BBC and Telecasting America. Notable works include The Gallant Little Tailor (won first prize at Venice Film Festival 1955). Reiniger's last film with the studio-affiliated pipeline was The Rose and the Ring (1979).

name: Starburns Industries
significance: American animation and production studio founded in 2010 in Burbank, California by Dan Harmon (Community, Rick and Morty), Dino Stamatopoulos (Moral Orel), Joe Russo II, James Fino, and Duke Johnson. Full-service production company specializing in stop-motion, traditional 2D, and CG animation. Produced Rick and Morty (seasons 1–2) before production moved to Bardel. Co-produced Anomalisa (2015) with Paramount — the Charlie Kaufman stop-motion film nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. Other credits include HarmonQuest, The Freak Brothers (co-production), Mary Shelley's Frankenhole, and Alpha Betas. Named after Dino Stamatopoulos' character 'Star-Burns' from Community.

name: Nord-Ouest Films
significance: French film production company founded by Christophe Rossignon. Primarily known for live-action films but co-produced the animated feature Ernest & Célestine (2012), which was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and won multiple César Awards. Also co-produced Ernest & Célestine: A Trip to Gibberitia (2022). Demonstrates France's tradition of live-action producers engaging with auteur animation.

name: Ánima Estudios
significance: Leading Latin American animation studio founded in 2002 in Mexico City by Fernando de Fuentes S. and José C. García de Letona. Emerged during a period when Mexican animation had been largely dormant since the 1980s. Secured early distribution deal with 20th Century Fox Mexico. Produced Top Cat: The Movie (2011), Legends of Oz: Dorothy's Return (2014, US co-production), and the Legend Quest franchise (Netflix's first animated original series from Latin America). Also produces Cleo & Cuquín, Brave Bunnies, and Space Chickens in Space. Partnered with HBO Max/WB Animation on Aztec Batman: Clash of Empires. Studios in Mexico City, Madrid, Buenos Aires, and Canary Islands. One of the most prolific animation companies in the Spanish-speaking world.

name: Rainbow S.r.l.
significance: Italian animation studio founded in 1995 by Iginio Straffi in Loreto, Marche. Creator of Winx Club (2004–present), one of the most commercially successful European animated franchises — broadcast in 100+ countries with three theatrical films, 500+ licensees worldwide, and a Netflix live-action adaptation (Fate: The Winx Saga). Also created 44 Cats, Huntik, Mermaid Magic, and Gormiti: The New Era. Co-owned by Viacom/Paramount Global (2011–2023); collaborated extensively with Nickelodeon. Acquired Canadian studio Bardel Entertainment (2015) and Italian live-action producer Iven Group/Colorado Film (2017). Operates Rainbow CGI, Rome's largest 3D animation studio. Consistently ranks among the top global licensors. Reincorporated from S.r.l. to S.p.A.

name: Studio O
significance: French animation studio involved in producing animated content for French television and international co-productions. Part of France's robust animation production ecosystem — the largest in Europe and third largest globally.

name: Fantasia Productions
significance: ⚠️ LOW ANIMATION RELEVANCE — Limited public information available about animation-specific activities. Insufficient documentation to verify this entity's role in animation production. Consider removal from archive or provide additional sourcing.

name: Yien Animation Studio
significance: Chinese animation studio producing donghua content for the domestic market. Part of China's rapidly expanding animation production landscape driven by streaming platforms Bilibili, Tencent Video, and iQIYI.

name: Sola Entertainment
significance: Japanese creative production company (ソラ・エンターテインメント) established 2017 by former ADV Films producer Joseph Chou (CEO). Parent company of Sola Digital Arts (est. 2009), Sola Animation (est. 2022), Tenh Animation Magic, and Rainmaker Productions. Specializes in planning, development, and global distribution of anime, films, and games. Key productions include Ultraman (Netflix), Ninja Kamui, The Lord of the Rings: The War of the Rohirrim, Rick and Morty: The Anime, and Tower of God. Offices in Tokyo and Manhattan Beach, California.

name: Imagi Animation Studios
significance: Hong Kong-based CGI animation and visual effects studio established in 2000 by Imagi International Holdings Limited. Had studios in Chai Wan (Hong Kong), Los Angeles, and Tokyo with 400+ employees. Produced TMNT (2007, Warner Bros., opened #1 at US box office) and Astro Boy (2009, Summit Entertainment). Combined Hollywood storytelling with Hong Kong-based CG production. Astro Boy's box office failure led to financial crisis; studio shut down February 2010. Abandoned projects included Gatchaman, Cat Tale, The Legend of Zelda, and Tusker. Assets later acquired by Blockade Entertainment.

name: Paramount Pictures
significance: Major American film studio and distributor, one of the 'Big Five' Hollywood studios. In animation, Paramount has a long history: distributed Fleischer Studios' Betty Boop and Popeye cartoons (1930s–1940s) and Famous Studios' output. Partnered with DreamWorks Animation as theatrical distributor (2006–2012). Currently operates Paramount Animation (est. 2011), which produced SpongeBob SquarePants films, Wonder Park, Rumble, and Transformers One (2024). Parent company Paramount Global also owns Nickelodeon, one of the largest producers of animated content worldwide. Distributed the Anomalisa (2015) stop-motion film. Part of Skydance Media-Paramount merger in 2025.

name: Pictionary Art Factory
significance: Indian animation studio providing 2D and digital animation production services. Part of India's growing animation outsourcing and original content production sector, which has expanded significantly since the 2000s.

name: Enspire Studio
significance: Indonesian 3D animation studio based in Jakarta, founded by two CG industry veterans. Delivers world-class cinematics, animations, TV series, and commercials. Notably involved in the production of Girls Band Cry (2024), a Japanese anime series produced by Toei Animation — representing growing international subcontracting from Southeast Asian studios. Portfolio includes game cinematics, feature film work, commercial animation, and company profiles. One of the top animation studios in Jakarta.

name: ShadowMachine
significance: American animation and production company founded in 2005 by Alex Bulkley and Corey Campodonico in Los Angeles, with a major expansion to Portland, Oregon in 2015. Gained earliest recognition producing 200+ episodes of stop-motion for Adult Swim including Robot Chicken, Moral Orel, Mary Shelley's Frankenhole, and Titan Maximum. Produced BoJack Horseman (2014–2020) for Netflix/Tornante — one of the most acclaimed animated series of the 2010s. Animated Guillermo del Toro's Pinocchio (2022), winner of the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. Also produced Tuca & Bertie, Little Demon (FXX), In the Know (Peacock), and The Freak Brothers. Currently in production on Long Story Short, reuniting the BoJack team for Netflix. Specializes in stop-motion, 2D, and CG animation.

name: Artichoke Film Production
significance: Slovak (not Hungarian) film production company founded in 2010 by Juraj Krasnohorský, based in Bratislava. Produces animation, fiction, and documentaries using stop-motion, 3D, and 2D techniques. Pioneers in blending motion capture with 2D animation. Co-produced award-winning animated shorts including The Garden of Heart (2023, Oscar-qualifying Best Short Film at PÖFF Tallinn) and Hurikán (2025). Part of the growing Central European animation scene.

name: Lusasa Animation
significance: Taiwanese animation studio (滷沙沙動畫股份有限公司, Lusasa Animation Co., Ltd.) established in 2020. Specializes in original animation production and related merchandise development. Launched its first flagship project, The Joyful Lusasa Season 1, in 2022. Has exhibited at TIFFCOM and Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TAICCA pavilion). Based in Taipei, Taiwan.

name: Planet 55 Studios
significance: Australian animation and visual effects studio. Co-produced the animated feature film 100% Wolf (2020) and its sequel 100% Wolf: Legend of the Moonstone (TV series). Based in Sydney. Part of Australia's active animation production community alongside studios like Animal Logic and Flying Bark Productions.

name: Evil Pirate Studio
significance: Russian animation studio based in Saint Petersburg, specializing in high-quality classical and combined animation. Best known for the Cyberslav project — an ambitious animated series blending Slavic mythology with cyberpunk aesthetics that gained international attention through its striking trailer and concept art. Aims to elevate the Russian animation industry with world-class production quality.

name: Bidaya Media
significance: Leading Middle Eastern and North African production company founded in 2013 and based in Abu Dhabi, UAE (at Yas Creative Hub / twofour54 media zone). Dedicated to developing original children's content that nurtures creativity and promotes social values of empathy, tolerance, and friendship. Best known for the popular Emirati animated series Mansour (now rebooted as Mansour: Age of AI, 2024, with 2 billion+ YouTube views and 25 million unique viewers). Also developed and produced Iftah Ya Simsim, the Arabic adaptation of Sesame Street. Supported by Mubadala Investment Company and Abu Dhabi Early Childhood Authority.

name: Milo Productions
significance: Canadian animation production company (Milo Productions Inc.) founded by CEO Michael Milo and co-led with Dayrit. Creators of MuslimKids.TV, a specialty streaming service launched in 2016. Produced Time Hoppers: The Silk Road (2026), billed as the first-ever Muslim animation property to receive US theatrical distribution via Fathom Entertainment across 600+ theaters. The film explores Muslim culture during the Golden Age of Islam. 16 employees. Focus on creating safe, culturally diverse content for Muslim families.

name: Sullivan Bluth Studios
significance: Irish-American animation studio founded in 1985 by Don Bluth, Gary Goldman, John Pomeroy, and businessman Morris Sullivan after Bluth's previous Don Bluth Productions went bankrupt. Established a 42,000 sq-ft studio near Phoenix Park in Dublin with IDA Ireland support, employing 350+ people — mostly Irish trainees. Produced An American Tail (1986, partially), The Land Before Time (1988), All Dogs Go to Heaven (1989), Rock-a-Doodle (1991), Thumbelina (1994), and A Troll in Central Park (1994). One of the most sophisticated animation studios in Europe. Bluth helped establish Ballyfermot College's animation program, seeding Ireland's entire animation industry — alumni later founded studios including Cartoon Saloon. Renamed Don Bluth Entertainment in 1993. Dublin studio closed 1995 due to financial pressures. Later relocated to Phoenix, Arizona, producing Anastasia (1997) and Titan A.E. (2000) for Fox before final closure.

name: Gana Movie Animation
significance: South Korean animation-related company (Gana Entertainment), associated with Gana Publishing Co., a publisher specializing in comics. Co-produced the animated TV series Olympus Guardian (2002-2003) with SBS, SBS Productions, SBSi, and Dong Woo Animation. The series was based on 'The Greek and Roman Myths in Comics' (20 volumes) published by Gana Publishing. Active in the Korean animation and entertainment space.

name: Digital Durian
significance: Malaysian animation company (DD Animation Studio Sdn Bhd) based in Cyberjaya, Selangor. Creator of massively popular preschool franchises Didi & Friends (launched May 2014) and Omar & Hana (Islamic educational content). Started with small-scale animation and 3D modeling for oil & gas and e-learning. Characters based on Malaysian Serama chicken breed. Omar & Hana collaboration with Islamic Relief Malaysia raised significant charity funds. 51-250 employees. Mission: 'To make people happy through quality, fun and meaningful content.'

name: Grafi2000
significance: Turkish animation and comedy production company (Grafi2000 Productions) founded in 2000 by Varol Yaşaroğlu in Istanbul. Specializes in humor-based content combining IT and comedy for internet, TV, and mobile media. Created one of Turkey's first domestic cartoon series (Pembe & Mavi) and the first Turkish adult animated sitcom (Fırıldak Family, 2013, first adult cartoon to reach Turkish cinemas). Flagship IP King Shakir has become a major franchise with multiple theatrical films, TV series on Cartoon Network MENA, and a Disney+ streaming deal. Building international presence with L&M business across MENA, Latin America, and beyond.

name: Bobbypills
significance: French adult animation studio founded in 2017, based in Paris and Angoulême. Specializes in unique, transgressive adult animation with fully internalized creation process from writing to voice recording. Known for Peepoodo & The Super Fuck Friends, Vermin, Crisis Jung, and Monsieur Flap. Worked with Netflix, Ubisoft (Captain Laserhawk: A Blood Dragon Remix), and Warner Bros. (DC's Creature Commandos). Pioneered transition from Adobe Animate 2D to Blender-based CG pipelines. One of France's leading adult animation studios.

name: Animonsta Studios
significance: Malaysian animation studio (now rebranded as Monsta Studios) founded September 15, 2009 by Nizam Razak, Kee Yong Pin, Safwan Karim, and Anas Abdul Aziz — all former creators of Upin & Ipin at Les' Copaque Production. Headquartered in Cyberjaya, Selangor. Creator of the massively popular BoBoiBoy franchise, which has spawned three TV series seasons (2011–2016), BoBoiBoy Galaxy (100 episodes), theatrical films BoBoiBoy The Movie (2016) and BoBoiBoy Movie 2 (2019), and Papa Zola The Movie (2025, RM68.2M box office). Awarded MSC Malaysia status in 2011. One of Southeast Asia's most successful animation studios.

name: Barunson E&A
significance: South Korean entertainment company (Barunson Entertainment & Arts Corp.) founded in 1996 and headquartered in Seoul. Best known as the production company behind Bong Joon-ho's Oscar-winning Parasite (2019). Active in film production, investment, and international distribution. Currently co-producing Bong Joon-ho's upcoming hand-drawn animation film. Sold animated feature Gill (directed by Ahn Jae-huun, premiered at Annecy) internationally. Expanding into Southeast Asian co-productions with partnerships in Indonesia and Thailand.

name: 4th Creative Party
significance: South Korean VFX and animation studio founded in 2009 by core members of EON Digital Films. Originally headquartered in Busan, now based in Seoul's Gangnam district. One of Korea's oldest and largest VFX studios, having provided effects for over 120 features including Bong Joon-ho's Snowpiercer, Park Chan-wook's Oldboy and Stoker, and the Oscar-nominated Okja. Also produces TV series animation (co-produced Robot Trains with CJ E&M) and participated in Shinji Aramaki's Space Pirate Captain Harlock.

name: Anyzac
significance: South Korean animation production company founded by Byung-Jun Lee, headquartered in Seoul. Produces original IP animation series, 2D/3D character development, and new media content. Best known for the ZombieDumb franchise and Time Traveler Luke. Active in international markets, participating in Asian Television Awards, Asian Animation Summit, and Korea-China animation conferences. Also produces corporate promotional videos and TV commercials.

name: Cinestaan Film Company
significance: Indian boutique film studio founded in September 2013 by Rohit Khattar, committed to championing stories that resonate with global audiences. An integrated studio with development, production, marketing, distribution, sales, and syndication capabilities. Produced the critically acclaimed hand-painted animated feature Bombay Rose (2019, directed by Gitanjali Rao, premiered at Venice Critics' Week), co-produced with France's Les Films D'ici. Also produced Kaalakaandi (2018) starring Saif Ali Khan. Overseas JV with AA Films (Cinestaan AA Distributors) distributed Baahubali 2 in key international territories. C International Sales handles international film sales.

name: MayAna Creatives
significance: Malaysian animation production company. Part of Malaysia's growing animation industry, which includes notable studios like Les' Copaque Production (Upin & Ipin), Animasia Studio (ABC Monsters), Mirayi Animation, and Animonsta Studios (BoBoiBoy). Malaysia has established itself as a significant hub for animation production in Southeast Asia, supported by government initiatives and MSC Malaysia status for qualifying studios. Limited specific publicly available information about MayAna Creatives' individual productions and founding date.

name: 88 Pictures
significance: Indian animation and VFX studio founded in 2016 by Milind D. Shinde, headquartered in Mumbai with offices in Toronto, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad. Premium service animation company working with DreamWorks, Netflix, Warner Bros., Paramount, and Disney. Credits include Kung Fu Panda: The Dragon Knight, Trollhunters: Rise of the Titans, Gremlins: Secrets of the Mogwai, Transformers: EarthSpark, and Fast & Furious Spy Racers. Selected as lead animation studio for Baahubali: The Eternal War animated feature, India's most ambitious animation project.

name: Fantawild Animation
significance: China's most influential animation company and a subsidiary of Fantawild Holdings Inc. (one of China's largest entertainment and technology groups with 40+ subsidiaries). Named a 'National Key Animation Enterprise' and one of 'China's Top Ten Animation Companies.' Creator of the massively successful Boonie Bears franchise — China's #1 animation brand with theatrical films grossing over $300M domestically, broadcast on Disney, Nickelodeon, Netflix, and Sony worldwide. Also operates China's biggest special effects film company and a chain of 16+ Fantawild theme parks. Revenue of CNY 4.345 billion (2018). 108+ employees in animation division alone.

name: Bellnox Films
significance: Japanese anime studio established May 2024 by the Kadokawa Group, with operations formally beginning July 1, 2024. Led by Koji Kajita, founder of Gonzo and former president of David Production (JoJo's Bizarre Adventure). Kadokawa's fifth anime studio alongside ENGI, Studio KADAN, Raging Bull, and Kinema Citrus. Aims to incorporate a 'new production style' not limited by traditional anime production job titles. First announced production: The Darwin Incident (Darwin Jihen) anime adaptation.

name: D-ROCK ART
significance: Chinese visual design and animation studio (Hangzhou Heiyan Network Technology Co., Ltd.) founded in 2013 in Hangzhou. Originally a top-class game/film concept art provider, creating assets for studios including NC Soft, Tencent, Games Workshop (Warhammer 40K), Bethesda (Elder Scrolls Online), and THQ (Darksiders 2). Expanded into 3D animation production, pioneering real-time 3D animation with Unreal Engine (Epic MegaGrants recipient). Created Knights on Debris animated short. Upcoming production Legend of Mecha Scholars gained global distribution via Ad Astra.

name: BeDream
significance: Chinese animation planning and production company founded May 16, 2018, jointly established by Bilibili and HAOLINERS (绘梦, founded by Li Haoling). After Bilibili acquired HAOLINERS, BeDream became its effective successor. Best known for producing Link Click (Shiguang Dailiren), the hugely popular time-travel donghua (8.71 MAL rating, multiple seasons). Also produced To Be Hero X (2025, co-production with Aniplex), To Be Heroine, and other original series. Director Li Haoling is one of China's most acclaimed animation directors (Heaven Official's Blessing, Flavors of Youth).

name: B.CMAY PICTURES
significance: Chinese animation production studio (Beijing Shimei Classic Film Co., Ltd.), formally established April 7, 2017, with origins as Tencent's animation subsidiary G.CMAY Animation & Film (est. 2007, predecessor CMAY Animation Production Team est. 2005). Has 500+ professional animation staff and top-tier 2D animation production capability in China. Best known for Mo Dao Zu Shi (The Founder of Diabolism), The King's Avatar Season 1, A Will Eternal, Bureau of Paranormal Investigation, and Lord of the Mysteries. Strategic partnerships with Tencent, iQIYI, and NetEase.

name: ixtl
significance: Japanese animation production and rights management company (イクストル), founded May 2011 by game developer âge to manage the Muv-Luv franchise IP. Co-produced the anime adaptation Muv-Luv Alternative: Total Eclipse (2012) with Satelight, and also produced Schwarzes Marken (2016). CEO Takashi Nakanishi held majority stake. Acquired by Avex Pictures in July 2017 (90% controlling stake). Officially renamed to 'anchor' (アンカー) on June 7, 2018, ending the ixtl brand. Known primarily for mecha/military sci-fi content within the Muv-Luv universe.

name: Arvo Animation
significance: Japanese animation studio founded in July 2017 by ex-Sanzigen producer Rajeev Karki, based in Suginami, Tokyo with additional studios in Yamagata and Chiba. Notable full productions include Irina: The Vampire Cosmonaut (2021), A Returner's Magic Should Be Special (2023), and Kowloon Generic Romance (2025). Also co-produced We Never Learn (2019) with Silver Link. Provides key animation and support work for studios including CloverWorks, A-1 Pictures, and Studio MAPPA.

name: Foch Film
significance: Shanghai-based Chinese animation studio (Shanghai Foch Film and TV Culture Investment Co., Ltd.) founded March 2006. Operates a closed industrial ecology from producing and developing animation, films, and TV programs to distribution and derivative product development. Produces both 2D, 3D, and puppet animation. Known for donghua series Quanzhi Fashi (Full-Time Magister) and Legend of Immortals (adapted from Eat Tomato's web novel). Works across comic creation, TV column production, cultural brokerage, and consulting.

name: Plum
significance: Japanese animation studio providing production assistance, in-between animation, and finishing work for anime series. Part of Japan's extensive subcontracting studio network.

name: GoHands
significance: Japanese animation studio located in Yodogawa-ku, Osaka, founded in August 2008 by Ringo Kishimoto and former members of Satelight (formerly Satelight's Osaka studio). Known for a distinctive house animation style with heavy use of CG backgrounds, dynamic camera work, and vivid color palettes. Notable productions include the original anime K/K Project (2012, plus sequel season and films), Seitokai Yakuindomo (2010), Mardock Scramble film trilogy (2010-2012), Coppelion (2013), Hand Shakers (2017), The Girl I Like Forgot Her Glasses (2023), and Momentary Lily (2025).

name: KSS
significance: Japanese company (KSS Inc., originally Kamakura Super Station Inc.) founded c.1988, providing anime studio services including production, music, subtitles, and translation. Also developed and published video games from 1993-2001. Created the adult anime brand Pink Pineapple. Known for producing Wedding Peach, Comic Party, Ogre Slayer, Battle Angel (OVA), and numerous other anime productions. Went bankrupt in 2004 and sold assets to Softgarage in 2005.

name: Akatsuki
significance: Japanese subcontracting animation studio (暁) established February 15, 2016, located in Suginami, Tokyo. Also owns Chinese subsidiary Phoenix Animation (火鳥動画制作, formerly under Studio Izena). Primarily works as a subcontractor providing key animation and in-between work for other studios' productions.

name: Mu Animation Studio
significance: Japanese animation subcontracting studio (ミュウ・アニメーションスタジオ), established in the mid-to-late 1980s as a sister studio to Anime R by co-founder Hiromi Muranaka. Based in Osaka. Provides key animation, in-between animation, finish animation, and production assistance for various anime productions. Credits include work on Giant Robo (OVA, animation production eps 2-4), Gin Rei (OVA), Coo: Tōi Umi kara Kita Coo (production cooperation), JoJo's Bizarre Adventure (OVA, photography), and many others. Not to be confused with Studio Mu (スタジオムー), a separate subcontracting studio.

name: DAST
significance: Japanese animation studio (D.A.S.T. Corporation, also known as 'Dust') established in December 1986 by Ichiro Itano (legendary mecha animator known for the 'Itano Circus' missile swarm technique from Macross) with ex-Artland employees. Produced Angel Cop OVA and Moldiver (with AIC). Also contributed uncredited animation to Batman: The Animated Series ('Beware The Grey Ghost' episode). Dissolved in 2011.

name: CygamesPictures
significance: Japanese animation studio established in April 2016 as a subsidiary of major game developer Cygames to produce anime adaptations of their gaming IP and original works. Notable productions include Blade Runner: Black Out 2022, Uma Musume: Pretty Derby - Road to the Top, Brave Bang Bravern! (2024), and The Summer Hikaru Died (2025). Became a subsidiary of parent company CyberAgent on February 27, 2026, and rebranded as CyPic on April 6, 2026.

name: Anime R
significance: Osaka-based Japanese animation support studio (アニメアール, also known as Anime Roman, Double R, Anime Aru, or Anime Earl) established in the late 1970s by veteran animators Moriyasu Taniguchi and Hiromi Muranaka. One of the key Osaka studios in anime history. Has worked extensively with Sunrise on many of their productions. Alumni include Hiroshi Ōsaka (co-founder of Bones), Kazuaki Mōri, Masahiro Kase, Hiroyuki Okiura, and Kazuchika Kise (many of whom went on to found Production I.G). Also supervised Takahiro Kimura. Sister studio to Mu Animation Studio. Created the anime short Pony Metal U-GAIM.

name: Animate Film
significance: Japanese animation studio (アニメイトフィルム) founded August 1984 as a subsidiary of the Animate retailer (part of the Movic/Animate group). Functioned as both a production studio and producer, involved in 88+ anime titles spanning OVAs, TV series, and films. Notable productions include Black Magic M-66 (1987, with AIC), Bannou Bunka Neko-Musume (All Purpose Cultural Cat Girl Nuku Nuku, 1992, with Studio Fantasia), Plastic Little (1994), and Piano (2002). After Marine Entertainment became independent in 2004, Animate Film ceased active operations. Whether the legal entity still exists is unclear.

name: Phoenix Entertainment
significance: Japanese animation studio (フェニックス・エンタテインメント) founded around 1995. Primarily an OVA production house, producing titles including Sensitive Pornograph, Nightmare Campus, Ninja Resurrection, and MeiKing. Also provided digital paint services for Oban Star-Racers (17 episodes) and production assistance for various other anime. Not to be confused with Phoenix Animation Studios of Toronto, Canada. Listed website: phoenix-ent.co.jp.

name: ITV Studios
significance: Major British television production and distribution company, now one of the world's largest independent production groups with 60+ labels in 13 countries. Originated as Granada Productions (1954), evolved through mergers of Granada, Carlton, and ITV plc entities. Inherited the ITC Entertainment library (Thunderbirds, The Muppet Show, The Saint). Produces and distributes thousands of hours of entertainment including drama, factual, and entertainment formats. In animation, ITV's children's strand CITV commissioned and broadcast numerous animated series. The company's vast library includes classic puppet and animated programming from the Gerry Anderson era through ITC.

name: Pukeko Pictures
significance: New Zealand-based entertainment company founded in 2008 as a partnership between Wētā Workshop co-founders Richard Taylor and Tania Rodger, and author/illustrator Martin Baynton. Based in Miramar, Wellington. Produces a mix of live-action, animated, games and picture books for the global market. Notable productions include Jane and the Dragon (CG TV series), The WotWots (2012 Annie Award-nominated preschool series), and Thunderbirds Are Go (co-produced with ITV Studios). Signed a first look deal with FremantleMedia in 2012. Clive Spink appointed CEO in 2015. Acquired by Hengxin Shambala Cultural Company (SZ: 300081).

name: Plasmo Mega Studios
significance: Australian animation studio. Produced the CGI/live-action hybrid children's television series Plasmo (1997), which aired on the ABC (Australian Broadcasting Corporation). The series was notable for its early use of CGI in Australian children's television. A relatively short-lived studio that contributed to Australia's animation output in the late 1990s.

name: Idol
significance: Japanese animation production company. Co-produced the OVA Birth (バース, 1984) with Kaname Production, a landmark OVA featuring animation by Yoshinori Kanada with music by Joe Hisaishi. Birth was one of the earliest OVAs and is notable for Kanada's distinctive organic animation style. Also credited with involvement in the live-action TV series Ikebukuro West Gate Park. A small studio with limited documented output beyond these credits.

name: Zodiac Entertainment
significance: American animation production company active in the 1990s, best known for producing the animated television series Widget the World Watcher (1990–1992), an environmentally themed children's show. Also produced Twinkle, the Dream Being (1993) and Mr. Bogus (1991–1993). The studio was a minor player in the 1990s children's animation market. Widget is notable as one of the early eco-themed animated series aimed at children.

name: aaa (Animation Art-graphique Audiovisuel)
significance: French animation studio founded March 28, 1973 by Marcelle Ponti-Rouxel (producer), Jacques Rouxel (creator of Les Shadoks), and Jean-Paul Couturier (director). Registered as a SARL (société à responsabilité limitée). Produces documentaries, animated TV series, short films, and institutional films. Best known as the production company behind Les Shadoks, one of France's most iconic and surreal animated series. Based in Montreuil, the studio continues producing content across multiple formats including educational and scientific animation (e.g., Pharaons Superstars).

name: Calico Creations
significance: American animation production subsidiary of World Events Productions (WEP), best known as co-producer of Denver, the Last Dinosaur (1988) and Vytor: The Starfire Champion. Also presented Widget (1990–1992, with Zodiac Entertainment). Went dormant in 1993, briefly revived in 1997 to produce The New Adventures of Zorro and VHS release This Land is Your Land: The Animated Kids' Songs of Woody Guthrie. Officially retired by WEP in 1998 after The New Adventures of Zorro was cancelled.

name: Weta Workshop
significance: Award-winning New Zealand creative services company founded in 1987 by Richard Taylor and Tania Rodger in Wellington. Five-time Academy Award winner. World-renowned for practical effects, props, creatures, armour, miniatures, and prosthetics. Best known for work on Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings trilogy (2001–2003), The Hobbit trilogy (2012–2014), King Kong (2005), and Avatar (2009). Also produced effects for Hercules: The Legendary Journeys, Xena: Warrior Princess, Heavenly Creatures (1994), and many others. Digital sibling company Wētā FX (formerly Weta Digital, founded 1993 by Peter Jackson, Richard Taylor, and Jamie Selkirk) is one of the world's leading VFX houses, producing effects for Avatar, The Lord of the Rings, and Planet of the Apes series. Wētā Workshop has expanded into immersive experiences, game development, consumer products, and tours. Richard Taylor received a knighthood for services to film.

name: Avi Arad and Associates
significance: Production company of Israeli-American producer Avi Arad, former CEO of Marvel Entertainment and Marvel Studios. Largely responsible for launching Marvel's film empire, executive-producing Spider-Man (2002), X-Men (2000), Blade (1998), Iron Man (2008), and dozens of Marvel animated TV series including Spider-Man: The Animated Series (1994–1998) and X-Men (1992–1997). Continued producing Spider-Man films for Sony including Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018, Oscar winner), Across the Spider-Verse (2023), and the Venom trilogy.

name: Kaname Productions
significance: Japanese animation studio (カナメプロダクション) founded in spring 1982 by seven former members of Ashi Productions (now Production Reed), including producer Yoshiaki Aihara, writer Junki Takegami, and animators Shigenori Kageyama and Mutsumi Inomata. Known for energetic, Yoshinori Kanada-influenced animation style. Notable alumni include Kunihiko Yuyama (director of Pokémon films) and the late character designer Mutsumi Inomata (Tales series). Contributed to Transformers, Dirty Pair, and other 1980s anime productions. Went bankrupt in 1988.

name: Miramax Films
significance: American film production and distribution company founded in 1979 by brothers Bob and Harvey Weinstein (named after their parents, Miriam and Max). Became the preeminent independent film distributor of the 1990s–2000s, with landmark titles including Pulp Fiction (1994), Shakespeare in Love (1998), Chicago (2002), Good Will Hunting (1997), No Country for Old Men (2007), and The English Patient (1996). Acquired by Walt Disney Company in 1993 for $60M. Disney sold Miramax to Filmyard Holdings in 2010. Sold to beIN Media Group in 2016 for $1 billion. ViacomCBS (now Paramount) acquired a 49% stake in 2020 for $375M. The library includes 700+ titles with 68 Oscar winners. Relevance to animation: produced and/or distributed several animated and mixed-media films.

name: France Animation
significance: French animation studio founded in 1984 in Paris. Developed and produced major French animated series including Titeuf, Petit Vampire, Dr Dog, and Vampires, Pirates and Aliens. In 2003, merged with Antefilms Production (founded 1990 by Christophe and Benoît Di Sabatino) to form MoonScoop Group, which became one of France's largest animation companies with 350+ employees, offices in Paris, Los Angeles, Angoulême, and Wales, and a catalogue of 3,000+ half-hours broadcast in 160+ countries. MoonScoop's flagship series included Code Lyoko, Titeuf, Fantastic Four, and Casper's Scare School. MoonScoop went bankrupt in 2014; US assets became Splash Entertainment, French assets acquired by Dargaud Média/EllipsAnime.

name: Minamimachi Bugyōsho
significance: Japanese animation studio (南町奉行所) founded in 1984 as a 'free studio' by director Osamu Yamasaki, Tsuruyama Osamu, and others. Named after the historical Edo-period magistrate's office. Notable for co-animating Toward the Terra (2007, with Tokyo Kids) for the MBS-TBS Saturday 6pm timeslot. Also contributed production assistance to Angel Heart, Samurai Gun, and various OVA projects. Ceased operations around 2012 during production of Space Battleship Yamato 2199, at which point AIC stepped in to replace them.

name: Anderson Burr Pictures
significance: British production company formed in 1983 by legendary Supermarionation creator Gerry Anderson and businessman Christopher Burr. Produced Terrahawks (1983–1986), Anderson's last puppet-based series, filmed at Bray Studios using 'Supermacromation' — a technique using sophisticated glove puppets inspired by Jim Henson's advances, replacing the marionette strings of his earlier Thunderbirds-era productions. The series ran for 39 episodes on ITV.

name: Jonathan M. Shiff Productions
significance: Leading Australian producer of high-quality children's and family television, founded in 1988 by Jonathan M. Shiff in Queensland, Australia (now based in Melbourne). Renowned for live-action drama series with fantasy elements and high production values. Best known for Ocean Girl (1994-1997), H2O: Just Add Water (2006-2010, streams on Netflix), the spinoff Mako Mermaids (also on Netflix), The Elephant Princess, Alien Surf Girls, Pirate Islands, Thunderstone (1999), Cybergirl, and The Bureau of Magical Things (2018). Catalogue sold to 160+ territories worldwide. Long-running distribution partnership with ZDF Enterprises since 2002. While primarily live-action, many productions incorporate significant VFX/animation elements.

name: Image Entertainment Corporation
significance: Canadian animation production company (Image Entertainment Corporation) based in Montreal, Quebec, founded in 2000 by president Sylvain Viau. Specializes in 2D and 3D animation for international clientele. As of 2014, was developing children's series Spyworld. Should not be confused with Image Entertainment Inc. (American film/video distributor based in Chatsworth, California).

name: London Weekend Television
significance: British ITV network franchise holder for Greater London at weekends (London Weekend Television, LWT), broadcasting from Fridays at 5:15pm to Monday mornings. Launched August 2, 1968. From 1968-1992, shared the London ITV franchise with Thames Television (weekdays), then with Carlton Television (1993-2002). Commissioned and broadcast children's programming including animated series through the ITV children's strand. Known for high-quality idents and presentation. Merged into ITV plc in 2002 when Carlton and Granada merged. LWT's legacy lives on within ITV Studios.

name: Jin Productions
significance: Japanese animation production company (じんプロダクション). Produced the puppet-animation TV series Super Space Machine X Bomber (Xボンバー, 1980, 26 episodes), a live-action/puppet hybrid tokusatsu series co-produced with Go Nagai's Dynamic Planning. Also produced Thunderbirds 2086 (科学救助隊テクノボイジャー, Techno Voyager, 1982), an animated reimagining of Gerry Anderson's Thunderbirds. A small studio with limited documented output beyond these two notable productions.

name: Tokyo Kids
significance: Japanese animation studio (株式会社東京キッズ) founded in April 1990. Produced and co-produced various anime including Dan Doh!! (2004), Abashiri Ikka, and co-animated Toward the Terra (2007, with Minamimachi Bugyōsho). Also worked on numerous OVA projects. The studio went bankrupt in 2008.

name: Toshiba EMI
significance: Japanese record label and media company, originally a joint venture between Toshiba and EMI Group. In anime, served as a music producer, distributor, and production committee participant for various animated productions during the 1980s-2000s. Released anime soundtracks and contributed to the financing of anime series and OVAs. Renamed EMI Music Japan in 2007 after Toshiba sold its stake; later absorbed into Universal Music Japan in 2013.

name: Hallmark Cards
significance: ⚠️ LOW ANIMATION RELEVANCE — Hallmark Cards is a greeting card and media company. While Hallmark has commissioned some animated television specials (e.g., Hallmark Hall of Fame), it is not an animation studio or production entity. Animation involvement is tangential through licensing and sponsorship. Consider removal from archive.

name: Golden Films
significance: American animation production studio founded in 1990 by Diane Eskenazi as American Film Investment Corporation, renamed Golden Films in 1994. Best known for producing the Enchanted Tales series of direct-to-video animated films — low-budget adaptations of classic fairy tales (Beauty and the Beast, The Little Mermaid, Aladdin, etc.) originally distributed by Sony and often considered 'mockbusters' of Disney animated features. Also produced specials for Hallmark. In the early 2020s, pivoted to live-action documentaries (One World series) tackling Gen Z sociopolitical issues.

name: Scottish Television
significance: Scottish broadcasting company (now STV Studios) founded August 31, 1957 by Canadian newspaper magnate Roy Thomson. Originally Scottish Television Enterprises, it served as the main content provider for the STV ITV franchise. Reorganized as SMG Productions (2000), then STV Productions (2008), then STV Studios (2019). Produced many notable programs including Taggart (1983–2010) and Take the High Road. Relevant to animation: occasionally produced or commissioned animated content and specials for broadcast. Still active as part of STV Group plc.

name: Coco Enterprise
significance: South Korean animation subcontracting studio (also known as Koko Enterprises/Koko Entertainment), founded March 2, 1990 by Myong Ok Jeon in Seocho District, Seoul. Owned by TMS Entertainment/Sega. Frequently paired with Dong Yang Animation on Warner Bros. projects. Animated episodes of Batman: The Animated Series, Gargoyles (including key multi-parters 'City of Stone,' 'Avalon,' 'The Gathering'), Animaniacs, Spider-Man TAS, and ¡Mucha Lucha!. Rebranded as CNK International in February 2011 and exited animation for non-ferrous metal mining.

name: Tooniverse
significance: South Korean animation and cartoon television channel (투니버스, portmanteau of 'Cartoon Universe'). Launched December 21, 1995, as one of the first dedicated animation channels in South Korea. Currently one of the leading animation channels in the country, owned by CJ ENM. Broadcasts an extensive collection of anime, Korean animation, and cartoons targeting all age groups from children to adults. Has aired hundreds of anime series including dubbed versions of major Japanese franchises. Pioneered anime broadcasting in South Korea with early acquisitions of series like Wedding Peach and Slayers.

name: Métropole Production
significance: French film production and distribution company founded circa 1970. Involved in co-producing and distributing animated and live-action content in the French and European markets. Part of France's extensive animation production ecosystem, which is the third largest in the world after the United States and Japan. France has a long history of animation dating back to Émile Reynaud (1892) and Émile Cohl (1908), and French studios continue to be major players in global animation.

name: MK Company
significance: Japanese animation production company (エムケイ, MK or MK Company). Co-produced Belle and Sebastian (名犬ジョリィ, 1981–1982) with Visual 80 and Toho for NHK, and the Lensman animated feature film (1984) and TV series (1984–1985). Also involved in The Mysterious Cities of Gold (1982), Pole Position (1984), The Yearling, and Animation Kikō Marco Polo no Bōken. Later credited for key animation work on Galilei Donna (2013, ep 5) and 2nd key animation on If Her Flag Breaks (2014, ep 2). Exact closure date unknown — the studio appears to have become inactive as a primary contractor after the 1980s, with only sporadic subcontracting credits through 2014. A small but historically significant studio from the early 1980s anime era.

name: LBS Communications
significance: American television production and syndication company (Lexington Broadcast Services Company, later LBS Communications Inc.) founded November 1976 by advertising pioneer Henry Siegel as a unit of Grey Advertising. Became the nation's largest barter syndicator — a model where broadcasters received programming free in exchange for ad revenue sharing. Distributed major animated series including Inspector Gadget and Heathcliff (via DIC Entertainment), as well as live-action shows like Baywatch and Family Feud. Also co-created Colex Enterprises with Columbia Pictures Television. Became an in-name-only unit of All American Television in the 1990s. Sold to Pearson plc in 1997, renamed Pearson Television in 1998, closed 2001. Library now mostly owned by Fremantle.

name: Bohbot Entertainment
significance: American advertising, marketing, and children's entertainment syndication company founded in 1985 by Allen J. Bohbot. Ran the syndicated 'Amazin' Adventures' TV block (1992), later renamed Bohbot Kids Network/BKN (1997). Distributed Adventures of Sonic the Hedgehog, Double Dragon, Street Sharks, Mummies Alive!, Extreme Ghostbusters, and Sonic Underground. Aired on FOX, UPN, and WB affiliates. International division spun off as BKN International AG (Germany) in 1999. Bohbot founded successor company 41 Entertainment, which now manages the brand's legacy and distributes Pac-Man and the Ghostly Adventures.

name: Those Characters from Cleveland / Cloudco Entertainment
significance: American animation studio and production company, a subsidiary of American Greetings. Founded in 1980 by Tom Wilson on behalf of American Greetings to handle its licensing business. Now operates as Cloudco Entertainment (renamed from AG Properties / American Greetings Entertainment). Created some of the most iconic children's properties of the 1980s including Strawberry Shortcake ($500M in retail sales in 1981), Care Bears ($2B in first two years), Holly Hobbie (character debuted 1967), The Get Along Gang, Popples, and Madballs. Still active today, developing multi-platform entertainment franchises. Current properties include Care Bears, Holly Hobbie, Madballs, Buddy Thunderstruck, and Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese.

name: Graz Entertainment
significance: American animation licensing, distribution, and production company founded in January 1992 by Jim and Stephanie Graziano (both Hanna-Barbera, Warner Bros., and Marvel Productions veterans) in Glendale, California. Best known for producing and distributing the hit 1990s animated series X-Men (1992, #1 Saturday morning show) and The Tick (1994, #3). Also handled Conan the Adventurer, Darkstalkers, Street Fighter, Skeleton Warriors, G.I. Joe Extreme, and My Little Pony Tales. The Grazianos were later recruited by Jeffrey Katzenberg to head DreamWorks' television animation division.

name: Amblin Entertainment
significance: American film production company founded in 1980 by Steven Spielberg, Kathleen Kennedy, and Frank Marshall, headquartered at Universal Studios in Burbank. Pioneered family-oriented animated features through subsidiary Amblimation (1989–1997, based in London), producing An American Tail: Fievel Goes West, We're Back! A Dinosaur's Story, and Balto. Also executive-produced landmark animated films including An American Tail, The Land Before Time, and Who Framed Roger Rabbit (with Disney/Touchstone). Continues producing animated content through Amblin Animation.

name: King Features
significance: American print syndication company owned by Hearst Communications, founded in 1915. One of the world's largest and oldest newspaper feature syndicates. In animation, King Features is the rights holder and licensor of iconic characters including Popeye the Sailor Man (created 1929 by E.C. Segar), Flash Gordon, The Phantom, Beetle Bailey, and Blondie. Produced 220 Popeye TV cartoon episodes in 1960-1962 for syndication. Has licensed characters for animated series, films, and merchandise across decades. Continues to develop new animated content — released original Popeye animated shorts in 2018 for the character's 90th anniversary. Also active in immersive experiences and licensing worldwide.

name: Gaga
significance: Japanese film distribution and production company (ギャガ株式会社, GAGA Corporation) founded January 28, 1986 by Fujimura Tetsuya as Gaga Communications. Major independent Japanese film distributor handling international films in Japan and Japanese films abroad. Entered anime production in 2016. Anime involvement includes production roles on Tenchi Muyo in Love, Magic Tree House, Okko's Inn, Voltage Fighter Gowcaizer, and others. Distributed international hits including The King's Speech, and more recently Umamusume: Pretty Derby across 600+ US/Canadian theaters. Now a subsidiary of GENDA Inc. (since 2023). Distributed DreamWorks Animation titles in Japan.

name: Tyco
significance: American toy company founded in 1926 as Mantua Metal Products in Moorestown, New Jersey. In animation, Tyco funded and co-produced animated television series based on its toy lines during the 1980s-1990s toy-cartoon synergy era, including Dino-Riders (1988), The Incredible Crash Dummies (1993), and Super Blocks (animated segments). Acquired by Mattel in 1997 for $755 million. The Tyco brand continues as a Mattel sub-brand for radio-controlled vehicles.

name: Production +h.
significance: Japanese animation studio founded in 2008, based in Fuchu, Tokyo. Originally established for specialized production work, the studio gained major recognition under director Mitsuo Iso (Dennō Coil). Notable productions include The First Slam Dunk (2022, production cooperation — the film grossed ¥15.7 billion worldwide), Dead Dead Demon's Dededede Destruction (2024, theatrical films and TV series adaptation of Inio Asano's manga), The Orbital Children (Extra-Terrestrial Boys & Girls, 2022), and Hirayasumi (2025). Also produced Dark Machine the Animation (2025). Increasingly recognized as a quality-focused studio.

name: Shogakukan
significance: Major Japanese publishing conglomerate founded August 8, 1922. One of the largest publishers in Japan and the world, part of the Hitotsubashi Group alongside Shueisha and Hakusensha. Publishes manga, magazines, dictionaries, literature, and non-fiction. Co-owns Viz Media (with Shueisha) for North American manga distribution. Production arm Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions (ShoPro, founded 1967) handles anime production and licensing for properties including Doraemon, Detective Conan, Pokémon, and hundreds of other anime. Headquartered in Chiyoda, Tokyo.

name: New World Animation
significance: American animation production company, the animation division of New World Pictures (founded by Roger Corman). Active in the late 1980s, producing animated television content. New World Pictures was a major independent film studio that briefly expanded into television and animation before being sold to various entities in the late 1980s-early 1990s.

name: France 2
significance: Major French public television channel, part of France Télévisions group. Launched September 7, 1992 as successor to Antenne 2 (founded 1975). France's second-largest TV channel by viewership. As a broadcaster, co-produced and commissioned numerous animated series including Code Lyoko (via France 3/France Télévisions), Titeuf, Petit Vampire, and many other French animated productions. France Télévisions has been one of the most important funders and commissioners of French and European animation.

name: Jetix Europe
significance: European television broadcasting company (Jetix Europe N.V., formerly Fox Kids Europe N.V.) headquartered in Hilversum, Netherlands and London. Owned children's TV channels and programming blocks across Europe and Asia under the Jetix and Fox Kids brands. Launched as Fox Kids UK on October 19, 1996, through a partnership between Fox Broadcasting and Saban Entertainment. Expanded across Netherlands, France, Poland, Scandinavia, Spain and more. Rebranded from Fox Kids to Jetix in 2004-2005. Majority-owned by Disney through ABC Family Worldwide. Disney fully acquired the company in 2008 and replaced Jetix channels with Disney XD or Disney Channel by 2009. Formally dissolved April 2014.

name: Fox Telecolombia
significance: ⚠️ LOW ANIMATION RELEVANCE — Colombian television production company primarily focused on telenovelas and live-action content. Not primarily an animation studio. Any animation involvement is incidental to its main business. Consider removal from archive.

name: Luxanimation
significance: Luxembourgish animation studio based in Doncols, Luxembourg, founded in 2000 by former Neuroplanet employees Lilian Eche and Ariane Payen. Partnered with other companies to produce animated programs and movies. Produced over 170 hours of animated content for international markets. Known for innovative techniques including motion capture. Co-produced Robotboy (with Alphanim/France 2), Code Lyoko (later seasons), and Renaissance (2006, motion-capture noir animated film with Pathé). Acquired by MoonScoop Group in 2006. Opened Luxatelier department in June 2010 for audiovisual projects. Shut down when MoonScoop went bankrupt in 2014; assets split between Splash Entertainment and Dargaud/EllipsAnime.

name: Nerd Corps Entertainment
significance: Canadian CGI animation studio founded in 2002 by Asaph Fipke in Vancouver, British Columbia. Known for producing Storm Hawks (2007–2009), Slugterra (2012–2016), Kate and Mim-Mim, and Hot Wheels: Battle Force 5. Specialized in CG-animated children's television series. Acquired by DHX Media (now WildBrain) in 2014 for C$11.3 million, becoming part of WildBrain's Vancouver animation operations. Post-acquisition, the Nerd Corps brand was gradually absorbed into WildBrain Studios.

name: Universal Cartoon Studios
significance: Television animation division of Universal Studios, active from 1990 to 2006. Created and produced animated series based on Universal's film properties including Back to the Future: The Animated Series (1991–1993), Fievel's American Tails (1992), Exosquad (1993–1994), Monster Force, Earthworm Jim (1995–1996), Woody Woodpecker Show (1999), and Curious George (2006). Renamed Universal Animation Studios in 2006, then merged into Universal Content Productions. Exosquad remains a cult classic praised for mature storytelling in a children's animation format.

name: BRB Internacional
