significance: Spanish animation production, distribution, and licensing company founded July 30, 1972 in Alcobendas, Madrid by Tito Basto, José Rodríguez, and Claudio Biern Boyd (name from founders' initials). Over 40 years of experience producing beloved children's series including Around the World with Willy Fog, Dogtanian and the Three Muskehounds, and The World of David the Gnome. Long-standing partnership with Japan's Nippon Animation. Also distributed Hanna-Barbera and Warner Bros. properties in Spain. Library acquired by DeAPlaneta Entertainment after Biern Boyd's passing.

name: Seyoung Animation
significance: South Korean animation studio (세영동화, Sei Young Animation Co., Ltd.) founded in 1981 by animator Kim Dae-jung. One of the prominent Korean OEM animation studios of the 1980s–90s, frequently subcontracted by DIC Entertainment and Japanese studios. Animated The Super Mario Bros. Super Show!, The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3, The Legend of Zelda (TV), and Japanese productions including Final Yamato, Video Senshi Laserion, and Nadia: The Secret of Blue Water. In 1993, merged with The Island Corporation to form the short-lived Animagic Studio Inc. Ultimately merged with Dong Woo Animation in October 1998 due to the 1997 Asian financial crisis. Founder Kim Dae-jung died September 14, 2017.

name: Cambria Productions
significance: American animation studio founded in 1958 in West Hollywood by cartoonist Clark Haas and cameraman Edwin Gillette. Pioneered the Syncro-Vox animation technique — superimposing live human lips onto still drawings to simulate speech, dramatically reducing production costs. Created Clutch Cargo (1959, first widely-known Syncro-Vox series, 130 episodes on 65 stations), Space Angel (1962), and Captain Fathom (1965). Also produced The New Three Stooges animated series with live-action segments. Despite extreme limited animation, the series were surprise commercial hits due to imaginative storytelling.

name: KBS
significance: Korean Broadcasting System (KBS), South Korea's national public broadcaster, founded in 1961. Operates seven radio networks, ten television channels (including flagship KBS1 and entertainment-oriented KBS2), and online services including KBS World international broadcasting in twelve languages. Launched children's channel KBS Kids in May 2012, broadcasting Korean-produced animated series (Miniforce, Catch! Teenieping, Tea-Tea Cherry) as well as Korean-dubbed international programs (Pokémon, One Piece). KBS has been a key broadcaster and co-producer of Korean animation, including the classic Fly, Superboard (1990-2002, produced by Hanho Heung-Up). Part of the development of South Korea's significant animation industry.

name: Kugatsusha
significance: Personal animation studio of Yoshikazu Yasuhiko, the renowned animator, manga artist, and director best known for his work on the original Mobile Suit Gundam (1979, character designer/animation director) and Crusher Joe (1983). Kugatsusha (九月社, 'September Company') produced The Venus Wars (1989), an anime film based on Yasuhiko's manga, featuring a score by Joe Hisaishi and produced by Bandai Visual, Gakken, and Shochiku. The studio was a small, personal outfit primarily dedicated to Yasuhiko's own projects.

name: Bardel Entertainment
significance: Canadian animation studio founded in 1987 by Barry Ward and Delna Bhesania in Vancouver, British Columbia (name derived from 'Bar' + 'Del'). Started as a cel painting service house, grew into internationally recognized full-service studio. Best known for animating Rick and Morty, Teen Titans Go!, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, and The Dragon Prince. Purchased by Italy's Rainbow S.p.A. in 2015. Has 375+ employees. Also produced VeggieTales content and Dragon Booster.

name: Alphanim
significance: French animation production and distribution company founded in February 1997 by Christian Davin, former president of France Animation. Built a catalogue of over 800 half-hours broadcast in 130+ countries, including Galactik Football and Animal Crackers. In 2008, acquired by Gaumont for €25 million, marking Gaumont's return to TV animation. Renamed Gaumont-Alphanim in 2009, then rebranded as Gaumont Animation in 2013.

name: Anderson Entertainment
significance: British production company managing the legacy and IP of legendary creator Gerry Anderson (Thunderbirds, Captain Scarlet, Stingray, UFO, Space: 1999). Creates, develops, produces, and nurtures Anderson's extensive IP catalogue for contemporary audiences. Currently developing animated feature Merry Christmas, Earthlings! (debuted at Berlinale 2026) and partnered with Hanna-Barbera Studios Europe/Warner Bros. Animation on Hit Squad, an adult animated series based on an unseen 1980s Gerry Anderson concept.

name: Antefilms
significance: French animation production company founded in 1990 by brothers Christophe and Benoît Di Sabatino. Became a major figure in French animation, pioneering the integration of 3D into 2D production. In 1994, made its first creation Les Pirates de Noël. Opened a state-of-the-art 3D animation and motion-capture studio in Angoulême in 1998. Best known for co-creating Code Lyoko (2003) with France 3 and Canal J — a landmark French animated series blending 2D and CGI that ran for 97 episodes. Also produced Funky Cops (2002) and Jojo la Frite. Acquired France Animation in September 2003 (gaining the Titeuf franchise). In 2004, merged distribution operations to form the MoonScoop Group, which would later file for bankruptcy in 2014.

name: Columbia TriStar Television
significance: American television production and distribution company formed February 21, 1994 from the merger of Columbia Pictures Television and TriStar Television under Sony Pictures Entertainment. Produced and distributed a vast library of television content. The animation division (Columbia Television Animation) handled animated content including adaptations and co-productions. Subsumed Merv Griffin Enterprises (Jeopardy!, Wheel of Fortune) in 1994. Renamed Sony Pictures Television on September 16, 2002, which continues today as one of the largest TV production companies globally.

name: Groupe IDDH
significance: French production company (International Droits et Divers Holding) founded in 1979 by Bruno-René Huchez. Originally produced French-dubbed versions of Japanese anime. From 1985, became a producer of French animation series, co-producing with various American majors. Best known for co-producing Denver, the Last Dinosaur (1988, with World Events Productions) — an American-French animated series about conservation and ecology that aired in syndication. Also co-produced Clémentine (1985). Animation was outsourced to studios like Pacific Animation Corporation (Japan).

name: World Events Productions
significance: American animation and distribution company based in St. Louis, Missouri. Founded in 1980 by Ted Koplar, son of KPLR-TV founder Harold Koplar. Best known for adapting and releasing the Japanese anime Voltron: Defender of the Universe (1984–1985), created by combining footage from Toei's Beast King GoLion and Armored Fleet Dairugger XV for Western audiences. Also released Saber Rider and the Star Sheriffs and produced the original animated series Denver, the Last Dinosaur. The Voltron franchise was later revived as Voltron: Legendary Defender (2016–2018) by DreamWorks Animation and Netflix, animated by Studio Mir.

name: BKN International
significance: German-registered children's TV production and distribution company, originally founded as Bohbot Entertainment Worldwide in 1994 as the international division of Bohbot Communications. Renamed BKN International in 1997. Split from parent BKN Inc. as a standalone public company in 1999, registered in Cologne. Acquired French animation house Studio Arles Animation in 2000. Produced and distributed series including Kong: King of Atlantis, Zorro: Generation Z, and Roswell Conspiracies. Had offices in UK, US, Singapore, and Spain. Filed for insolvency circa 2009; library of 10,000+ half-hours of programming rights was liquidated.

name: Sunbow Productions
significance: American television production company founded in 1980 by Tom Griffin in New York City as a subsidiary of Griffin-Bacal Advertising. Best known for producing the original animated series for Hasbro's toy lines: Transformers (1984–1987), G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero (1983–1986), Jem and the Holograms (1985–1988), and My Little Pony (1986–1987). Also produced Inhumanoids, Visionaries, and C.O.P.S. The studio's Hasbro collaborations, animated by studios including Toei, AKOM, and Marvel Productions, became defining 1980s pop culture properties. Sunbow was acquired by Sony Wonder in 1998 and later became part of Entertainment One (eOne). The name Sunbow was derived from 'son of a gun' in Yiddish.

name: DePatie-Freleng Enterprises
significance: American animation studio founded in 1963 by David H. DePatie and legendary Looney Tunes director Friz Freleng in Burbank, California, after Warner Bros. closed its animation department. Created the iconic Pink Panther animated shorts (1964–1980, Oscar-winning debut The Pink Phink), The Inspector, and The Ant and the Aardvark. Also produced Dr. Seuss TV specials, animated the lightsaber effects in the original Star Wars (1977), and created Spider-Woman (1979). Became a major competitor to Hanna-Barbera and Filmation. Sold to Marvel in 1981, becoming Marvel Productions.

name: NUT
significance: Japanese animation studio (株式会社ナット) founded in 2017 by ex-Madhouse producer Takuya Tsunoki and Chiptune CEO Masayuki Narai. Based in Suginami, Tokyo. Known for dynamic action sequences and detailed world-building. Notable productions include Saga of Tanya the Evil (Youjo Senki, 2017), Deca-Dence (2020, original), Blue Giant (2023, theatrical film), FLCL Alternative, and NegaPosi Angler. Acquired by Twin Engine in 2026, becoming part of the Twin Engine Group to strengthen production capabilities and deepen its role in original IP development.

name: Jetlag Productions
significance: Japanese-American animation studio that specialized in developing animated films based on popular fairy tales and public-domain literature during the 1990s. Similar to Golden Films, produced low-budget direct-to-video animated adaptations (Cinderella, Snow White, Sleeping Beauty, Heidi, etc.) animated in Japan by KKC&D Asia and Animaru Ya, among South Korean studios. Films were distributed through GoodTimes Home Video/GoodTimes Entertainment. Often considered 'mockbusters' alongside Golden Films' output. Dubbed into many languages for worldwide distribution. After GoodTimes' bankruptcy in 2005, copyrights transferred to Gaiam.

name: MoonScoop
significance: French animation production and distribution company established in 2003 from the merger of Antefilms Production (est. 1990) and France Animation (est. 1984), by brothers Christophe and Benoît Di Sabatino. Headquartered in Paris with offices in the UK and USA. Best known for Code Lyoko (2003–2007), a landmark French animated series blending 2D and CGI. Also produced Titeuf, Chloe's Closet, and Funky Cops. Acquired Mike Young Productions (2005) and majority of LuxAnimation (2006). Expanded into digital media with MoonScoop Digital Media. Entered administration in July 2013; assets divested — Mike and Liz Young repurchased the US division (renamed Splash Entertainment), while Dargaud Média acquired the French operations (absorbed into EllipsAnime).

name: Harmony Gold
significance: American entertainment company founded in 1983 by Frank Agrama in Los Angeles. Best known as the creator and rights holder of Robotech (1985), the landmark 85-episode anime series adapted by Carl Macek from three unrelated Japanese anime (Super Dimension Fortress Macross, Super Dimension Cavalry Southern Cross, Genesis Climber MOSPEADA). Robotech was pivotal in introducing anime to American audiences and spawned a massive franchise including films, games, comics, and merchandise. Also produced Captain Harlock adaptations, live-action mini-series Shaka Zulu, and the game show Name That Tune. In 2021, signed an expansive agreement with Big West and Studio Nue for worldwide Macross/Robotech distribution.

name: The Curiosity Company
significance: American production company founded April 21, 1997 by Matt Groening, creator of The Simpsons. Also known as The ULULU Company (2018–2023) before reverting to The Curiosity Company name. Produced for Gracie Films. Productions include Futurama (1999–2026, 180 episodes across multiple revivals on Fox, Comedy Central, and Hulu), Disenchantment (2018–2023, Netflix, 50 episodes), and the TV film Olive, the Other Reindeer (1999). The company logo features ocean wave footage from 'A Study in Wet,' a short film made by Groening's father, Homer.

name: Century 21 Productions
significance: British production company, the renamed successor of AP Films, founded by Gerry Anderson in the mid-1960s. The Century 21 Organisation encompassed production, merchandising, publishing (TV Century 21 comic), and music divisions. Produced the final Supermarionation series Captain Scarlet and the Mysterons (1967), Joe 90 (1968), and The Secret Service (1969), then pivoted to live-action with UFO (1970) and Space: 1999 (1975). Also produced the theatrical films Thunderbirds Are Go (1966) and Thunderbird 6 (1968). The organisation represented the peak commercial expansion of Anderson's puppet empire.

name: Knack Productions
significance: Japanese anime and film production company (now ICHI Corporation since August 2008), founded September 25, 1967 by Seiichi Hayashi and Seiichi Nishino, former employees of Mushi Productions and Toei. Despite notable staff including Go Nagai and Ken Ishikawa, developed a reputation for low production quality even by contemporary standards. Produced over two dozen shows from 1970-1991 including Astroganger (1972, early super robot anime), Chargeman Ken! (1974, gained internet cult status for its 'so bad it's good' quality), and adaptations based on Go Nagai properties. Earliest show was Ijiwaru Baasan (1970) based on Machiko Hasegawa's manga.

name: Pioneer LDC
significance: Japanese media company founded as a subsidiary of Pioneer Corporation, originally focused on LaserDisc distribution of anime — hence 'LDC' (Laser Disc Corporation). A major anime distributor and production committee participant during the 1990s OVA boom. Funded and released landmark titles including Tenchi Muyo!, Serial Experiments Lain, Armitage III, Key the Metal Idol, and Dual! Parallel Trouble Adventure. Also distributed anime in North America through Geneon Entertainment USA (formerly Pioneer Entertainment). Renamed Geneon Entertainment in 2003 after Pioneer sold its stake. Geneon USA ceased operations in 2007; Japanese operations merged into NBC Universal Entertainment Japan in 2009.

name: 20th Century Fox Television
significance: Founded May 19, 1999 as Fox Television Animation, the TV animation arm of 20th Century Fox. Produced and oversaw iconic adult animated series including The Simpsons, Family Guy, King of the Hill, Futurama, American Dad!, Bob's Burgers, and The Cleveland Show. Following the 2019 Disney-Fox merger, rebranded as 20th Television Animation in 2020 and became a unit of Disney Television Studios. One of the most prolific adult animation producers in television history.

name: Too Kyo Games
significance: Japanese creative studio founded November 2017 by Kazutaka Kodaka (Danganronpa creator) and Kotaro Uchikoshi (Zero Escape creator), along with other notable game and anime creators including character designer Rui Komatsuzaki and composer Masafumi Takada. Primarily a video game development studio, but produced the anime series Akudama Drive (2020, animated by Studio Pierrot) and was involved in the anime project World's End Club. The studio represents the convergence of game narrative design and anime storytelling. Disbanded in late 2023 with Kodaka founding Homura Machine.

name: Procidis
significance: French animation studio founded in 1962 by Albert Barillé, a pioneer in edutainment animation. Best known as creator of the 'Once Upon a Time…' (Il était une fois…) educational animated saga — seven series covering Man, Space, Life, The Americas, The Discoverers, The Explorers, and Planet Earth — translated into 80 languages and broadcast in 100+ countries. Also produced The Adventures of Colargol (preschool series). Programs are evergreens and have been a reference in educational broadcasting for 40+ years. Led by Hélène Barillé since 2009. In 2024, Banijay Kids & Family acquired a majority stake, integrating Procidis into the Banijay Entertainment group alongside Totally Spies! and Mr Bean: The Animated Series producers.

name: AP Films
significance: British production company (Anderson Provis Films) co-founded in 1957 by Gerry Anderson and Arthur Provis in Maidenhead, Berkshire. Birthplace of 'Supermarionation' — the revolutionary marionette puppet technique using electronic moving parts. Produced The Adventures of Twizzle (1957), Torchy the Battery Boy (1958), Four Feather Falls (1960), Supercar (1961), Fireball XL5 (1962), Stingray (1964), Thunderbirds (1965), Captain Scarlet and the Mysterons (1967), and Joe 90 (1968). Renamed Century 21 Productions in 1966. One of the most influential companies in British television history.

name: Adelaide Productions
significance: Television animation division of Sony Pictures Television, founded April 12, 1993 by Columbia Pictures Television in Culver City, California. Also known as Columbia TriStar Television Animation and Columbia TriStar Children's Television. Produced notable animated series including Extreme Ghostbusters, Men in Black: The Series, Jackie Chan Adventures, The Boondocks, and Roughnecks: Starship Troopers Chronicles. Became dormant after 2014 when The Boondocks ended; production capabilities later absorbed by Sony Pictures Animation (via Chuck Productions, Inc.) in 2022. Remains an active legal subsidiary of Sony Pictures Television holding copyrights to its prior productions.

name: Saban Entertainment
significance: American-Israeli entertainment company founded in 1983 by Haim Saban and Shuki Levy. Best known for adapting Japanese tokusatsu series into Mighty Morphin Power Rangers (1993), creating a global franchise. In animation, distributed and co-produced Digimon Adventure, Dragon Ball Z, Samurai Pizza Cats, and numerous European animated series for the US market (Inspector Gadget reruns, Saban's Adventures of Oliver Twist). Created DiC Entertainment competitor in children's TV. Saban Entertainment was acquired by The Walt Disney Company in 2001 as part of Fox Family Worldwide for $5.2 billion. Saban later reacquired Power Rangers from Disney in 2010 before selling to Hasbro in 2018.

name: ITC Entertainment
significance: Major British television production and distribution company (Incorporated Television Company), founded in 1954 by Lew Grade. Became one of the UK's most important entertainment companies. Distributed all of Gerry Anderson's Supermarionation and live-action series (Thunderbirds, Captain Scarlet, UFO, Space: 1999) through Century 21 Productions. Also produced/distributed The Muppet Show, The Prisoner, The Saint, and financed films including The Dark Crystal (1982), The Muppet Movie (1979), The Last Unicorn (1982), and The Boys from Brazil (1978). Bought by Bell Group in 1988, then Bond Corporation. Library eventually acquired by PolyGram, then Universal.

name: Ruby-Spears Productions
significance: American animation studio founded in 1977 by Joe Ruby and Ken Spears, the creators of Scooby-Doo at Hanna-Barbera. Produced Thundarr the Barbarian (1980–1981), Rubik, the Amazing Cube, Alvin and the Chipmunks (1983–1990), Mr. T (1983–1986), and the Mega Man animated series (1994–1996). Created the original animated Rambo: The Force of Freedom and Police Academy series. Became a subsidiary of Taft Entertainment in 1981, later part of Turner Broadcasting/Warner Bros. through corporate mergers. Ruby and Spears were among the most prolific creators in Saturday morning animation history, having also created Dynomutt and Jabberjaw at Hanna-Barbera.

name: Marvel Productions
significance: American animation production company (Marvel Productions Ltd.) founded in 1981 when Marvel Comics' parent company Cadence Industries purchased DePatie-Freleng Enterprises. Based in Hollywood, Los Angeles. Produced landmark animated TV series and films including Spider-Man and His Amazing Friends, The Incredible Hulk, The Transformers, G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero, Muppet Babies (Emmy winner), My Little Pony: The Movie (1986), The Transformers: The Movie (1986), and G.I. Joe: The Movie (1987). Partnered with Sunbow Entertainment (1983-1987) and Hasbro for toy-based programming. Co-founder David H. DePatie continued as studio head until 1985. Renamed New World Animation in 1993 after New World Entertainment acquisition. Eventually absorbed into Fox/News Corporation. Non-Hasbro catalog now owned by Walt Disney Company.

name: Créativité et Développement (C&D)
significance: French animation production company founded in 1987 by Jean Chalopin after he left DIC Entertainment (which he had originally founded in 1971). Chalopin retained the French arm of DIC (DIC Audiovisuel) and renamed it Créativité et Développement (C&D). Continued producing animated television series for the European and international markets. Operated as an independent French animation studio during the golden age of European animation co-productions in the 1990s and early 2000s.

name: DIC Entertainment
significance: French-American animation studio founded in 1971 by Jean Chalopin in Paris (pronounced 'deek'). US arm founded 1982 in Burbank by Andy Heyward. Became one of TV's most prolific animation studios, producing Inspector Gadget (1983), Heathcliff, Rainbow Brite, The Real Ghostbusters, Sailor Moon (US adaptation), Sonic the Hedgehog, and many others. Owned by Capital Cities/ABC (1993–1996), then Disney (1996–2000). After Heyward reacquired it in 2000, acquired by Cookie Jar Group in 2008. Library now owned by WildBrain. When Chalopin left in 1987, he retained the French arm and formed Créativité et Développement (C&D).

name: Marathon Media
significance: French animation and television production company (Marathon Media, originally Marathon Productions) founded February 1990 by Olivier Brémond and Pascal Breton in Neuilly-sur-Seine. Vincent Chalvon-Demersay and David Michel joined in 1999 to develop the animation division. Best known for creating and producing the globally successful Totally Spies! (2001, 7 seasons), Martin Mystery, and other anime-influenced French animated series. Shows dubbed into numerous languages and broadcast worldwide. Acquired by Zodiak Media Group in 2007. Folded into Zodiak Kids Studios in April 2015 alongside The Foundation and Tele Images Productions. Now operates as the French unit of Zodiak Kids & Family under the Banijay Group, led by Benoît Di Sabatino.

name: Duckbill Entertainment
significance: Singapore-based animation production and co-production company, incorporated March 30, 2011 by Japanese producer Hideki Kunugiyama. Operates as a bridge between Japanese and Southeast Asian animation production. Co-produced One Stormy Night: Secret Friends (Arashi no Yoru Ni: Himitsu no Tomodachi, 2012) with Sparky Animation (Singapore), Baku Enterprise, and Bandai Visual — a CG animated TV series for TV Tokyo. Also co-produced SUMMER (Guebo, 2024) with Japan's Xanthus Animation Studio, selected for the 2022 Annecy International Animation Market.

name: Folivari
significance: French animation studio founded by Didier Brunner (former Les Armateurs). Produced The Summit of the Gods (2021), Ernest & Celestine: A Trip to Gibberitia (2022), and co-produced Wolfwalkers (2020).

name: Maybe Movies
significance: French animation production company founded by César Award-winning producer Henri Magalon (Oscar-nominated for Ernest & Celestine). Produced Long Way North (Tout en haut du monde, 2015), directed by Rémi Chayé, which won the Audience Award at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival. Produced Calamity, a Childhood of Martha Jane Cannary (2020), also directed by Chayé, a beautifully animated 2D feature about young Calamity Jane on the Oregon Trail. Known for distinctive hand-drawn 2D animation with bold, painterly visual styles and strong female protagonists. Co-productions with Danish studio Nørlum and French broadcasters.

name: BreakThru Films
significance: Polish production company founded by Hugh Welchman. Produced Oscar-winning Peter and the Wolf (2006) and the world's first fully oil-painted feature Loving Vincent (2017). Pioneered oil-painting animation technique.

name: Digital Dimension
significance: Montreal-based CGI animation and VFX studio founded 1996. Six-time Emmy Award winner for work on television animation. Produced animation for major game cinematics, commercials, and TV series. Closed May 2024, citing reduced demand and changes to Quebec tax credit programs that made operations financially unviable.

name: One Animation
significance: Singaporean CGI animation studio founded 2008. Created 'Oddbods' (2014), a non-dialogue slapstick comedy that received 3 Emmy nominations. Also produced 'Insectibles' and 'Rob the Robot.' Acquired by Moonbug Entertainment (part of Candle Media) in 2022. Studio closed February 2024 following Moonbug layoffs.

name: 3Hz
significance: Japanese anime studio founded March 2013 by Yuichiro Matsuka (ex-Kinema Citrus). Known for distinctive visual style in 'Flip Flappers' (2016), 'Princess Principal' (2017), and 'Sword Art Online Alternative: Gun Gale Online' (2018). Acquired by A-1 Pictures (Sony Music Entertainment Japan) in June 2024, effectively ending independent operations.

name: The Mill
significance: Global VFX studio primarily serving advertising and branding. Founded in London, acquired by Technicolor in 2015 for ~$300M. Award-winning commercial work including Nike, Apple campaigns. Film work includes posters for Nope (Jordan Peele). Collapsed February 2025 with Technicolor administration.

name: Technicolor Animation
significance: Historic company famous for bringing color to cinema. Worked on classics from The Wizard of Oz to Disney's 1940 Pinocchio. Parent of MPC, The Mill, Mikros Animation, and Technicolor Games. After aggressive acquisitions created unsustainable debt, collapsed February 2025 in administration (UK) and liquidation (France, US). At peak employed 4,000-10,000 globally. One of the largest collapses in VFX history.

name: ON Animation Studios
significance: Montreal-based CGI animation studio owned by Mediawan. Known for feature films including Mune: Guardian of the Moon, The Little Prince (2015, dir. Mark Osborne), Playmobil: The Movie (2019), and Ladybug & Cat Noir: The Movie (2023). Closed February 2025 after Quebec government capped animation/VFX tax credits at 65%, contributing to widespread industry collapse in the province.

name: Axis Studios
significance: Scotland's largest animation and VFX studio, founded in Glasgow by Richard Scott, Dana Dorian, Stuart Aitken, and Graham McKenna. Created content for BBC, Netflix, Blizzard, Activision, and Marvel (Eyes of Wakanda). Known for iconic Dead Island trailer and game cinematics for Halo, Gears of War, League of Legends. Entered administration July 2024 due to declining projects and rising labor costs; 162 employees lost jobs.

name: Xanthus Animation Studio
significance: Taiwanese CGI animation studio established in 2004. Creative team with expertise in both product development and production. Known for popular children's series Yameme and collaborations on global franchises including Final Fantasy and Monster Strike. Produced 2049+ Voice of Rebirth (2021), a CGI sci-fi feature based on the Netflix series 2049, co-produced with Greener Grass Production. Leading brand in Taiwanese multimedia and digital entertainment.

name: Submarine Studio
significance: Dutch animation and production studio known for innovative techniques. Co-produced Undone with Minnow Mountain, pioneering oil-painting rotoscope animation.

name: WAU Animation
significance: Malaysian CG animation studio (WAU Animation) founded March 18, 2013 by Usamah Zaid Yasin, a graduate of MMU Cyberjaya. Creators of Ejen Ali (Agent Ali), Malaysia's most iconic animated series and the first animation IP published by Media Prima Berhad. Ejen Ali premiered on TV3 in April 2016. The Ejen Ali Movie (2019) earned RM30 million at the Malaysian box office. Specializes in end-to-end CG animation production. Based in Cyberjaya, Malaysia.

name: Comenius-Film
significance: German production company founded by Louis Hagen Jr. that financed pioneering silhouette animator Lotte Reiniger's work from 1923 onward. Produced Die Abenteuer des Prinzen Achmed (The Adventures of Prince Achmed, 1926), widely regarded as the oldest surviving animated feature film. Also produced Doctor Dolittle and His Animals (1928) and other Reiniger silhouette films. Based in Berlin during the Weimar Republic era.

name: Robot Playground Media
significance: Singapore's leading animation studio founded by Ervin Han. Award-winning works include TimeScapes and Downstairs. Known for distinctly Singaporean storytelling.

name: Big Cat Studio
significance: Taiwanese animation studio founded in 2012 by Wang Wei Xiu in Taipei. Best known for creating Brave Animated Series (2022), Taiwan's first original animation on Netflix, produced with Public Television Service. Also created Diego & Pea miniseries, and animated shorts Seven Thirty Astronaut and Our Moon. Part of the growing Taiwanese original animation industry.

name: Canadian Film Development Corporation
significance: Canadian federal Crown corporation established in 1967 to foster and promote the development of a feature film industry in Canada. Restructured as Telefilm Canada in 1984. Provided financing for Canadian animated and live-action productions.

name: BBC Wales
significance: BBC's national region in Wales, headquartered in Cardiff. Co-produces animated content including collaborations with Soyuzmultfilm and S4C.

name: Warner Premiere
significance: Direct-to-video production arm of Warner Bros. Entertainment, established in 2006. Produced original films and animated features for home video release. Merged into Warner Bros. Animation in 2013.

name: CINAR Corporation
significance: Canadian entertainment company specializing in children's programming. Produced and co-produced animated series including Arthur and Caillou. Involved in accounting scandal in 2000; restructured as Cookie Jar Entertainment in 2004 (now WildBrain).

name: France 3
significance: French public national television channel, part of France Télévisions. Co-produces and broadcasts animated content, including international co-productions with European partners.

name: S4C
significance: Sianel Pedwar Cymru (Channel Four Wales), Welsh-language public television channel. Commissions and co-produces Welsh-language animation, including collaborations with BBC Wales and international partners.

name: Gross Films
significance: Israeli animation studio founded by Yoram Gross in 1962, producing the Middle East's first animated feature 'Joseph the Dreamer' (Ba'al Hahalomot) using stop-motion puppetry. Gross later relocated to Australia in 1968 and founded Yoram Gross Film Studios, producing Dot and the Kangaroo and Blinky Bill.

name: WDR
significance: Westdeutscher Rundfunk, Germany's largest public broadcaster based in Cologne. Co-produces animated films and series, including international co-productions with Revcom and other European partners.

name: TV2 Denmark
significance: Danish television network. Co-produces and broadcasts animated content, including collaborations with A. Film A/S and other Danish animation studios.

name: Discreet Arts
significance: Indian animation studio founded in Hyderabad by CEO Srikanth Pottekula (originally as Laughing Lion Studio in 2008, rebranded 2012). Work-for-hire studio with offices in Hyderabad, Chennai, Manila, and Burbank. Clients include Ánima Estudios, Titmouse, and Studio 100.

name: Novanima
significance: French animation production company founded in 2006 by Marc Faye in Dordogne. Member of César Academy and AFCA. Produces animated and documentary films with artistic focus. Known for traditional 2D animation and socially-engaged documentaries.

name: Studioul Cinematografic București
significance: Romanian state film studio based in Bucharest. Ion Popescu-Gopo worked there from 1950. The animation department was spun off as Animafilm in 1964. Produced over 118 films during the Communist era.

name: Prime Focus
significance: India's largest integrated media services company, founded 1997 by Namit Malhotra in Mumbai. Pioneered India's first Digital Intermediate system. Merged with Academy Award-winning DNEG in 2014. Provides VFX, stereo 3D conversion, and animation for global studios.

name: Koninck International
significance: British production company founded in 1979 by Keith Griffiths together with the Brothers Quay (Stephen and Timothy Quay). The name originates from a Belgian beer label (De Koninck) whose typography appealed to them. Also known as Atelier Koninck or Koninck Studios — the studio and production company operate as one entity. The Quays are acclaimed stop-motion puppet animators influenced by Jan Švankmajer and Eastern European surrealism. Known for Street of Crocodiles (1986), cited by Terry Gilliam as one of the ten best animated films ever made. Worked extensively with the Brothers Quay and Jan Švankmajer on experimental puppet animation including Conspirators of Pleasure (1996). Key partner for Channel 4's international animation co-productions. MoMA held their first major retrospective in 2012. Still active today and registered with UK Companies House.

name: Porchlight Entertainment
significance: American animation and live-action production company founded February 1995 by Bruce D. Johnson (former Hanna-Barbera VP) and William T. Baumann in Los Angeles. Produced family-friendly TV series including Jay Jay the Jetplane and Adventures From the Book of Virtues for PBS. Acquired by Trilogy Animation Group in 2018.

name: Heart of Europe Prague
significance: Czech/UK international co-production company founded in 1977 by Welsh producer Keith Griffiths. Specialized in European art animation co-productions, working with the Brothers Quay and Jan Švankmajer. Griffiths was Deputy Head of Production at BFI Production Board from 1976. Still operating as of 2021 with productions including Magic Lantern: A Film About Prague.

name: Youmex
significance: Japanese anime production company and record label founded in 1985 as a subsidiary of Toshiba EMI by Junji Fujita. Operated the Futureland label. Produced cult OVAs including Bubblegum Crisis, AD Police, and Dragon's Heaven through partnerships with AIC and Artmic.

name: GFM Animation
significance: British animation production and sales company founded March 2011 by former HandMade Films executives Guy Collins, Fred Hedman, and Michael Ryan. Successor to HandMade Films. Focuses on family-oriented animated feature films for global theatrical release.

name: Novinski
significance: Bratislava-based Slovak music and film production company founded in 2005 by composer Michal Novinski. Co-produced 'Living Large' (2024) with Barletta and Novanima. Run by Michal and producer Agata Novinski.

name: Biographic Films
significance: British animation studio co-founded in 1955 by Bob Godfrey, Keith Learner, and Jeff Hale. Made the first cartoon commercial for ITV's launch night in September 1955. Produced hundreds of TV commercials and short films before Godfrey left to form Bob Godfrey Films in 1965.

name: UniKo
significance: Spanish animation and advertising production company based in Bilbao, founded 2009. Co-produces Alberto Vázquez's features with Abano Producións including 'Unicorn Wars' and 'Decorado'. Over 350 international awards across 12 short films and 3 features.

name: Abano Producións
significance: Galician animation studio based in La Coruña, Spain. Primary producer of Alberto Vázquez's acclaimed films including 'Birdboy: The Forgotten Children' (Goya Award), 'Unicorn Wars' (2022), and 'Decorado' (2025). Known for dark, artistically bold adult animation.

name: Revoroot
significance: Founded April 1, 2016 as Twin Engine subsidiary. Originally Nishitokyo, relocated to Suginami 2022. FLCL Alternative (co-prod), Babylon, I've Been Killing Slimes for 300 Years. BECAME INDEPENDENT from Twin Engine 2021. CEO Kazuki Emani also runs spinoff Crew-Cell (stayed in Nishitokyo).

name: Geno Studio
significance: Founded November 19, 2015 by Kōji Yamamoto (ex-Fuji TV Noitamina executive). Suginami, Tokyo. Created to complete Genocidal Organ after Manglobe bankruptcy, using former Manglobe staff. 100% Twin Engine subsidiary. Golden Kamuy (S1-3), Kokkoku, Star Wars: Visions (Lop & Ochō). 17 employees.

name: Studio M2
significance: Founded March 2016 by legendary producer Masao Maruyama (co-founder Madhouse 1972, founder MAPPA 2011). Pre-production planning company. Pluto (2023, Netflix - 6 years in development, 94% RT audience score). Maruyama's third major studio at age 75.

name: SynergySP
significance: Founded September 24, 1998 as Synergy Japan by ex-Studio Junio staff (Minoru Okazaki, Minoru Maeda, Hiroshi Wagatsuma). Koganei, Tokyo. Major (S4-6), Mermaid Melody, Princess Comet. Affiliated with Shogakukan-Shueisha Productions 2005 (renamed to SynergySP). SHIN-EI ANIMATION subsidiary since April 2017.

name: Gallop
significance: Founded December 13, 1978 by ex-Mushi Pro members. Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters franchise (2000-2019, 6 series defining the studio), Ojarumaru (1998-present, 2000+ episodes, first NHK digital ink-and-paint), Kodocha, Dirty Pair episodes. Long-running children's/card game specialist.

name: Nexus
significance: Founded 2012. Suginami, Tokyo. Ex-A-1 Pictures staff. First film: Santa Company (2014). Chivalry of a Failed Knight (co-prod w/ Silver Link), Comic Girls, Darwin's Game, Granbelm (2019, first original TV), The Eminence in Shadow. Growing isekai/fantasy specialist.

name: Lay-duce
significance: Founded August 2013 by Noritomo Yonai (ex-Bones producer). Nakano, Tokyo. Twin Engine affiliate 2018-2021 (CEO on Twin Engine board). Fate/Grand Order -First Order-, Release the Spyce, Tomo-chan Is a Girl!, Rising Impact. Over 20 titles by 2025.

name: Yokohama Animation Lab
significance: Founded July 2015 by Yuma Ogami (ex-Production I.G Division 7 producer). Naka-ku, Yokohama - rare non-Tokyo HQ. Lapis Re:LiGHTs, Villainess Level 99, Hell Mode. 50 employees by 2023. ACQUIRED BY FRONTIER WORKS (Animate Group) September 2025.

name: EMT Squared
significance: Founded July 25, 2013 by Hideaki Miyamoto (ex-TMS Entertainment producer). Suginami, Tokyo. Nyanko Days, Love Tyrant, Assassin's Pride, The Demon King's Daughter is Too Kind. Has integrated CG department for 3DCG support.

name: Kachigarasu
significance: Founded August 5, 2008 as Encourage Films by ex-Gonzo producer Tōyō Ikeda and director Fumitoshi Oizaki. Nerima, Tokyo. Hitorijime My Hero, Is the Order a Rabbit? production. Ikeda passed 2013, Oizaki became CEO. RENAMED TO KACHIGARASU December 2023.

name: Studio Kai
significance: Founded June 2019 by ADK Emotions. Suginami, Tokyo. Inherited Gonzo's anime production/IP rights July 2019. Uma Musume Pretty Derby S2-S3 (breakout), Super Cub, Skeleton Knight in Another World, Captain Tsubasa S2. Reported ¥165M loss in 2020.

name: Bibury Animation Studios
significance: Founded May 1, 2017 by Motoki 'Tensho' Tanaka (director of Kiniro Mosaic, Grisaia at White Fox/8-Bit). Grisaia: Phantom Trigger (2019, first major work), Azur Lane: The Animation, The Quintessential Quintuplets S2-movie, 100 Girlfriends, Black Rock Shooter: Dawn Fall. Sister studio Bibury Animation CG handles 3DCG.

name: Connect
significance: Japanese animation studio founded April 2012 as a subsidiary of Silver Link. Co-produced Strike the Blood, ORESUKI, The Honor Student at Magic High School. Absorbed by Silver Link in July 2020—dissolved as a separate company but continues as an internal division/brand name within Silver Link.

name: Silver Link
significance: Founded December 2007 by ex-Frontline producer Hayato Kaneko. Mitaka, Tokyo HQ. Shin Ōnuma (ex-Shaft) directs most shows, giving distinctive visual style. Baka and Test, Non Non Biyori, Fate/kaleid liner, BOFURI, My Next Life as a Villainess. ACQUIRED BY ASAHI BROADCASTING 2020, moved under ABC Animation 2023.

name: David Production
significance: Founded September 2007 by Kōji Kajita (ex-Gonzo president) and Taito Okiura in Kodaira, Tokyo. First lead: Ristorante Paradiso (2009). JoJo's Bizarre Adventure (2012-present, defining franchise), Cells at Work!, Fire Force, Urusei Yatsura (2022). ACQUIRED BY FUJI TV August 2014.

name: Studio Trigger
significance: Founded August 22, 2011 by ex-Gainax staff Hiroyuki Imaishi and Masahiko Ōtsuka. Spiritual successor to Gainax's style. Kill la Kill (2013, first TV series), Little Witch Academia, Darling in the Franxx (with A-1), Promare (first film), SSSS.Gridman, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners. Known for kinetic action, bold colors.

name: Wit Studio
significance: Founded June 1, 2012 by George Wada (ex-Production I.G) as IG Port subsidiary. ¥30M initial capital. Attack on Titan S1-3 (debut project), Kabaneri of the Iron Fortress, Vinland Saga, Spy x Family (with CloverWorks), Bubble. Director Tetsurō Araki. JOEN joint venture with CloverWorks 2022.

name: White Fox
significance: Founded April 2007 by Gaku Iwasa (ex-OLM Team Iwasa). First production: Tears to Tiara. Breakthrough: Steins;Gate (2011), Katanagatari (2010). Re:Zero, Akame ga Kill!, The Devil is a Part-Timer!, Goblin Slayer. Studio Bind subsidiary. ACQUIRED BY ALPHAPOLIS July 2025.

name: Studio Pierrot
significance: Founded May 1979 by Yuji Nunokawa (ex-Tatsunoko/Mushi Pro) in Mitaka, Tokyo. Creamy Mami, Urusei Yatsura (from Studio Deen), Yu Yu Hakusho, Naruto, Bleach, Tokyo Ghoul, Black Clover. Acquired Studio Kikan 2008 (renamed Pierrot+, then Studio Signpost 2017). Studio Pierrot+ became Pierrot Films 2024. 45th anniversary 2024.

name: Telecom Animation Film
significance: Founded May 19, 1975 as TMS Entertainment subsidiary. Created by Yutaka Fujioka to train full-animation animators for US market. Early home of Hayao Miyazaki, Isao Takahata, Yasuo Otsuka. Castle of Cagliostro support, Little Nemo. Disney subcontract work (DuckTales, Gargoyles). Lupin III films. Now Sega Sammy subsidiary.

name: Studio Deen
significance: Founded March 14, 1975 by ex-Sunrise producer Hiroshi Hasegawa. Name from first job: Brave Raideen. Started as finishing studio for Sunrise. Own productions from 1982. Took over Urusei Yatsura from Pierrot. Rurouni Kenshin, Fate/stay night (2006), KonoSuba, Higurashi. Subsidiaries: Danny Donghua, Megumi, Umidori. IMA Group subsidiary since 2011.

name: Gainax
significance: Began as Daicon Film 1981 by university otaku: Hideaki Anno, Yoshiyuki Sadamoto, Hiroyuki Yamaga, Takami Akai, Toshio Okada. Officially founded 1984. Royal Space Force, Gunbuster, Nadia, Neon Genesis Evangelion (1995), FLCL, Gurren Lagann. Financial troubles, sued by Khara 2016. DECLARED BANKRUPTCY 2024, DISSOLVED DECEMBER 2025.

name: Shanghai Animation Film Studio
significance: Founded April 1957 in Shanghai. Led by Te Wei and Wan Brothers (Princess Iron Fan, 1941). China's oldest/largest animation studio. 500+ films, 40,000+ minutes. Uproar in Heaven (1964), Nezha, Black Cat Detective, Calabash Brothers. 'Chinese School of Animation.' 200+ awards. Part of Shanghai Film Group.

name: Madhouse
significance: Founded 1972 in Nakano, Tokyo by ex-Mushi Pro animators: Masao Maruyama, Osamu Dezaki, Rintaro, Yoshiaki Kawajiri. Contract work until 1990s. Trigun, Cardcaptor Sakura, Perfect Blue, Death Note, One-Punch Man S1. Satoshi Kon's home studio. Maruyama left 2011 to found MAPPA. Spawned Triangle Staff, Nomad, Studio VOLN, Nut.

name: Ajia-do Animation Works
significance: Japanese animation studio founded October 4, 1978 in Saitama by noted animators Tsutomu Shibayama, Osamu Kobayashi, and Michishiro Yamada, all former members of A Production (Shin-Ei Animation). The name Ajia-dō (亜細亜堂, 'Hall of Asia') is a pen name used by Shibayama and Kobayashi. Originally a yugen-gaisha (limited company), it became a kabushiki-gaisha (stock company) in 1985. Established digital animation division in 1998. Best known for the NHK long-running children's series Nintama Rantarō (1993–present, 2500+ episodes). Other notable works include Spirit of Wonder (1992 OVA), Zettai Shōnen (Absolute Boy, 2005), Emma: A Victorian Romance (2005–2007), Izetta: The Last Witch (2016), and Ascendance of a Bookworm (2019–2022). Also established subsidiaries Dap International and Japan Taps (with Takara, disbanded ~1995). Currently headed by president Shinichiro Ozawa with approximately 81 employees.

name: Studio Hibari
significance: Founded July 1979 in Ōizumi, Gunma by Sachiko and Hiroyoshi Mitsunobu (ex-Tsuchida). Moved to Nerima 1998. ~100 employees. Duel Masters, Mirumo de Pon!. Founded Larx Entertainment (3DCG, 2006) and Lerche (2011) subsidiaries. Son Seiji became managing director 1985.

name: Topcraft
significance: Founded February 1, 1972 by Toru Hara (ex-Toei). Rankin/Bass primary hand-drawn studio: The Hobbit (1977), Return of the King (1980), The Last Unicorn (1982). Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind (1984) with Miyazaki. Dissolved 1985; staff became Studio Ghibli (Hara as first manager) and Pacific Animation Corporation (ThunderCats, Silverhawks).

name: Magic Bus
significance: Founded April 1972 by Satoshi Dezaki (brother of Osamu Dezaki) in Nishi-Tokyo. First work: Shin Kyojin no Hoshi (1977). Captain (1983). Known for 1980s OVA gore (Beast Fighter, Big Wars). Largely animation subcontractor for other studios (especially Eiken). 200+ anime credits. Niigata satellite studio.

name: Rough Draft Korea
significance: Founded April 20, 1992 by Park Kyung-sook in Seoul as Rough Draft Studios' overseas division. Parent founded 1991 by Gregg Vanzo in Van Nuys garage. The Simpsons (S4-30), Futurama (primary), SpongeBob SquarePants. Alternates with Digital eMation on Futurama S8+. Hyejoon Yun coordinates international liaison.

name: Toon City Animation
significance: Founded 1993 by British animator Colin Baker in Manila with ~10 animators. Emmy-winning. Primary Disney Television Animation contractor. Universal, Netflix, Warner Bros., Xilam partner. 350+ artists. 2D hand-drawn, ToonBoom Harmony, Adobe Animate. Vancouver expansion 2023. 'We take fun seriously.'

name: Yeson Entertainment
significance: Founded 1993 by President Kyung-Ja Park in Seoul. Started as Rough Draft Korea collaborator (40% of their production). Independent since 1998. The Simpsons, King of the Hill, Family Guy, Daria, Dilbert, Bob's Burgers, Ed Edd n Eddy, Fairly OddParents. Traditional animation foundation, now digital via ToonBoom.

name: Wang Film Productions
significance: Founded 1978 by James Chung-Yuan Wang as Cuckoo's Nest Studio in Taiwan. Also Hong Guang Animation. Hanna-Barbera co-owned/trained. 4,000+ TV episodes, 66 features. 1990s: 1,000+ employees, 70% of world animation, largest studio globally. The Smurfs, Rugrats, Animaniacs. Disney, WB, Nelvana, Universal.

name: Dong Yang Animation
significance: Founded 1981 in Seoul. Also known as Dongyang Animation, DongYang-DongHwa. Long-term TMS/Koko partner. Every DCAU series except Zeta Project. Batman TAS, Batman Beyond, Superman TAS (Emmy Awards). Also Captain N S1, Filmation, Disney, Saban. Often paired with Koko Enterprises on WB projects.

name: Saerom Animation
significance: Founded 1987 by Gilhwan Kim in Seoul. Originally Sae Rom Productions Co., Ltd. Disney (Aladdin series, Gargoyles, Clerks), Nickelodeon (Hey Arnold! S2-5, Dora the Explorer, Go Diego Go), Cartoon Network (Johnny Bravo, My Gym Partner's a Monkey). Smiling Friends S3 primary studio. Known for deranged animation style.

name: Plus One Animation
significance: Founded January 1991 by veteran director Choon Man Lee as Saerom Animation subsidiary. DiC origin (Slimer spinoff). Mike Judge specialist: King of the Hill, Beavis and Butt-Head, Daria. Also Doug, 101 Dalmatians series, Recess S2+. Now Plus One Entertainment. Website still active post-Flash deprecation.

name: Koko Enterprises
significance: Founded March 2, 1990 by Myong Ok Jeon in Seoul. TMS Entertainment/Sega ownership. Warner Bros. regular (Animaniacs, Gargoyles, Histeria!, Iron Man TAS S2). Often paired with Dong Yang Animation. Rebranded as CNK International 2011, pivoted to mining industry. Animation ceased April 2011.

name: Digital eMation
significance: Founded March 27, 1993 in Seoul. Name: 'e' (education) + 'mation' (animation). Originally educational content. Family Guy, Cleveland Show, Animaniacs (2020), OK K.O.! Let's Be Heroes, Futurama S8+ (even episodes, alternating with Rough Draft Korea). Victor and Valentino.

name: Yearim Productions
significance: Founded 1991 in Seoul, LA satellite office. Full-service 2D/digital animation. Warner Bros. regular (Duck Dodgers, Baby Looney Tunes, Looney Tunes Cartoons, Tom & Jerry series). Also Family Guy, American Dad, Big Mouth, Gravity Falls, Dragon Tales. Uses ToonBoom Harmony.

name: Sunwoo Entertainment
significance: Founded 1974 as Sunwoo Production Inc in Seoul. Now Sunwoo & Company. Disney Afternoon pioneer (Chip 'n Dale, Darkwing Duck). Nickelodeon mainstay (Rocko's Modern Life, Invader Zim). Also Duckman, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. Now IP business enterprise focusing on content production, distribution, and licensing.

name: AKOM Production
significance: Founded 1985 by Nelson Shin (animated Star Wars lightsaber effects at DePatie-Freleng) in Seoul's Songpa-gu. Over 200 Simpsons episodes plus The Simpsons Movie (2007). Also X-Men TAS, Batman TAS (fired for quality issues), Tiny Toon Adventures, Arthur. Pioneer of Korean OEM animation industry. Multiple Emmy Awards.

name: MOI Animation
significance: Founded 1998 as DR Movie spinoff in Seoul. Madhouse ownership/partnership. Emmy Award-winning. Avatar: TLA Book 3 (10 episodes with JM Animation). Warner Bros. regular (Justice League, Batman). Castlevania (Netflix). Rebranded as Tiger Animation 2018 under CEO Seohoon Son. Vietnam satellite studio.

name: Hanho Heung-Up
significance: Founded 1984 by Steven Hahn in Seoul. Now known as Dream Creator Hanho. 1,400+ episodes produced. Disney (Darkwing Duck, Winnie the Pooh), Nickelodeon (Doug), Bob's Burgers, The Real Ghostbusters, Magic School Bus, Paradise PD. Korean productions: Dooly the Baby Dinosaur, Fly Superboard (1990-2002). Kim Seok-Ki currently president.

name: JM Animation
significance: Founded August 20, 1997 in Seoul. Avatar: The Last Airbender (32 episodes across all 3 books, with DR Movie and MOI). Jae-Myung Yu worked here before founding Studio Mir. Pre-production on Legend of Korra before transfer to Mir. Also Dante's Inferno animated, Anyamaru Tantei Kiruminzuu.

name: Fortiche Production
significance: Founded June 3, 2009 by Pascal Charrue, Jérôme Combe, Arnaud Delord in Paris. Studios in Paris, Montpellier, Las Palmas. Long-term Riot Games partnership. Arcane (Netflix, 2021/2024) - most-watched animated series. Distinctive 2D/3D hybrid style. France 2030 laureate.

name: DR Movie
significance: Founded November 1990 by Jeong-Gyun Jeong in Seoul. Exclusive Madhouse partnership since 1991 (partial owner 2001). ~400 employees, largest Korean animation workforce. Avatar: TLA (Books 1-2), Claymore, Tenjho Tenge. Only Korean studio partnered with Studio Ghibli. Qingdao JV 2007.

name: Dong Woo Animation
significance: Founded March 1991 in Seoul (incorporated April 1999). Renamed Dong Woo A&E 2012. Studio Gallop subsidiary and primary outsourcer since 1994. Warner Bros. Animation main overseas house since 2002. Yu-Gi-Oh! franchise, Teen Titans, The Batman.

name: SAMG Entertainment
significance: Founded July 26, 2000 as SAMG Animation by Suhoon Kim in Seoul. Korea's leading 3D/CGI studio. Renamed SAMG Entertainment 2021. Miraculous Ladybug (co-producer), Miniforce, Watch-Car, Vroomiz. Expanded into toys, e-commerce, licensing. Public company.

name: Zagtoon
significance: Founded May 15, 2009 by Jeremy Zag and Jacqueline Tordjman (ex-Saban) in Paris. Univergroup subsidiary. Also known as ZAG Entertainment, ZAG Animation Studios. Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir (global phenomenon). Miraculous Corp JV with Mediawan 2024.

name: Cyber Group Studios
significance: Founded August 2005 by Pierre Sissmann and Dominique Bourse (ex-Disney EMEA) in Paris. Acquired Pictor Media 2016. US subsidiary 2017 (Culver City). Roubaix studio 2018. Studios in France, USA, UK, Italy, Singapore. Gigantosaurus, Zorro the Chronicles.

name: Blue Spirit
significance: Founded 2004 by Éric Jacquot. Part of Studio TF1 group since 2017. Olivier Lelardoux CEO 2023. Studios: Angoulême, Paris, Montreal. My Life as a Zucchini (Oscar nom, César), Blue Eye Samurai (Netflix), What If...? (Marvel), Gremlins: Secrets of the Mogwai.

name: Mikros Animation
significance: Founded 1985 as Mikros Image by Maurice Prost in Paris. VFX and animation for European cinema. Acquired by Technicolor 2015. Credits: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem, PAW Patrol films, Captain Underpants, SpongeBob: Sponge on the Run, Thelma the Unicorn, Star Trek: Prodigy. After Technicolor collapsed February 2025, acquired by Rodeo FX in March 2025, preserving ~287 jobs in Montreal and Paris. Studios: Paris, Montreal.

name: Illumination Studios Paris
significance: Formed 2011 when Universal/Illumination acquired Mac Guff animation division. Renamed from Illumination Mac Guff 2021. Paris HQ. Produces all Illumination films: Despicable Me series, Minions, Secret Life of Pets, Sing, The Super Mario Bros. Movie. Benefits from French animation subsidies.

name: Method Studios
significance: Founded 1998 in Los Angeles. VFX for commercials, music videos, then films. Acquired Atomic Fiction 2015. Work on Deadpool 2, Black Panther, Avengers: Infinity War. Sold by Deluxe to Framestore 2020 (finalized 2022). Studios: LA, NYC, Atlanta, Vancouver, Montreal, Melbourne.

name: Mac Guff
significance: Founded 1986 as MGL Studio in Paris by Jacques Bled and 4 partners. VFX pioneer, La Vie des bêtes (1988). Despicable Me animation (2010). Animation arm sold to Universal 2011, became Illumination Mac Guff (now Illumination Studios Paris). VFX division continues independently.

name: TeamTO
significance: Founded 2005 by Guillaume Hellouin, Corinne Kouper, Caroline Souris in Paris. Second facility in Bourg-lès-Valence 2008. Angelo Rules, Mighty Mike, Presto! School of Magic. Netflix, Disney partnerships. Acquired by RIVA Studios December 2024 after financial difficulties.

name: Superprod Animation
significance: Founded 2010 by Clément Calvet and Jérémie Fajner (ex-Gaumont Animation directors). Paris and Angoulême studios, offices in LA and NY. USD/Pixar pipeline technology. Acquired Red Monk Studio (Italy) 2021, Melusine Productions (Luxembourg). Fast-growing European animation group.

name: Method Animation
significance: Founded 1998 as Method Films by Aton Soumache in Paris. CGI and 2D animation. Merged with Chapter 2 and Onyx Films 2014. Acquired by Mediawan 2018 via ON Kids & Family. The Little Prince (2015), Playmobil: The Movie. Now part of Mediawan Kids & Family division.

name: Wētā FX
significance: Founded 1993 as Weta Digital by Peter Jackson, Richard Taylor, Jamie Selkirk for Heavenly Creatures. Wellington HQ. Lord of the Rings, King Kong (Oscar), Avatar (Oscar), Planet of the Apes trilogy. Pioneered motion capture, Massive crowd software. Rebranded Wētā FX 2021. Unity Technologies acquisition 2021.

name: Cinesite
significance: Founded 1991 in Hollywood (Kodak Cineon system), London 1994. Independent VFX and animation group. Addams Family (2019/2021), Iwájú (Disney+). Subsidiaries: Image Engine, Trixter, L'Atelier Animation, Squeeze. $215M raised 2025. London HQ, Montreal, Vancouver studios.

name: Moving Picture Company
significance: Founded April 1, 1970 by Mike Luckwell in London. VFX pioneer: The Jungle Book (Oscar 2017), 1917, The Lion King (2019). Now part of Technicolor Creative Studios. Global studios: London, LA, Montreal, Bangalore, Vancouver. Leading creature/environment work.

name: DNEG
significance: Founded 1998 as Double Negative in London. Merged with Prime Focus 2014, rebranded DNEG. 7 VFX Oscars: Inception, Interstellar, Ex Machina, Blade Runner 2049, First Man, Tenet, Dune. DNEG Animation division. 11,000 employees, 19 studios worldwide.

name: Framestore
significance: Founded December 1986 by William Sargent, Sharon Reed, Tim Webber in London. Merged with Computer Film Company 1997. Europe's largest VFX studio (~3,000 staff). Gravity (Oscar), The Golden Compass (Oscar), Paddington films. Locations: London, NYC, LA, Montreal, Mumbai.

name: Industrial Light & Magic
significance: Founded May 28, 1975 by George Lucas for Star Wars VFX. Presidio SF HQ. Pioneered modern VFX: motion control, digital compositing, CGI characters. Computer graphics division became Pixar (1986). 16 Oscar wins for VFX. Now Lucasfilm/Disney subsidiary. Studios in SF, London, Vancouver, Sydney.

name: Animal Logic
significance: Founded 1991 by Zareh Nalbandian and Chris Godfrey in Sydney. First Australian CG feature: Happy Feet (2006, Oscar winner). Also Happy Feet Two, Legend of the Guardians, Peter Rabbit series, The LEGO Movie. Acquired by Netflix 2022, now part of Netflix Animation Studios. VFX/animation hybrid.

name: Reel FX Animation
significance: Founded 1993 as Reel Magic by Dale Carman and David Needham in Fort Worth, Texas garage. Dallas HQ, plus Santa Monica and Montreal. Free Birds (2013), The Book of Life (2014), Rumble. Texas Avery Animation Award since 2007. Super Giant Robot Brothers! (2022) pioneered Unreal Engine TV animation.

name: Ilion Animation Studios
significance: Founded 2002 in Madrid by Javier and Ignacio Pérez Dolset (Pyro Studios founders). Planet 51 (2009), Mortadelo y Filemón (2014). Partner with U-Tad university. Skydance partnership 2017, acquired 2020, rebranded as Skydance Animation Madrid. Now part of Paramount Skydance Corp.

name: The SPA Studios
significance: Founded 2004 as Animagic S.L. by Sergio Pablos (ex-Disney animator: Tarzan, Treasure Planet) and Marisa Román in Madrid. Renamed 2010 (Sergio Pablos Animation). Created concepts for Despicable Me and Smallfoot. Klaus (2019, Netflix's first animated feature, BAFTA winner, Oscar nom). Currently producing Ember.

name: Rough Draft Studios
significance: Founded March 20, 1991 by Gregg and Nikki Vanzo in Van Nuys garage. Pioneered US-Korea animation pipeline via Rough Draft Korea (Seoul, 1992). The Simpsons (seasons 4-30), Futurama, The Ren & Stimpy Show. Now headquartered in Glendale, CA. Revolutionized TV animation outsourcing model.

name: Skydance Animation
significance: Founded March 16, 2017 by David Ellison (Skydance Media). Acquired Ilion Animation Studios (Madrid) 2020, rebranded Skydance Animation Madrid. Led by John Lasseter. Apple TV+ deal 2019-2023, now Netflix. Luck (2022), Spellbound (2024). Merged into Paramount August 2025.

name: Netflix Animation Studios
significance: Founded March 2018 to develop in-house animation. Burbank HQ with Sydney and Vancouver offices. Klaus (2019, Oscar nom, BAFTA win), I Lost My Body, Over the Moon. Acquired Animal Logic 2022-2024. Recruited DreamWorks Animation executives. ~6 animated features per year target.

name: Titmouse
significance: Founded May 3, 2000 by Chris and Shannon Prynoski, named after Chris's favorite bird. Started as t-shirt company, pivoted to animation. LA/NYC/Vancouver/Paris studios, 700+ employees. Metalocalypse, The Venture Bros., Big Mouth, Star Trek: Lower Decks, Legend of Vox Machina. Vancouver studio unionized 2020 (IATSE Local 938).

name: Eesti Joonisfilm
significance: Independent successor to Tallinnfilm animation department (1976). Led by Priit Pärn, Estonia's most celebrated animator. Known for surrealist, philosophical auteur films: Triangle (1982), Breakfast on the Grass (1987), Hotel E (1992). 80+ international festival awards. Major influence on Eastern European animation.

name: Soyuzmultfilm
significance: Founded June 10, 1936 as Soyuzdetmultfilm (renamed 1937). USSR's largest animation studio, 1,500+ films. Nu, Pogodi!, Cheburashka, Winnie-the-Pooh (Soviet). Known for experimental diversity in styles. Puppet division added 1954. Now Russian state-owned. Two theme parks in Moscow and Kazan.

name: Nathan Love
significance: Founded by Joe Burrascano in New York. CG character animation studio for advertising: Kellogg's, Kraft, Pepsi, Nickelodeon. Acquired by Aardman 2015, became Aardman Nathan Love (reverted 2019). Bristol/NYC locations. Expanding into original IP and long-form.

name: Xilam
significance: Founded by Marc du Pontavice in Paris after leaving Gaumont. Oggy and the Cockroaches, Space Goofs, Zig & Sharko. Oscar-nominated I Lost My Body (2019). 2,700+ episodes, distributed in 190+ countries. Studios in Paris, Angoulême, Ho Chi Minh City. Publicly traded.

name: Les Armateurs
significance: Founded by Didier Brunner in Paris. Five Oscar nominations, two César Awards. Kirikou and the Sorceress (1998), The Triplets of Belleville (2003), Brendan and the Secret of Kells (2009), Ernest & Celestine (2012). Top French animation production house.

name: Cartoon Network Studios
significance: Founded October 21, 1994 as Hanna-Barbera division. Became independent entity 1999. Dexter's Laboratory, The Powerpuff Girls, Adventure Time, Steven Universe, Regular Show. Warner Bros. Discovery subsidiary. Absorbed Hanna-Barbera legacy.

name: WildBrain
significance: Founded in San Francisco (as Wild Brain) by ex-Colossal Pictures staff. Acquired by DHX Media 2010, which rebranded as WildBrain 2018. Peanuts Worldwide owner. Higglytown Heroes, Yo Gabba Gabba, Strawberry Shortcake. Major children's content company. In 2025, shut down its linear broadcast channels business (Family Channel, Family Jr., Télémagino) to focus on streaming and content licensing.

name: Mercury Filmworks
significance: Founded by Clint Eland in Vancouver, now based in Ottawa. Pioneered digital ink and paint in North America. Disney Television Animation partner since 2010: Mickey Mouse shorts, Wander Over Yonder, The Owl House. Co-founded Lighthouse Studios with Cartoon Saloon (2017).

name: Nickelodeon Animation Studio
significance: Founded as Games Animation 1992 by Vanessa Coffey and Mary Harrington. Renamed Nickelodeon Animation Studio 1998. SpongeBob SquarePants, Rugrats, Avatar: The Last Airbender, The Loud House, Dora the Explorer. Burbank and NYC locations. Paramount Global division.

name: Rankin/Bass Productions
significance: Founded by Arthur Rankin Jr. and Jules Bass as Videocraft International. Iconic holiday specials: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer (1964), Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town, Frosty the Snowman. Pioneered 'Animagic' stop-motion with Japanese animator Tadahito Mochinaga at MOM Production. Also The Hobbit (1977), The Last Unicorn.

name: Fleischer Studios
significance: Founded by Max and Dave Fleischer. Disney's chief competitor in 1930s. Betty Boop, Popeye, Superman, Koko the Clown. Invented the rotoscope (1915). First studio to produce sound cartoon sync (1924). Acquired by Paramount 1942. Pioneered many animation techniques including multiplane backgrounds.

name: Hanna-Barbera
significance: Founded July 7, 1957 by William Hanna, Joseph Barbera, George Sidney after MGM closed animation. Tom and Jerry creators. The Flintstones, Scooby-Doo, The Jetsons, Yogi Bear. Dominated Saturday morning TV. Acquired by Turner 1991, absorbed by Warner Bros 2001. ~249 cartoon series, 1,200+ hours.

name: Filmation
significance: Founded by Lou Scheimer, Norm Prescott, Hal Sutherland in Reseda, CA. He-Man and the Masters of the Universe, She-Ra, Fat Albert, Star Trek: The Animated Series. Notable for keeping all animation in-house (no outsourcing). Closed 1989. Superman cartoon series (1966) was breakthrough.

name: DreamWorks Animation
significance: Founded by Steven Spielberg, Jeffrey Katzenberg, David Geffen as DreamWorks SKG animation division. Shrek (first Best Animated Feature Oscar), Madagascar, Kung Fu Panda, How to Train Your Dragon, Trolls. Spun off as public company 2004. Acquired by NBCUniversal 2016.

name: Pixar Animation Studios
significance: Originated as Lucasfilm Computer Division (1979). Founded as independent company 1986 by Ed Catmull and Alvy Ray Smith with Steve Jobs investment. First fully CG feature: Toy Story (1995). Acquired by Disney 2006. Finding Nemo, The Incredibles, Up, Inside Out, Coco. 15 Best Animated Feature Oscars.

name: Aardman Animations
significance: Founded by Peter Lord and David Sproxton in Bristol. Wallace & Gromit, Shaun the Sheep, Chicken Run, Creature Comforts. Four Academy Awards. Pioneered claymation for television/commercials. Nick Park joined 1985. Name from their first character for BBC's Vision On.

name: Illumination
significance: Founded in 2007 by Chris Meledandri (ex-Fox Animation president). Also known as Illumination Entertainment. Despicable Me franchise (highest-grossing animated franchise ever), Minions, Sing, The Secret Life of Pets, Super Mario Bros. Movie. $9B+ worldwide gross. Production done at Illumination Studios Paris (formerly Mac Guff). Universal Pictures partnership. Spun off as public company 2004. Acquired by NBCUniversal 2016.

name: Sony Pictures Animation
significance: Founded May 9, 2002 as Sony Pictures Entertainment division. Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018 Oscar winner), Hotel Transylvania franchise, Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs, The Mitchells vs. The Machines. Works with Sony Pictures Imageworks for digital production. Based in Culver City, CA.

name: Shuka
significance: Spun off from Brain's Base staff who worked on original Durarara!!. Durarara!!x2 (Shou/Ten/Ketsu), Natsume's Book of Friends (S5-S6), 91 Days. Continues Brain's Base's ensemble storytelling tradition with same core staff and director (Takahiro Omori).

name: Khara
significance: Founded by Hideaki Anno to produce Rebuild of Evangelion tetralogy. Also known as Studio Khara. Name from Greek 'χαρά' (joy), logo handwritten by Anno's wife Moyoco. Took over Evangelion rights from Gainax. HQ in Suginami, Tokyo.

name: Brain's Base
significance: Founded by ex-TMS Entertainment staff. Durarara!!, Baccano!, Natsume's Book of Friends, Penguindrum, Spice and Wolf. Known for complex ensemble storytelling. HQ in Mitaka City. Shuka studio spun off in 2015.

name: Satelight
significance: Founded in Sapporo, Hokkaido. Created world's first fully digital TV anime (Bit the Cupid, 1996). Macross Frontier/Zero/Delta, Aquarion, Symphogear franchises. Shōji Kawamori as special adviser. Name: S(apporo) A(nimate) T(echnology) E(ntertainment).

name: Bee Train
significance: Japanese animation studio founded June 5, 1997 by Kōichi Mashimo under Production I.G as a subsidiary (became independent in 2006). Known for .hack//Sign, .hack//Roots, Noir, Madlax, Phantom: Requiem for the Phantom, Tsubasa Chronicle, and the 'Girls with Guns' trilogy (Noir, Madlax, El Cazador de la Bruja). Strong yuri fandom following for female leads with ambiguous relationships. Animation production operations were reorganized into C-Station (which became independent via management buyout). Effectively inactive since Hyougemono (2011), with no new productions. The company entity still technically exists but is dormant — should be considered defunct.

name: Arms
significance: Japanese animation studio founded in 1996. Known for ecchi and adult-oriented works including Elfen Lied (2004), Ikki Tousen (2003), Queen's Blade (2009), Kite (1998), and Mezzo Forte (2000). Renamed Common Sense Co. in 2017. Filed for bankruptcy in August 2020. Final project Shin Ikki Tousen (2022) was completed by Studio Signpost after the studio's closure.

name: Studio Elle
significance: Originally Leo Production (1961), renamed 1975. Support studio specializing in finish/in-between animation. Attack on Titan, Bleach (support work). Star Wars: Visions 'Tatooine Rhapsody' (2021). Acquired Anime Spot 2012. HQ in Nakano, Tokyo.

name: Hal Film Maker
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by ex-Toei Animation staff. Known for critically acclaimed series including Princess Tutu (2002–2003), the ARIA series (2005–2008, directed by Junichi Sato), Tamayura (2011–2013), and Prétear (2001). Junichi Sato served as a board director from 2000, bringing distinctive slice-of-life sensibility to the studio's output. Merged into Yumeta Company (now TYO Animations) in 2009.

name: Studio Fantasia
significance: Japanese animation studio founded in 1983 by Tomohisa Iizuka, formerly of Tokyo Movie Shinsha. Known primarily for ecchi and mecha anime including Agent Aika (1997), Stratos 4 (2003), Best Student Council (2005), and Najica Blitz Tactics (2001). Also contributed production work on numerous other anime as a subcontractor. Ceased operations in 2016 following financial difficulties.

name: AIC
significance: Anime International Company (AIC). Founded June 15, 1982 by Kazufumi Nomura and Toru Miura (ex-Mushi/Tezuka) in Nerima, Tokyo. Pioneered OVA format alongside Studio Pierrot. Megazone 23, Bubblegum Crisis, Tenchi Muyo!, El-Hazard, Ah! My Goddess, Gall Force. At peak had eight divisions including AIC ASTA, AIC Build, AIC Classic, AIC Digital, AIC Frontier, AIC PLUS+, AIC Spirits, and AIC Takarazuka. Became Aplix subsidiary in 2011; shares sold back to founder Toru Miura for ¥8,000 in January 2014. Spawned Troyca and Production IMS from ex-staff departures in 2013. Animation production department officially disbanded August 2015. AIC RIGHTS Co., Ltd. was spun off in December 2015 as a separate entity to manage and exploit legacy IPs (Megazone 23, Tenchi Muyo!, Bubblegum Crisis, El-Hazard); AIC RIGHTS partnered with Toei Agency in 2021 for new content development.

name: Diomedéa
significance: Originally Studio Barcelona, spun off from Group TAC. Renamed Diomedéa 2008. Squid Girl, Girlish Number, Aho Girl, Domestic Girlfriend, Ron Kamonohashi. Partners with Studio Blanc (Ezóla brand). ~73 employees.

name: Eiken
significance: Formerly Tele-Cartoon Japan (TCJ). Sazae-san (1969-present), the longest-running anime ever with 7,000+ episodes. Last anime to use hand-painted cels (until 2015). Fuji TV owns 10%. Acquired by Krafton (South Korea) via ADK Holdings in 2025.

name: Studio Comet
significance: Established January 1986 in Nerima, Tokyo. Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai, Kirarin Revolution, Future GPX Cyber Formula, Whistle!, A Salad Bowl of Eccentrics (2024). Known for children's anime and game adaptations.

name: Tezuka Productions
significance: Founded by Osamu Tezuka to manage his IP and continue animation. Astro Boy (1980, 2003), Black Jack, Phoenix. Manages all Tezuka works licensing (publishing, animation, toys, games). Headquartered in Shinjuku with animation studio in Niiza, Saitama.

name: Shin-Ei Animation
significance: Founded by Daikichirō Kusube (ex-Toei). TV Asahi subsidiary since 2010. Doraemon (1979-present), Crayon Shin-chan (1992-present). Produces most Fujiko Fujio adaptations. Ghost Cat Anzu (2024, Annecy Paul Grimault Award), Totto-chan (2023). HQ in Nishitokyo.

name: Artland
significance: Japanese animation studio founded in 1978 by Noboru Ishiguro, renowned director of Space Battleship Yamato. Notable productions include Legend of the Galactic Heroes (1988–1997 OVA, widely regarded as one of the greatest anime ever made), Mushishi (2005, award-winning), Macross: Do You Remember Love? (1984, co-production), and Katekyo Hitman Reborn! (2006–2010). Became a Marvelous subsidiary in 2006. Filed for bankruptcy in July 2017.

name: Group TAC
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by ex-Mushi Production staff including director Gisaburo Sugii. Notable productions include Touch (1985–1987), Night on the Galactic Railroad (1985, directed by Sugii), Street Fighter II V (1995), and numerous other anime adaptations. Originally started as a sound production firm before expanding to full animation production. Filed for bankruptcy in September 2010 with approximately ¥585 million in debt. Studio Diomedéa was later formed by former Group TAC staff.

name: Tatsunoko Production
significance: Pioneering studio founded by Yoshida brothers. Speed Racer/Mach GoGoGo (1967), Gatchaman/Battle of the Planets (1972), Casshan, Time Bokan series. Name means 'Tatsu's child' and 'sea dragon' (hence seahorse logo). Major influence on international anime fandom.

name: Studio Chizu
significance: Mamoru Hosoda's studio, co-founded with producer Yuichiro Saito. Wolf Children (2012), The Boy and the Beast (2015), Mirai (2018, Oscar-nominated), Belle (2021, highest-grossing Hosoda film), Scarlet (2025). Three Japan Academy Prize wins. Logo references Girl Who Leapt Through Time.

name: OLM
significance: Oriental Light and Magic, best known for Pokémon franchise (1997-present, 1,200+ episodes). Also animated Berserk (1997), Komi Can't Communicate, Beyblade series. IMAGICA Group subsidiary since 2016. Multiple subsidiaries including OLM Digital and OLM Asia (Malaysia, 2017).

name: Gonzo
significance: Pioneer of digital/CG anime integration. Hellsing (2001), Last Exile (2003), Full Metal Panic!, Gankutsuou, Welcome to the N.H.K., Blue Submarine No. 6, Afro Samurai. Name means 'ruffian' in Italian. Merged with Digimation 1999; faced financial troubles 2008-2009, now smaller operation.

name: Manglobe
significance: Japanese animation studio founded in 2002 by ex-Sunrise producers Shinichirō Kobayashi and Takashi Kochiyama. Known for a distinctive cinematic visual style and mature storytelling. Notable productions include Samurai Champloo (2004, directed by Shinichirō Watanabe), Ergo Proxy (2006), Deadman Wonderland (2011), The World God Only Knows (2010–2013), Gangsta. (2015), and Samurai Flamenco (2013). Filed for bankruptcy in October 2015 with approximately ¥350 million ($2.36M USD) in debt. The studio's closure during production of Gangsta. left the series incomplete.

name: Toei Animation
significance: One of Japan's oldest and largest studios, Toei Company subsidiary. Dragon Ball franchise (1986-present), One Piece (1,100+ episodes), Sailor Moon, Digimon, PreCure, Slam Dunk. Also contracted for US productions (Transformers, G.I. Joe). HQ in Ohizumi, Nerima, Tokyo.

name: P.A. Works
significance: Progressive Animation Works, founded by Kenji Horikawa in Nanto, Toyama (rare non-Tokyo HQ). Angel Beats! (2010), Shirobako (anime industry meta-series), Hanasaku Iroha, Charlotte, Canaan, True Tears. Known for beautiful backgrounds and workplace/coming-of-age dramas.

name: C-Station
significance: Established as extension of Bee Train Production, chaired by Ryoji Maru. Best known for Yuru Camp△/Laid-Back Camp (S1-S2, movie), High School Star Musical (Starmyu), Seikoku no Dragonar. Also provides key animation support for major productions.

name: Eight Bit
significance: Founded by ex-Satelight staff. That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime (2018-present), Blue Lock (2022), The Irregular at Magic High School, Yuru Camp S3. Became wholly-owned Bandai Namco Filmworks subsidiary in April 2024. Opened Niigata studio in 2021.

name: Ufotable
significance: Acclaimed for industry-leading digital compositing and action animation. Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba (2019-present, box office record-breaking), Fate franchise (Fate/Zero, UBW, Heaven's Feel). Known for in-house digital pipeline, Ufotable Café merchandise chain. Relocated HQ to Shinjuku Front Tower.

name: Nomad
significance: Japanese animation studio in Suginami, Tokyo, founded by ex-Pierrot staff and Madhouse producer Tatsuya Ono. Known for Megalobox (2018, Crunchyroll Award nominee), Rozen Maiden, Kämpfer, Dropkick on My Devil!!

name: Project No.9
significance: Japanese animation studio known for light novel adaptations. Notable works include The Angel Next Door Spoils Me Rotten (and Season 2 for 2026), Bottom-tier Character Tomozaki, Ro-Kyu-Bu!, and various romantic comedy series.

name: Liden Films
significance: Major Japanese animation studio, Ultra Super Pictures subsidiary (alongside Trigger, Sanzigen, Ordet). ~318 employees across Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka studios. Known for Tokyo Revengers, Rurouni Kenshin (2023), Call of the Night, Heroic Legend of Arslan, Berserk (2016). One of industry's largest independents.

name: Studio Signpost
significance: Japanese animation studio, formerly known as Pierrot Plus. Known for Kingdom anime (Seasons 3-6), My Clueless First Friend, Tokyo Ghoul:re. Maintains connection to parent Studio Pierrot while operating independently on select projects.

name: Pine Jam
significance: Japanese animation studio in Asagaya, Tokyo, founded by ex-Eight Bit producer Kazuyoshi Mukaitouge. Known for Gamers!, Just Because!, Gleipnir, Kageki Shojo!!, 'Tis Time for Torture Princess. Character-driven storytelling with detailed backgrounds.

name: AXsiZ
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by former Studio Gokumi second studio staff. Close partnership with Gokumi on many productions. Known for Pandora in the Crimson Shell, Seiren, Wagamama High Spec. Also provides key animation support for major productions like Attack on Titan and Chainsaw Man.

name: Typhoon Graphics
significance: Japanese animation studio in Tokyo specializing in full production cycle. Known for One Room series, Room Mate, Douse Koishite Shimaunda. Expanded with Maebashi Studio in Gunma (2024). Full-service from planning through compositing and rendering.

name: Studio Blanc
significance: Japanese animation studio in Nerima, Tokyo. ~25 employees. Collaborated with Diomedéa under 'Ezóla' brand (2018-2020). Known for Ayaka: A Story of Bonds and Wounds, support work on various productions. Specializes in animation production assistance.

name: Studio Gokumi
significance: Japanese animation studio established by former Gonzo 5th studio staffers. Known for Kiniro Mosaic, A-Channel, Tsuredure Children, World's End Harem. Frequently collaborates with AXsiZ. Specializes in slice-of-life and comedy anime with cute character designs.

name: Actas
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by ex-Tatsunoko and Ashi Productions staff. Bandai Visual subsidiary since 2017. Iconic for Girls und Panzer franchise, Princess Principal, Transformers: Armada/Energon. Specializes in military-themed and sci-fi anime with detailed mechanical animation.

name: Studio Palette
significance: Japanese animation studio in Suginami, Tokyo with Kobe branch. ~46 employees. Contributed to 100+ projects including Demon Slayer, Attack on Titan Final Season. Primary studio for The World's Finest Assassin and Quality Assurance in Another World.

name: Yostar Pictures
significance: Japanese animation studio, subsidiary of Chinese game publisher Yostar. Founded to produce anime for Yostar games when no other studios would. Known for Arknights series (Prelude to Dawn, Perish in Frost, Rise from Ember), Azur Lane: Slow Ahead!, Blue Archive PVs. Collaboration with ARCH and ALBACROW.

name: Asread
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by ex-Xebec staff. Known for Future Diary (Mirai Nikki), Shuffle!, Corpse Party, Big Order. Specializes in thriller and survival game adaptations. Notable for Yuno Gasai's iconic yandere character.

name: Seven Arcs
