significance: Japanese animation studio, TBS Holdings subsidiary since 2018. Received ¥2.5 billion investment in 2022. Iconic for Magical Girl Lyrical Nanoha franchise, Dog Days, Trinity Seven, TONIKAWA. Founded by former Pierrot staff. Merged with Seven Arcs Pictures in 2019.

name: Studio Flad
significance: Japanese animation studio founded July 3, 2013 in Suginami, Tokyo. Known for Banished From the Hero's Party (2021-2023) and Alma-chan Wants to Be a Family! (2025). Previously provided in-between animation and production assistance for series including Aikatsu Stars!, A3!, and various isekai adaptations.

name: Anima
significance: Japanese 3DCG animation studio (株式会社アニマ, ANIMA Inc.) established October 1997, headquartered in Takadanobaba, Shinjuku, Tokyo. Founded by Shinya Sasahara. Approximately 148 employees as of April 2025. Netflix production partner known for Altered Carbon: Resleeved (2020). Specializes in stylized 3D animation including Japanese anime aesthetic rendered in 3D, game cinematics, VFX for music videos, and original content. Has worked with Nintendo on Fire Emblem cutscenes and trailers. Contributed to Star Wars: Visions (2021). Also operates Chinese subsidiary Anima & Foraise (Dalian) Technology Co., Ltd. One of Japan's leading independent CG studios with expertise across film, games, and commercial animation.

name: Marza Animation Planet
significance: CG animation studio, subsidiary of Sega Sammy Holdings. Known for Lupin III: The First (with TMS), Captain Harlock 3D, Sonic the Hedgehog films VFX. Originally VE Institute, renamed in 2011. Expertise in high-end 3DCG feature films.

name: Sublimation
significance: CG animation studio spun off from Production I.G's CG team. Pioneered cel-shaded 3DCG anime. Netflix partner since 2019. Known for Dragon's Dogma, Shikizakura, Onimusha. Provided CG work for Love Live! and Mobile Suit Gundam Hathaway. Studios in Tokyo, Nagoya, and Sendai.

name: NAZ
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by producer Yasuo Suda. Pioneered innovative 'Guild System' for in-house production. Netflix partner. Known for ID:INVADED (Newtype Award winner), Hamatora, Thermae Romae Novae, Good Night World. Multiple Netflix top 5 chart placements.

name: Studio VOLN
significance: Japanese animation studio in Suginami, Tokyo, founded by ex-Madhouse producer Keiji Mita. Name means 'Visiting Old, Learn New'. Known for Ushio & Tora (co-production with MAPPA), I Want to Eat Your Pancreas film, and Blue Exorcist later seasons.

name: Polygon Pictures
significance: One of the world's oldest digital animation studios. Pioneers in CG anime with ~500 staff across Tokyo, Malaysia, and India. Known for Knights of Sidonia, Ajin: Demi-Human, Blame!, Transformers Prime, and Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man. Strong partnerships with Netflix and Disney.

name: Sanzigen
significance: Japanese 3DCG animation studio specializing in cel-shaded anime. Known for BanG Dream! franchise (seasons 2-3, films), Arpeggio of Blue Steel, and New Initial D films. Also provided CG work for Promare (Studio Trigger). Established 'Nichigaline' production brand.

name: Graphinica
significance: Japanese CG animation studio known for cel-shaded 3D anime films. Produced Hello World (2019), Expelled from Paradise (2014, screenplay by Gen Urobuchi), and Record of Ragnarok. Also worked on Hellsing Ultimate episodes 8-10 and Tokyo Mew Mew New.

name: Studio 3Hz
significance: Japanese animation studio founded in 2013 by Yuuichirou Matsuya and Hideaki Kubo in Tokyo. Known for visually inventive originals: Flip Flappers (2016), Princess Principal (2017), Sword Art Online Alternative: Gun Gale Online (2018), and Heavenly Delusion (2023). Planning and production transferred to A-1 Pictures in 2024; studio ceased independent operations.

name: Troyca
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by ex-AIC producer Toshiyuki Nagano, director Ei Aoki (Fate/Zero), and compositor Tomonori Katou. Debuted with Aldnoah.Zero (2014). Known for Re:Creators, IDOLiSH7 (ongoing franchise), and Bloom Into You. Name derives from Russian 'troika' (team of three).

name: Orange
significance: Japanese CG animation studio in Tokyo specializing in 3D anime. Breakthrough with Land of the Lustrous (2017), praised for expressive CG character animation. Also produced Beastars (2019-2024), Godzilla Singular Point (2021), and Trigun Stampede (2023). Known for pioneering high-quality anime CG that rivals hand-drawn.

name: Doga Kobo
significance: Japanese animation studio acquired by Kadokawa in 2024. Known for slice-of-life and comedy series including New Game!, Yuru Yuri, Monthly Girls' Nozaki-kun, Plastic Memories, Gabriel Dropout, and Oshi no Ko. Renowned for expressive character animation and comedic timing.

name: Kinema Citrus
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by former Production I.G and Bones staff in Suginami, Tokyo. Known for Made in Abyss, The Rising of the Shield Hero, Barakamon, Revue Starlight, and My Happy Marriage. Kadokawa and Bushiroad each acquired 31.8% stake in 2019.

name: Passione
significance: Japanese animation studio in Suginami, Tokyo, founded by Kazuhiro Saitō (former Studio Fantasia). Known for High School DxD Hero (seasons 4-5), Citrus, Mieruko-chan, Rokka: Braves of the Six Flowers, and Spice and Wolf: Merchant Meets the Wise Wolf (2024 remake).

name: Xebec
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by former Tatsunoko Production animators in Kokubunji, Tokyo. Known for Martian Successor Nadesico, Love Hina, Shaman King, To Love Ru, and Space Battleship Yamato 2199/2202 remakes. Subsidiary of IG Port. Production operations transferred to Sunrise in 2018; formally dissolved 2019.

name: Lerche
significance: Japanese animation studio, subsidiary of Studio Hibari. Known for Assassination Classroom, Danganronpa: The Animation, School-Live!, Asobi Asobase, Classroom of the Elite, and Monster Musume. Versatile studio handling psychological thrillers, comedies, and action series.

name: feel.
significance: Japanese animation studio in Koganei, Tokyo, founded by ex-Studio Pierrot staff. Known for romantic comedies and slice-of-life series. Produced My Teen Romantic Comedy SNAFU (Oregairu) seasons 2-3, Tsuki ga Kirei, Dagashi Kashi, and Hinamatsuri. Noted for emotional storytelling.

name: TNK
significance: Japanese animation studio in Nerima, Tokyo, founded by Nagateru Kato (former Tatsunoko Production producer). Known for controversial School Days adaptation (2007) and High School DxD series. Also produced Hand Maid May and I My Me! Strawberry Eggs.

name: Studio Colorido
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by Hideo Ishida (Fumiko's Confession) and Yojiro Arai. Known for vibrant, emotionally resonant films. Produced Pokémon: Twilight Wings, Burn the Witch (with Studio Colorido), and A Whisker Away for Netflix. Noted for fluid animation and strong character work.

name: Studio Bind
significance: Japanese animation studio established specifically to produce Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation as a long-term, continuous project. Subsidiary of Egg Firm, created to ensure consistent quality across the entire adaptation. Known for exceptionally detailed animation and world-building. Season 3 scheduled for 2026.

name: Pettufilmi Oy
significance: Finnish independent film production company based in Helsinki. Produces documentaries, short films, and animation. Known for artistic and experimental works. Productions include The Easy Writer, Paratiisi, and award-winning short films shown at Tampere Film Festival.

name: Nordisk Film
significance: One of the world's oldest continuously operating film production companies, founded in Copenhagen. Iconic polar bear logo dates to 1907. Now a leading Nordic entertainment company producing films, TV, and games. Distributed Help! I'm a Fish and other animated features. Part of Egmont Group.

name: Dentsu
significance: Japan's largest advertising agency and major media conglomerate. Long-standing involvement in anime production, licensing, and marketing. Established Dentsu Anime Solutions Inc. in 2023 for global anime expansion. Production committee member on numerous anime projects. Recently partnered with DreamWorks Animation for BE@RBRICK animated series.

name: Imagica
significance: Japan's premier post-production company for films, television, and animation. Founded as Japan's first commercial film laboratory in Kyoto. Provides comprehensive services including CG/VFX, color grading, audio mixing, film scanning, restoration, and archiving. Now part of IMAGICA GROUP Inc. with global operations.

name: Swan Film Production
significance: Danish animation production company (CVR 27451551) established November 1, 1984, dissolved March 1, 1999. Produced the landmark animated feature Valhalla (1986), based on Peter Madsen's comic series adapting Norse mythology. At DKK 40 million, it was Denmark's most expensive film ever made at release. Production spanned 1982-1986 with over 100 artists. Co-directed by Peter Madsen and Disney veteran Jeffrey J. Varab. Became a beloved classic of Danish animation featuring Thor and Loki.

name: Central Motion Picture Corporation
significance: Taiwan's largest and most comprehensive film production company, founded by the Kuomintang government. Launched careers of major directors including Ang Lee, Hou Hsiao-hsien, Edward Yang, and Tsai Ming-liang. Produced The Wedding Banquet and Eat Drink Man Woman. Owns studios, post-production facilities, theaters, and a movie theme park.

name: Haoliners Animation League
significance: Major Chinese animation studio based in Shanghai. Owned by Bilibili since 2021. Known for high-quality 2D animation and Chinese-Japanese co-productions. Operates Japanese subsidiary Emon Animation Company in Tokyo. Produced Flavors of Youth (2018) and numerous donghua series.

name: Withstand Film
significance: Award-winning Milan-based creative production company. Produces commercials, branded content, documentaries, short films, and animations. Co-produced The Puppet and the Whale with MIYU Productions and Arte.

name: Palladium
significance: Historic Danish film production and distribution company founded by Swedish entrepreneur Lars Björck. Distributed The Tinderbox (1946), Denmark's first color animated feature. One of Denmark's most influential production companies during the silent film era after Nordisk.

name: Hivemind
significance: Los Angeles-based film and television production company founded by Jason Brown and partners. Built around a philosophy of creative partnership. Known for developing franchises including The Witcher (Netflix) and World of Darkness projects with Paradox Interactive.

name: Lucasfilm
significance: Legendary American film and television production company founded by George Lucas. Produced first animated feature Twice Upon a Time (1983) using innovative 'Lumage' cutout animation. Now owns Lucasfilm Animation (Star Wars: The Clone Wars, etc.). Subsidiary of Walt Disney Studios since 2012.

name: Mother London
significance: Independent global advertising agency founded in London in December 1996 by Mark Waites, Stef Calcraft, Libby Brockhoff, and Robert Saville. While primarily an advertising agency, Mother has produced animated commercials and campaigns for major brands including Orange, Coca-Cola, IKEA, and KFC. Operates offices in London, New York, Los Angeles, Shanghai, Singapore, and Berlin.

name: Telecip
significance: French animation production company founded in 1963 and dissolved in 2014. Now part of Studio TF1. Co-produced René Laloux's Time Masters (1982) with Pannonia Film Studio, and La Linea season 2 with Belokapi. Known for television and film production across multiple genres including animation.

name: Pandora Film
significance: German independent film production and distribution company specializing in art house cinema. Founded in Frankfurt by Karl Baumgartner and Reinhard Brundig. Notable for international co-productions including The Congress (with Ari Folman) and collaborations with directors like Jim Jarmusch and Claire Denis.

name: S.N.D.
significance: Société Nouvelle de Distribution - French production, distribution, and international sales company, subsidiary of Groupe M6. Distributes animation including Asterix films and The Jungle Bunch franchise. One of France's top theatrical distributors with a library of over 1,000 titles.

name: Channel Four
significance: British public broadcaster that pioneered adult animation on UK television. Through its Four-Mations strand (1990-1998), commissioned and broadcast hundreds of animated shorts from around the world. Under Clare Kitson's commissioning, championed auteur animation and experimental works.

name: Arte
significance: Franco-German public European culture TV channel headquartered in Strasbourg. Major supporter and co-producer of animation, including experimental and art house animated films. Won Cartoon Tributes Broadcaster of the Year 2024. Key funding source for European animation.

name: Aircraft Pictures
significance: Academy Award and Emmy Award nominated Canadian production company founded 2005 by Anthony Leo and Andrew Rosen in Toronto. Co-produced The Breadwinner (2017, Oscar-nominated) with Cartoon Saloon and Melusine Productions, executive produced by Angelina Jolie. Acquired by Corus Entertainment in 2022. Also produced Holly Hobbie for Hulu and Geek Girl for Netflix. Specializes in scripted content for kids, families, and young adults.

name: Melusine Productions
significance: Luxembourg animation production company founded in 1997 by Stéphan Roelants. In partnership with Studio 352, produced acclaimed animated features including Oscar-nominated 'Song of the Sea' (2014), 'The Breadwinner' (2017), 'Wolfwalkers' (2020) with Cartoon Saloon, plus 'The Summit of the Gods' (2021) and 'Ernest & Celestine' series. Acquired by France's Superprod Group in April 2024.

name: Corona Cinematografica
significance: Italian production company based in Rome that produced documentary films, animated films, and newsreels from the 1960s to 1990s. Notable for international co-productions with Zagreb Film (Yugoslavia) and DEFA (East Germany). Collaborated on Oscar-nominated Tup Tup and other acclaimed animated shorts.

name: Sung Baek-yeop Productions
significance: Independent production entity of director/animator Sung Baek-yeop (born 1960). Best known for Oseam (2003), which won Best Feature Film at the Annecy International Animation Festival 2004. Sung directed, wrote, and produced the film, an adaptation of Jeong Chae-bong's Buddhist fairy tale novel. Also directed White Dog with White Heart (2000).

name: Red Cigarette Media
significance: Independent animation production by Indian filmmaker Ishan Shukla. Created 'Schirkoa: In Lies We Trust' (2024), the first Indian animated feature to premiere at Rotterdam Film Festival. Known for innovative use of Unreal Engine for animation.

name: Experimental Cinema of the Philippines
significance: Government-commissioned animation unit during the Marcos martial law era. Produced 'Tadhana' (1978), the first Philippine full-length animated feature, directed by Nonoy Marcelo with Imee Marcos as producer. A unique case of state-sponsored animation containing hidden social critique.

name: Peter Puluj Productions
significance: Austrian animation production entity of cinematographer Peter Puluj (1930-2017), born in Prague to a family of Ukrainian physicist Ivan Puluj. Collaborated with Czech surrealist animator Jan Švankmajer on films including Picknick mit Weissmann (1968). Puluj's farmhouse studio in Austria provided a creative refuge for Czechoslovak artists during the 1968 Warsaw Pact invasion.

name: Universidad Javeriana
significance: Pontificia Universidad Javeriana, major Colombian private university with a film and television program. Student productions include 'En Agosto' (2008), an early Colombian animated sci-fi short considered a precursor to Latin American genre animation.

name: EDF (Électricité de France)
significance: ⚠️ LOW ANIMATION RELEVANCE — Électricité de France (EDF) is France's national electric utility company. Tangential connection to animation through corporate sponsorship or commissioned animated content. Not an animation studio, production company, or funder in any meaningful sense. Consider removal from archive.

name: Laloux Studio
significance: René Laloux's personal animation studio, founded in 1977 in Angers—France's first dedicated animation studio. Produced 'Les Hommes-machines' (1977), the pilot film that would evolve into 'Gandahar' (1988). The studio operated from 1977-1980 before Laloux moved production abroad. Laloux was renowned for his pioneering work in animated science fiction and innovative cutout animation techniques. He died on March 15, 2004.

name: Fedora Productions
significance: Mexico City-based animation production company founded by Camilla Uboldi and Lucia Cavalchini. Focuses on shorts, series, and features with attention to innovative Latin American voices. Promotes women and LGBTQ+ representation in animation. Develops hybrid projects exploring transmedia, VR, and interactive formats.

name: Instytut Książki (Polish Book Institute)
significance: Polish cultural institution (Instytut Książki) that commissions and produces animated films promoting Polish literature and poetry. Produced VadeMecum (2021), a short by the Quay Brothers showcasing the life and works of Polish poet. Headquarters in Kraków.

name: Philippine Animation Studio Inc. (PASI)
significance: Filipino animation studio established in 1991. One of the oldest studios specializing in traditional animation and Adobe Flash/Toon Boom production. Major service studio for international productions including Seven Little Monsters, Captain Flamingo, Silverwing, and Producing Parker. Part of the PASI Group.

name: PiP Animation Services
significance: Ottawa-based Canadian animation studio founded by Dulcie Clark and Eleanor Noble in 1998. One of the leading Adobe Flash/Toon Boom studios in North America. Notable works include Cyberchase (PBS), Doki (Discovery Kids/Qubo), Wandering Wenda (CBC), and Pirate's Passage (2015).

name: MTV Animation
significance: Animation department of MTV Networks established in the late 1980s. Created animated bumpers and programming for MTV. Known for dark humor, edgy content, and pop culture references. Notable productions include Liquid Television (1991), Beavis and Butt-Head, Daria, and Celebrity Deathmatch.

name: DC Impression Vision
significance: Beijing-based animation studio (北京大呈印象科技发展有限公司). Team founded in 2001, formally established in 2008. Specializes in donghua (Chinese animation) production for web series. Notable works include Forty Millenniums of Cultivation (2022-2023) and other Tencent/Bilibili productions. Won Outstanding Short Film Award at CCGF Digital Image China Festival 2008.

name: Abis Studio
significance: Bucharest-based creative production and post-production house with 30 years of experience. One of Romania's leading production houses covering full-service production to post-production for TV commercials, feature films, corporate films, and music videos. Co-produced The Blissful Accidental Death (2021).

name: Matinee Entertainment
significance: Los Angeles-based animation production company. Co-produced the Malaysian animated series Kampung Boy (1997-1999) with Philippines Animated Studios and Astro, which won a Special Award at Annecy 1999. Director Frank Saperstein performed final edits on the show. Studio appears to have ceased operations circa 2000 after completing Kampung Boy (exact closure date unconfirmed).

name: MountainA
significance: American production company founded by Natalie Portman. Arco (2025) is its first animated project. Co-produced the Cannes-premiering feature with Remembers and France 3 Cinéma.

name: easyAction
significance: Los Angeles-based immersive content studio founded by Ethan Shaftel. Specializes in VR and AR narrative experiences. Produced Gargoyle Doyle (2023), which premiered at Venice Biennale and won Webby Award for Best Narrative Experience.

name: Wait a second!
significance: Berlin-based director-driven animation company founded by producer Karsten Matern together with directors Jalal Maghout, Marta Magnuska, Izabela Plucinska, Veronika Solomon, and Paulina Ziolkowska. Produced Dull Spots of Greenish Colours (2024) by Sasha Svirsky, Grand Prix winner at Animafest Zagreb 2025.

name: Remembers
significance: French animation production company founded by Ugo Bienvenu and Félix de Givry. Produces 2D animation with a focus on auteur features. Co-produced Arco (2025), Bienvenu's feature debut, which premiered at Cannes 2025, is distributed by Neon in the US, and received an Oscar nomination for Best Animated Feature.

name: The Caravel Animation
significance: Italian animation studio led by Gabriele Zucchelli. Produced the documentary Quirino Cristiani: The Mystery of the First Animated Movies, exploring the lost history of the first animated feature film El Apóstol (1917).

name: Part 3 Digital Art Design
significance: Chinese animation production company officially known as Tiangu Digital Art Design (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. (天古数码艺术设计). Produced The Magical Brush (2014), a 3D CGI remake of the classic 1955 Shanghai Animation Film Studio film, with Walt Disney China creative technical support and China Film Group distribution.

name: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation
significance: American arts foundation that financed pioneering animated films. Funded Oskar Fischinger's experimental abstract animation 'Motion Painting No. 1' (1947), a landmark in non-objective art cinema. Also financed 'The Adventures of *' (1957) by John and Faith Hubley, which won the 1957 Venice Film Festival Award for Excellence in Animated Short Subjects. Former Museum Director James Johnson Sweeney collaborated on the Hubley script. While not a production studio, served as crucial patron for avant-garde animation.

name: Culture Platform Co.
significance: South Korean animation production company founded in 2008 as Cinema Platform, expanded in 2011 to Culture Platform. Produces and publishes animation and graphic novels. Works with director Joung Yumi, whose Love Games (2013) won the Grand Prix at Animafest Zagreb—a first for Korean animation. Joung's works have screened at Berlinale, Cannes, and sold TV rights across Europe.

name: Service de la recherche (ORTF)
significance: Experimental art/technology research lab at French public broadcasting (RTF/ORTF), founded by Pierre Schaeffer. Incubated technical and aesthetic research in television, supporting novel animation techniques. Produced works by Robert Lapoujade and Piotr Kamler. Predecessor to Ex Machina.

name: Studio A, Linz
significance: Austrian animation studio based in Linz. Produced Jan Švankmajer's experimental short 'A Game with Stones' (Spiel mit Steinen, 1965). Part of the Austrian avant-garde animation scene. Appears to have been a small or project-based production house; estimated closure circa 1965-1970 (exact date unconfirmed).

name: Greater London Arts Association
significance: British arts funding body active 1966-1996. One of the regional arts associations that funded community arts projects in Greater London. Supported experimental animation and short film projects. Ceased to exist in 1996 when regional arts boards restructured.

name: Reniform Production
significance: Romanian boutique animation and VFX studio founded by Sergiu Negulici. Known for distinctive aesthetic approach to storytelling. Produced The Blissful Accidental Death (2017), which screened at Annecy and Animafest Zagreb.

name: Estúdio Giz
significance: Brazilian audiovisual production company based in Rio de Janeiro. Works on development, production and commercialization of audiovisual projects. Co-produced The Other Shape (2022) with HIERROanimación. Connected to international co-productions including El Auge del Humano 3.

name: Miso Film
significance: Danish production company, now part of Fremantle. Produces feature films and series across multiple genres. Animated work includes Jensen & Jensen (2011). Known for major productions like Max Manus: Man of War and The Bombardment.

name: Climb Films
significance: Pioneering Indian animation studio founded by legendary animator Bhimsain after his debut short The Climb (1970) won the Silver Hugo at Chicago Film Festival. Created iconic works including National Award-winning Ek Anek Aur Ekta and collaborated with National Film Board of Canada.

name: Les Films de l'Arlequin
significance: French animation production company founded in 1991. Remains faithful to its founding mission of producing animated films with distinctive graphic styles. Known for Eye of the Wolf (1998) and other animated features and shorts.

name: HIERROanimación
significance: Colombian animation studio based in Bogotá, specializing in mixed technique animation and IP development. Produced The Other Shape (2022), a dialogue-free dystopian feature that screened at Annecy and won Best Animated Feature at Sitges. Known for educational content, title sequences, and museum films.

name: Culture Entertainment Co.
significance: Japanese entertainment company (Culture Entertainment Co., Ltd. / カルチュア・エンタテインメント) that produced the avant-garde animated film Tamala 2010: A Punk Cat in Space (2002), directed by the two-person art collective t.o.L (trees of Life). The film combined 2D and 3D computer animation in a mostly black-and-white punk aesthetic, premiering at festivals worldwide. Also involved in Tamala's Adventurous Trip and related t.o.L multimedia projects. Part of the broader Culture Entertainment Group.

name: Canino Filmes
significance: Brazilian animation studio specializing in 2D animation and illustration. Known for short films including Plantae (2017), a contemplative environmental piece set in the Amazon.

name: El Gatoverde Producciones
significance: Spanish animation production company founded in 2015, based in Madrid. Produced Sultana's Dream (2023), Oscar-nominated animated short directed by Isabel Herguera. Focuses on artistic and culturally significant animation projects with international festival reach.

name: FAMU
significance: Film and TV School of Academy of Performing Arts in Prague. One of world's oldest film schools. Animation department founded by Jiří Trnka. Alumni include Jan Švankmajer, Jiří Barta. Produced Electra and many acclaimed student films.

name: Bent Barfod Film
significance: Danish animation studio founded in 1956 by Bent Barfod (1920-2007), a leading figure in Danish animation who trained at least two generations of animators over a 50-year career. Known for distinctive haptic style combining puppetry, cutout, and experimental techniques. Inspired by Eastern European animation traditions rather than Disney. Produced Samson & Sally (1984) with Jannik Hastrup. Served as training ground for future A. Film founders including Jørgen Lerdam. Closed following Barfod's death on October 9, 2007.

name: Exformat Films
significance: Thai animation studio. Produced The Legend of Muay Thai: 9 Satra (2018), Thailand's most expensive animated feature at time of release. Represents Thai animation industry's ambitions for international reach.

name: Zero G-Room
significance: Japanese animation studio founded in 1991 by Hiroshi Negishi. Produced M.D. Geist (1986 original, 1996 Director's Cut), cult classic mecha OVA known for violent, post-apocalyptic themes. Merged with Radix in September 2001 to form Radix Ace Entertainment. Negishi later founded Zero-G Inc. in 2011 as a separate successor studio.

name: Aronnax Animation Studios
significance: Peruvian animation studio founded in Lima by Hugo Rose and Abraham Vurnbrand as a joint venture with Televix Entertainment. Produced The Illusionauts (Los Ilusionautas, 2012), Peru's first CGI animated feature film—a Jules Verne-inspired adventure made by a team of ~70 animators. Later co-produced Condorito: The Movie (2017). Pioneering studio in South American CGI animation.

name: Atlantic Releasing Corporation
significance: American independent film distribution and production company active 1978-1989. Produced Starchaser: The Legend of Orin (1985), one of the first animated features released in 3D during the brief 1980s 3D revival.

name: Bibo Films
significance: French animation production company founded in 1993 by animator and director Bibo Bergeron (born Eric Bergeron, 1965), a Gobelins alumnus. Before founding the studio, Bergeron worked on Asterix in Britain (1986) and FernGully (1992). Through the company he co-produced Taxandria (1994), a live-action/animation hybrid directed by Belgian master Raoul Servais. Bergeron later directed The Road to El Dorado (2000) and Shark Tale (2004) at DreamWorks Animation, and returned to France to direct A Monster in Paris (2011).

name: Azeta Pictures
significance: Japanese animation production studio founded in January 1989, headquartered in Nerima, Tokyo. Primarily works as an outsourcing studio providing production assistance and animation for other studios. Credits include Detective Conan, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Space Symphony Maetel: Galaxy Express 999 Side Story (2004-2005), and various TV anime productions.

name: Am Stram Gram
significance: French animation production company run by producer Yves Bouveret. Produced The Night Boots (Les Bottes de la nuit, 2024) directed by Pierre-Luc Granjon using an Alexeïeff-Parker pinscreen named 'The Epinette,' on loan from the French Centre National du Cinéma. The film won the Cristal for a Short Film at Annecy 2025 and qualified for Academy Awards consideration in the Best Animated Short Film category. Specializes in artisanal animation techniques.

name: Are We There Yet? Productions
significance: Australian animation production company founded by Adam Elliot. Produced Memoir of a Snail (2024), winner of the Oscar for Best Animated Feature at the 97th Academy Awards. Previously produced Mary and Max.

name: Anibera Production
significance: Turkish full-service animation studio based in Istanbul, founded in 2014. Specializes in high-quality animation production from concept to completion, offering both 2D and 3D animation services. Produced Evliya Çelebi: The Fountain of Youth (Evliya Çelebi ve Ölümsüzlük Suyu, 2019), one of Turkey's earliest major 3D animated feature films. The studio has 11-50 employees and works on animated feature films, TV series, and commercials. Part of Turkey's growing animation industry.

name: Lightbox Entertainment
significance: Spanish animation studio based in Madrid. Produces CG animated features and series. Works include collaborations on Tad the Lost Explorer franchise. Known for high-quality European CGI animation.

name: Kepler22 Productions
significance: French documentary and film production company founded by Juliette Cazanave and César Díaz. While primarily focused on creative documentaries, Kepler22 has produced and co-produced nearly thirty documentary and fiction films across multiple countries. Pierre Jestaz joined the team in 2016.

name: Manuel Sicilia Productions
significance: Spanish CGI animation company founded by Manuel Sicilia (origins trace to 1992 as Melkor). As Kandor Graphics, produced Goya-winning The Missing Lynx (2008) and Justin and the Knights of Valour (2013) with Antonio Banderas as partner/producer. Sicilia now leads Rokyn Animation in Granada.

name: National Film Board of Canada
significance: Canadian federal government film and digital media producer/distributor. Animation unit founded 1941 by Norman McLaren. World-renowned for experimental animation. 13,000+ productions, 79 Academy Award nominations, 12 wins. Free online archive. Pioneered techniques in direct-on-film, pixilation, and computer animation.

name: Folimage
significance: French animation studio based in Bourg-lès-Valence. Founded by Jacques-Rémy Girerd. Known for nurturing filmmakers with fresh animation approaches. Oscar-nominated for A Cat in Paris (2012). Founded La Poudrière animation school in 1999. Artist-in-residence program for 25+ years.

name: IIDCYA (Kanoon)
significance: Institute for the Intellectual Development of Children and Young Adults, known in Iran as Kanoon (IIDCYA). Founded 1965. Oldest animation studio in Iran. Works in traditional cel, stop motion, and mixed/experimental techniques. Organizes Tehran International Animation Festival. Produced In the Shadow of the Cypress (2025 Oscar winner for Best Animated Short). Also known simply as 'Kanoon.'

name: Flying Bark Productions
significance: Australia's oldest continually operating animation studio, founded in 1967 by Yoram and Sandra Gross as Yoram Gross Film Studios. Went through several name changes: Yoram Gross-Village Roadshow (1996), Yoram Gross-EM.TV (1999), Flying Bark Productions (2007). Now a subsidiary of Belgian company Studio 100. With 500+ employees across studios in Sydney, Los Angeles, and Madrid, it is one of the largest animation studios in Australia. Produces award-winning original feature films and TV series in both 2D and CG animation. Notable productions include Blinky Bill, Maya the Bee: The Movie (2014), 100% Wolf (2020), and the upcoming Avatar: The Last Airbender feature film (partnered with Avatar Studios, 2022). Full-service production facility for both hand-drawn 2D and CG animation.

name: Metafilms
significance: Montreal-based film production company founded in 2003. Produces unusual creators' visions of cinema. 30+ short films, 20+ feature films. Produced Ville Neuve (2018), animated drama using ink on paper animation. Known for supporting exceptional creators in fiction and documentary.

name: Basque Films
significance: Spanish (Basque Country) production and international sales company. Partners with Zircozine on animation projects including Birdboy: The Forgotten Children. Supports Basque filmmakers and international co-productions.

name: Nippon Ramayana Film Co.
significance: Special-purpose Japanese-Indian production company established for Ramayana: The Legend of Prince Rama (1993). Founded by executive producer Matsuo Atsushi of TEM Co. 450 artists worked on production. Pioneering Indo-Japanese animation collaboration. Film hand-drawn using cel animation.

name: Sherman Pictures
significance: Australian production company founded by producer Emile Sherman. Produced the Annie Award Best Animated Feature-nominated stop motion film '$9.99' (2008), Australia's first stop-motion animated feature and first Australian-Israeli co-production. Also produced 'Candy' (2006) starring Heath Ledger and 'Disgrace' (2008, FIPRESCI Prize at Toronto). Sherman later co-founded See-Saw Films in 2008 with Iain Canning, producing Oscar winners 'The King's Speech' (2010) and 'The Power of the Dog' (2021).

name: Lama Films
significance: Israeli animation and film production company. Co-produced $9.99 (2008), a stop-motion animated feature directed by Tatia Rosenthal, based on Etgar Keret's stories. Film premiered at Toronto International Film Festival.

name: California Institute of the Arts
significance: Known as CalArts. Top-ranked US animation school. Character Animation program founded by Disney. Classroom A113 referenced as Easter egg by alumni in countless films. Alumni include John Lasseter, Brad Bird, Tim Burton, Pete Docter, Andrew Stanton, and many animation industry leaders.

name: Dream Well Studio
significance: Independent Latvian animation studio founded by director Gints Zilbalodis. Made history with Flow (2024), which won Latvia's first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature at the 97th Oscars. Also produced Away (2019), which won the Contrechamp award at Annecy. Known for minimalist, dialogue-free storytelling.

name: Arenamedia
significance: Australian production company producing bold, innovative screen content for over 20 years. Led by filmmaker Robert Connolly. Co-produced Memoir of a Snail (2024) with Adam Elliot. Known for compelling, thought-provoking films.

name: GKIDS
significance: Leading independent American animation distributor founded by Eric Beckman. 13+ Academy Award nominations in 15 years. Handles North American distribution for Studio Ghibli library. Distributes international art animation including Boy and the World, Birdboy, and many Oscar-nominated features. Acquired by Toho in 2024.

name: Zircozine
significance: Galician film production company founded in Santiago de Compostela by actor Luis Tosar and Farruco Castromán. Produced Birdboy: The Forgotten Children (Psiconautas, los niños olvidados, 2015), winner of Goya Award for Best Animated Feature. Works frequently with Basque Films on independent animation projects.

name: Melodrama Pictures
significance: Australian claymation studio founded by producer Melanie Coombs and Oscar-winning director Adam Elliot. Won Academy Award for Best Animated Short for Harvie Krumpet (2003). Known for distinctive handcrafted stop-motion style and emotionally resonant storytelling.

name: Atom Art
significance: Award-winning Latvian animation studio established 2001 in Riga by producer Sabine Andersone and director Edmunds Jansons. Produced feature film Jacob, Mimmi and the Talking Dogs (2019), co-produced with Poland's Letko Studio. Works in digital cut-out, traditional drawing, paint-on-glass, sand, charcoal, and puppet animation. Films screened at Berlinale, Annecy, Ottawa, and Hiroshima. Currently developing Born Happy feature.

name: Black White 'n' Green Animation Studio
significance: Serbian animation studio based in Belgrade. Produced Technotise: Edit & I (2009), one of the first Serbian animated feature films and a notable cyberpunk work. Co-produced with Yodi Movie Craftsman.

name: Cinemon Entertainment
significance: Multi award-winning Hungarian animation studio with over 25 years experience. Established reputation for quality kid's animation, television series, commercials and apps. Produced Four Souls of Coyote (2023) and Pelikan Blue.

name: Filme de Papel
significance: Brazilian animation production company founded by director Alê Abreu in São Paulo. Produced Boy and the World (O Menino e o Mundo, 2013), nominated for Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and winner of the Cristal Award at Annecy. Known for highly artistic, mixed-media visual style combining crayon drawings, collage, and digital animation. Abreu began animating at age 13 at the Brazilian Museum of Image and Sound.

name: Łódź Film School
significance: Polish National Film, Television and Theatre School, one of Europe's oldest and most prestigious film schools. Animation department produces approximately 300 student film projects annually. Alumni include many notable animators.

name: Focus Features
significance: American film production and distribution company, subsidiary of Universal Pictures/NBCUniversal. Distributed and co-produced animated films including 9 (2009), Coraline, Kubo and the Two Strings, and The Boxtrolls.

name: Match Cut Inc.
significance: Busan-based South Korean production and distribution company. Produced films including Six Nights (2022), Accidental Travelers (2024), and Math Genius Hyeongju (2024). Status listed as closed (폐업) on KOBIS. Director Yumi Jung served as company representative.

name: Tokyo University of the Arts
significance: First national art university in Japan (also known as Geidai). Animation department is Japan's most prestigious, with faculty including Koji Yamamura. Recognized as Best Animation School at Zagreb World Animation Festival 2010.

name: Marko Gutić Mižimakov (Independent)
significance: Croatian independent animator and filmmaker working in experimental and mixed-media techniques. Director of Dragon Hunt (Lov na zmajice, 2024), a short animated film blending traditional and digital animation methods. Part of Croatia's vibrant independent animation scene, which has produced internationally recognized talent through institutions like the Zagreb School of Animation. Croatia has a rich animation heritage dating to the founding of Zagreb Film in 1953.

name: Payut Ngaokrachang (Independent)
significance: Thai animator known as the 'Father of Thai Animation'. Created Thailand's first animated feature 'The Adventure of Sudsakorn' (1979). Self-funded and independently produced pioneering Thai animated works.

name: Álvaro Henrique Gonçalves (Independent)
significance: Brazilian animator who began creating animation in 1956 and single-handedly produced 'Presente de Natal' (1971), the first color animated feature film made in Brazil. Worked alone in São Paulo for 15 years on this pioneering achievement in Brazilian animation history. Independent animator rather than formal studio.

name: Nicolas Brault (Independent)
significance: Independent animation studio of Quebec animator Nicolas Brault. Won NFB's Cinéaste recherché(e) competition in 2000, launching his career. His film 'The Circus' (2011) was nominated for Best Animated Film at the 37th César Awards. 'Foreign Bodies' (2013) won the Off-Limits Award at Annecy. Known for experimental non-narrative films exploring the human body, entropy, and transformation. Brault has been Professor of Animation at Université Laval since 2019.

name: Quirino Cristiani (Independent)
significance: Argentine-Italian animator, creator of the world's first animated feature film 'El Apóstol' (1917) and 'Sin dejar rastros' (1918). Pioneer of feature-length animation. Most works lost to fires.

name: Nina Paley (Independent)
significance: American cartoonist, animator, and free culture activist. Created 'Sita Sings the Blues' (2008) entirely independently, released under Creative Commons. Known for combining multiple animation styles in single works.

name: Marcos Magalhães (Independent)
significance: Brazilian animator and professor. Won Special Jury Prize at 1982 Cannes Film Festival for 'Meow'. Later worked with NFB Canada on 'Animando'. Pioneer of Brazilian independent animation.

name: Gianini-Luzzati
significance: Italian animation collaboration between director Giulio Gianini (1927–2009) and designer Emanuele Luzzati (1921–2007). Created acclaimed cutout animation films set to classical music, earning two Academy Award nominations: La gazza ladra (1964) and Pulcinella (1973). Federico Fellini praised their 'imaginative design, humorous flair, fairy-tale sense and brilliant graphic solutions.' Their Rossiniana trilogy merged theatre, poetry, and illustration into a unique animation style. Also known as Giannini Luzzati Film.

name: Mono Film
significance: Thai film production and distribution company. Produced Thailand's most ambitious animated feature 'The Life of Buddha' (2007), a nearly 5-hour epic based on Theravada Buddhist traditions with a budget of 120 million baht. Considered one of the most accurate animated adaptations of the Buddha's life story.

name: Dansk Farve- og Tegnefilm
significance: Denmark's first animation studio, founded December 5, 1942 by Allan Johnsen in Copenhagen. Produced Denmark's first animated feature film 'Fyrtøjet' (The Tinderbox, 1946), based on Hans Christian Andersen's tale. The studio trained early Danish animators including Kaj Pindal and Bjørn Frank Jensen, who became influential figures in international animation. Ceased operations around 1950 after struggling to finance follow-up projects.

name: Segi Sangsa
significance: Pioneering South Korean animation studio from the 1960s (also known as Century Commercial/세기상사). Produced 'Hong Gil-dong' (1967), Korea's first theatrical animated feature, and 'Golden Iron Man' (1968), Korea's first animated science fiction film. 'Golden Iron Man' was so popular it was exported to Japan. Produced six feature animations between 1967-1971 before giving up animation production after commercial losses. The company continued as a film distributor.

name: Zora Film
significance: Croatian film production company active in the early years of Yugoslav animation. Animator Boris Kolar began his professional career at Zora Film and Duga Film studios in 1952 before joining Zagreb Film. Part of the broader Yugoslav animation scene that gave rise to the Zagreb School.

name: DeeDee Animation Studio
significance: Vietnamese animation studio founded 2017 in Hanoi by Quang Dang. Headquarters in Hanoi with branch in Ho Chi Minh City. Rising star in Asian animation with international clients including 6 Point Harness (USA), Shin-Ei Animation (Japan), JAM Media (Ireland), and M2 Animation (Thailand). Produced animated sequences for Netflix docuseries 'How to Become a Cult Leader' (2023). Won Silver Kite Award 2025. Focuses on Southeast Asian stories with international appeal.

name: Thaumatrope Animation
significance: Philippine animation studio that co-produced RPG Metanoia (2010) with Ambient Media and Star Cinema - the first full-length Philippine animated film presented entirely in 3D CGI. With a budget of ₱100 million, it became the most expensive Philippine animated film to date. Won Third Best Picture, Best Theme Song, and Best Sound Recording at the 2010 Metro Manila Film Festival.

name: Frenkel Brothers
significance: Three Egyptian Jewish brothers—Herschel (1902–1972), Shlomo (1912–2001), and David (1914–1994) Frenkel—who pioneered animated film in Egypt and produced the first animation on African soil in 1936. Self-taught animators who created Mafish Fayda (1936) featuring Mish-Mish Effendi, the first Arab cartoon star. Made over 30 films. Often called the 'Middle Eastern Disney brothers.' Emigrated to France after Israel's declaration of independence.

name: Ambient Media
significance: Philippine entertainment and multimedia company based in Muntinlupa City, founded in 2005. Co-produced RPG Metanoia (2010), the first feature-length Philippine animated film presented entirely in 3D CGI. Specialized in animation, augmented reality, and avatar puppetry for 2D and 3D content. Acquired by Swedish streaming company Mavshack AB in July 2015 and absorbed into its operations. No longer operates as an independent entity.

name: Star Cinema
significance: Major Philippine film production company under ABS-CBN. Co-produced RPG Metanoia (2010), the first full-length Philippine 3D CGI animated film. Primarily a live-action studio but has ventured into animation co-productions.

name: Pajarraco Films
significance: Chilean animation production company co-founded by producers Abraham Vurnbrand and Hugo Rose. Created Condorito: The Movie (2017), the first CGI animated feature based on René 'Pepo' Ríos's iconic Latin American comic strip character. $8 million budget with $8.3 million box office.

name: Krátký Film Praha
significance: Legendary Czech film production company. Origins trace to 1945 when predecessor studios were established; formally reorganized and centralized in 1957 through the Communist regime's restructuring, incorporating the Bratři v triku cartoon studio and Jiří Trnka's puppet studio. Won first prize at Cannes for an animated fairy tale in 1947 (under its predecessor). Created some of Czech animation's most iconic characters including Krtek (the Mole) by Zdeněk Miler, and produced most of the beloved Večerníček (bedtime story) programs still shown nightly on Czech Television. Jiří Trnka, called 'the Walt Disney of Eastern Europe,' was its first artistic director. Also housed newsreel production and scientific/technical film units. Relocated from Prague to Olomouc in 2005. Part of a golden era of Eastern European animation alongside Zagreb Film, Soyuzmultfilm, and Pannónia Film. Also listed as 'Kratky Film Praha' (without diacritics).

name: Zexcs
significance: Japanese animation studio established January 23, 1998 in Koganei, Tokyo by former J.C.Staff producer Tomoko Kawasaki. Known for Sister Princess, Diabolik Lovers, and The Great Passage (Fune wo Amu). Works closely with sister company Feel. Now owned by Fan Media.

name: Lights On
significance: Torino, Italy-based world sales company co-founded by Flavio Armone in 2015. Specializes in quality cinema from emerging international filmmakers. Notable premieres include Red Moon Tide (Berlinale 2020), Love Dog (Locarno 2022), Mammalia (Berlinale 2023), and Dreaming & Dying (Pardo d'oro winner, Locarno 2023).

name: A.P.P.P.
significance: Another Push Pin Planning (pronounced 'A Three P') was a Japanese animation studio founded June 22, 1984 in Suginami, Tokyo. President Kazufumi Nomura started at Mushi Production. Credited for landmark works including Project A-ko, Robot Carnival, and Roujin Z. Dissolved July 31, 2021 after Nomura's death.

name: Climax Studio
significance: Korean production company that expanded into animation through Netflix partnership. Lost in Starlight (2025) is Netflix's first Korean original animated film, directed by Han Ji-won (discovered through her Stonehenge jewelry commercial). Produced with Netflix Animation, the film features voices of Kim Tae-ri and Hong Kyung. Other notable live-action productions include Hellbound, Ballerina, D.P., and Concrete Utopia.

name: BAP - Animation Studio
significance: Portuguese cooperative of animation authors, founded as part of Bando a Parte in 2011, became cooperative in 2013 with 6 founding members. Percebes (2024) is a finalist for Academy Award Best Animated Short Film. Known for 2D animation with digital and watercolor painting techniques.

name: Now OR Never Studio
significance: South Korean animation studio (지금이 아니면 안돼) founded by director Jang Hyung-yun. Selected for Seoul Animation Center's production support project in 2010. Produced the acclaimed feature Satellite Girl and Milk Cow (2014), a fantasy animation voiced by Yoo Ah-in and Jung Yu-mi that screened at international festivals worldwide.

name: Tin House
significance: Created Sky Blue/Wonderful Days (2003), a landmark Korean animation combining 2D, 3D, and miniatures in 'Multi-Type Layer Animation.' Funded by Korean government and Samsung. Despite critical ambition to rival global animation, the film was a commercial disaster, representing Korean animation's defeat by American and Japanese monopoly capitalism.

name: Barletta Productions
significance: Progressive Czech film, commercial and service production company. Produced Living Large (2024), nominated for Best European Film and Best Animated Film at Czech Lion Awards. Works with animation including stop-motion/puppet and 3D animation techniques.

name: Evidencia Films
significance: Colombian film production company founded by director Franco Lolli, focused on daring auteur films with commercial potential. Based in Bogotá. Produced La Perra, an animated short that received Academy Award consideration for Best Animated Short Film. Other notable works include Gente de bien and Litigante.

name: Harvard Film Study Center
significance: ⚠️ LOW ANIMATION RELEVANCE — Harvard Film Study Center (now the Sensory Ethnography Lab) is an academic institution focused on ethnographic and documentary filmmaking, not animation production. While it has supported some experimental film work, its connection to animation is minimal. Consider removal from archive.

name: YHKT Entertainment
significance: Chinese CGI animation studio specializing in science fiction. Known for Ling Cage: Incarnation (2019), an ambitious post-apocalyptic series, and The Three-Body Problem (2022) anime adaptation of Liu Cixin's Hugo Award-winning novel. One of China's leading studios for hard sci-fi animation.

name: B&T Studio
significance: Chinese animation studio known for Big Fish & Begonia (2016), a visually stunning mythological fantasy that took 12 years to complete. Collaborated with Studio Mir (Korea) on animation production. The film became a major commercial success and cultural phenomenon in China, influencing directors Liang Xuan and Zhang Chun who cite Miyazaki, Ang Lee, and The Little Mermaid as inspirations. Key studio in the modern donghua renaissance.

name: HMCH
significance: Chinese animation studio (Beijing Hanmu Chunhua Animation Technology Co., Ltd.) founded in 2012 by animator MTJJ (Zhang Ping). Known for The Legend of Hei franchise, which began as a Flash-animated web series in 2011. The 2019 feature film became a cult favorite internationally for its dynamic action sequences. The Legend of Hei II (2025) achieved the highest Douban rating among Chinese theatrical releases that year.

name: Beijing Film Academy
significance: China's premier film school, training generations of filmmakers and animators. The Youth Film Studio (associated with BFA) has produced notable animated works including Little Soldier Zhang Ga (2005). Many major Chinese animation directors studied at the academy.

name: China United Film Company
significance: Pre-revolutionary Shanghai film company that produced China's first animated feature Princess Iron Fan (1941), directed by the Wan Brothers. A milestone in Asian animation history - the first animated feature made in Asia and only the fourth in the world. The studio's animation division later evolved into Shanghai Animation Film Studio.

name: DAGO Co
significance: Russian film and animation production company founded 1994 in Yaroslavl, directed by Dmitry Yurkov. Produced Alexander Petrov's Academy Award-nominated My Love (2006), a paint-on-glass animated adaptation of Ivan Shmelev's novel. Also produced Petrov's Oscar-nominated Mermaid (1997). The studio supported Petrov's distinctive and labor-intensive oil painting animation technique. Also produces commercials, feature films, and TV series.

name: Globo Rojo Films
significance: Chilean film production company based in Santiago. Produced The Wolf House (La Casa Lobo, 2018) by Cristobal León and Joaquín Cociña, a groundbreaking stop-motion feature that premiered at Berlin Film Festival. Known for supporting bold auteur animation with distinctive artistic vision. Also produced films by José Luis Torres Leiva.

name: Ka-Ching Cartoons
significance: Dutch animation studio in Rotterdam founded in 2007 by Joost van den Bosch and Erik Verkerk, who met at art academy and worked together at Ireland's Cartoon Saloon before returning to the Netherlands. Specializes in 2D animated feature films, TV series, and short films. Known for distinctive hand-drawn style. Has worked on international co-productions and received recognition at festivals including Clermont-Ferrand.

name: Lokiz Films
significance: Spanish animation studio created by director Pablo Berger as a pop-up production house specifically for the Oscar-nominated film Robot Dreams (2023). Originally, the animation was going to be done by Cartoon Saloon, but Berger established Lokiz Films to produce the hand-drawn 2D animated feature in-house. Robot Dreams premiered at Cannes 2023, was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature (2024), and grossed €10.4 million worldwide on a €5 million budget. The film, a dialogue-free adaptation of Sara Varon's graphic novel about a dog and a robot in 1985 New York, was a Spanish-French co-production with Arcadia Motion Pictures, Noodles Production, and Les Films du Worso.

name: Les Films du Worso
significance: French film production company (Les Films du Worso) founded in 2003 by Sylvie Pialat, after 21 years with Maurice Pialat (she co-wrote the screenplay for Police and Van Gogh, and adapted Sous le soleil de Satan, Palme d'Or at Cannes 1987). Has produced approximately 50 feature films, working with international directors including Abderrahmane Sissako, Corneliu Porumboiu, Amos Gitaï, Xavier Beauvois, and Gustave Kervern & Benoît Delépine. Co-produced the Oscar-nominated animated film Robot Dreams (2023). Won Silver Bear at Berlin 2020 for Effacer l'historique. Based in Paris.

name: Animal Tank
significance: Academy Award-nominated Belgian production company and animation studio founded in 2014 by Brecht Van Elslande and Bert Lesaffer in Ghent. Nominated for Oscar and European Film Awards for Beautiful Men (2023). Films have won prizes at Berlinale, Annecy, and Fantoche; selected at IFFR, SXSW, and Clermont-Ferrand. Works sold to ARTE France, Canal+, Canvas, MUBI, and HBO. Known for balancing originality with accessibility and experimental narratives.

name: Cornelius Films
significance: Barcelona-based production company developing fiction, documentary, and animation projects. Co-produced Olivia and the Invisible Earthquake (2025), winner of the Gan Prize at Annecy 2025. Supports committed, personal cinema close to its time. Seven partners combining audiovisual and business expertise.

name: Arcadia Motion Pictures
significance: Spanish film production company based in Barcelona, founded in 2004 by Ibon Cormenzana. Joined by Ignasi Estapé and Ángel Durández in 2008 and executive producer Sandra Tapia in 2019. Has produced over 30 feature films spanning fiction, animation, and documentary. Produced the Academy Award-nominated animated film Robot Dreams (2023) directed by Pablo Berger, which premiered at Cannes. Also produced acclaimed live-action films including The Beasts (As Bestas, 2022) by Rodrigo Sorogoyen, Blancanieves (2012) by Pablo Berger, and Mediterráneo (2021). Known for supporting auteur cinema and promoting emerging European filmmakers with international potential.

name: Noodles Production
significance: French animation production company, one of the three co-producers of the Oscar-nominated Robot Dreams (2023) alongside Arcadia Motion Pictures and Les Films du Worso. Also co-produced with broadcaster collaborations on other animated and live-action features. Based in Paris, France. Part of the growing network of French animation co-production houses that work across European borders.

name: Bígaro Films
significance: Spanish audiovisual production company founded 2011 in Valencia. Co-produces animation projects including stop-motion feature Olivia and the Invisible Earthquake with Citoplasmas Stop Motion and Cornelius Films. Also produced award-winning short Umbrellas (2020).

name: Televix Entertainment
significance: American entertainment distribution company founded in 1990. Licenses and distributes anime and animated series in Latin America and Brazil. Representative of Viz Media in Latin America.

name: Les Productions de Milou
significance: French animation production company founded by Annemie Degryse (co-founder of Lunanime). Co-produced award-winning shorts including The Miracle (2024, Animafest Zagreb Grand Prix winner). Works with Belgian and Dutch partners on European co-productions.

name: Letko Studio
significance: Polish 2D animation studio based in Warsaw, founded by Jakub Karwowski. Specializes in meaningful storytelling and expressive 2D animation. Produced the acclaimed preschool series Odo and multiple feature films.

name: Protos Film
significance: Montenegrin production company founded by producer Miljan Vučelić. Dedicated to working with young authors. Produces short fiction, animated and documentary films. Has a studio for VFX and 3D animation. Aims to raise quality of film production in Montenegro through regional collaboration.

name: Trẻ Studio
significance: Vietnamese production company officially established March 1, 1991, under the Ho Chi Minh City Youth Union (Thành Đoàn TP.HCM). Originally the Youth Union Film Project. Produces animated and documentary films. Key partner in Con Rồng Cháu Tiên (2017) animated short about Vietnamese origin mythology, alongside RedCat Motion and Redder Advertising. Celebrated 33 years of operation in 2024.

name: Istanbul State Fine Arts Academy
significance: Now known as Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University. Founded January 1, 1882 by Osman Hamdi Bey as Turkey's first Western-style art academy. Became the State Academy of Fine Arts in 1928 (first academy in Turkey), then Istanbul State Fine Arts Academy in 1969 with administrative autonomy. Has a Cartoon and Animation Department training new generations of Turkish animators. As the oldest and most prestigious art institution in Turkey, it has shaped the country's animation and visual arts education.

name: Bionaut
significance: Award-winning Czech film and television production company founded in 1999 by Vratislav Šlajer in Prague. One of the top Czech production companies in terms of output and turnover. Produces fiction, documentary, and animated films and TV series. In 2015, expanded with three specialized labels: Bionaut Animation, Bionaut Docs, and Bionaut Dark (English-language genre films). Has its own animation studio Kredenc for independent design, development and production. Won an International Emmy for the TV series #martyisdead (2020), the first Czech series to win the award. Subsidiary companies in Poland (Kosmonaut), Slovakia (Raketa), and Serbia (Aeronaut). Bionaut Works provides service production and co-production support across Central Europe.

name: Scythia Films
significance: Leading Canadian independent production company founded by Daniel Bekerman, with offices in Toronto, Vancouver, Winnipeg, Los Angeles, and London. Primarily produces live-action features but has expanded into animation. Produced The Witch (2015 Sundance Best Director winner), The Apprentice (2024, Oscar nominations), and animated film Endless Cookie (Sundance 2025 premiere). Known for supporting bold auteur projects.

name: Redder Advertising
significance: Vietnamese advertising agency founded in Ho Chi Minh City, now part of Dentsu as Dentsu Redder. Known for award-winning creative advertising campaigns. Frequently collaborates with Red Cat Motion on animated content. Multiple wins at MMA Smarties, PR Asia Awards, and YouTube Works Awards. Creative Agency of the Year in Vietnam 2019.

name: RedCat Motion
significance: Leading Vietnamese animation studio founded by director Leo Dinh. Pioneer in Vietnam's animation industry, creating TVCs, animated shorts, and music videos. Known for 2D animation, 3D animation, and motion graphics. Clients include Vinamilk, Biti's, and international brands. Leo Dinh is also known for Vietnamese animated films Con Rong Chau Tien and U Linh Tich Ky.

name: Keplerfilm
significance: Dutch film production company founded in 2016 by producers Derk-Jan Warrink and Koji Nelissen in Amsterdam. Focuses on feature films telling compelling, intelligent stories about real people. While primarily a live-action production company rather than an animation studio, Keplerfilm works across genres including drama, thriller, and documentary. Has produced internationally recognized Dutch features.

name: Japan Home Video
significance: Japanese production and distribution company founded May 9, 1984, based in Nakano, Tokyo. Known as JHV, the company played a significant role in the 1980s OVA boom, producing and distributing original video animations. Produced cult classics including Demon City Shinjuku (1988) and Cyber City Oedo 808 (1990-1991) in partnership with Madhouse. Also distributed adult anime content. Contributed to the diversification of anime beyond mainstream broadcast television during the unregulated VHS era.

name: Toho Animation
significance: Toho's animation division established in 2012. Produces and distributes major anime including My Hero Academia and Jujutsu Kaisen. Major player in modern anime industry as both producer and distributor.

name: Bandai Visual
significance: Japanese anime production and distribution company founded August 23, 1983 as AE Planning, later renamed Bandai Visual. Subsidiary of Bandai (later Bandai Namco). Distributed under the Emotion label. Produced and distributed major anime including Cowboy Bebop, many Gundam series, and works from Sunrise studio. Merged with Lantis to form Bandai Namco Arts in April 2018.

name: Shochiku
significance: One of Japan's oldest entertainment companies, founded in 1895 as a kabuki theater company. Entered film production in 1920 with Kamata Film Studio. Considered one of Japan's Big Four film studios and the oldest among them. Animation section established 1943. Produced the first Japanese talking motion picture (1931) and first color film in Japan (1951).

name: Tokyo Broadcasting System
significance: Major Japanese broadcasting network founded in 1955. Produces and broadcasts anime including Jujutsu Kaisen and My Hero Academia. Acquired anime studio Seven Arcs in 2017.

name: Molot Entertainment
significance: Russian animation production company. Co-produced First Squad: The Moment of Truth (2009) with Japan's Studio 4°C—a groundbreaking Russian-Japanese anime collaboration set during WWII. The film won the Kommersant newspaper prize.

name: NHK
significance: Japan's public broadcaster (Nippon Hōsō Kyōkai), reorganized in 1950 from the original 1926 state corporation. While primarily a broadcaster rather than animation studio, NHK has commissioned and co-produced numerous significant anime series including Conan the Boy in Future, Future Boy Conan, Cardcaptor Sakura, and collaborated with Studio Ghibli on documentaries like 10 Years with Hayao Miyazaki. NHK Educational TV broadcasts children's animation.

name: Dandelion Animation Studio
significance: Japanese CG animation planning and production company headquartered in Nerima, Tokyo. Works across animation, games, and branding. Notable for Pokétoon shorts and collaboration on various anime productions. Employs 51-200 people.

name: Project Team Argos
significance: Japanese animation production collective conceived by Madhouse founders Masao Maruyama and Rintarō. Co-produced Neo Tokyo (Meikyū Monogatari, 1987) with Madhouse, an influential sci-fi anthology featuring segments by Rintarō, Yoshiaki Kawajiri, and Katsuhiro Otomo. Also involved in Patlabor 3: WXIII (2002), their final production. Operated as a project-based collective rather than a permanent studio.

name: Mattel Creations
significance: Television and animation production division of American toy company Mattel, formed on March 31, 2016 as Mattel Creations to centralize content creation across global brands. Rebranded as Mattel Television in 2019. Produces animated and live-action series for Barbie, Hot Wheels, Monster High, Masters of the Universe, and other franchises. Merged with Mattel Films to form Mattel Studios in 2025.

name: Blur Studio
significance: Award-winning CG animation studio in Los Angeles, founded by Tim Miller. Oscar-nominated for short film Gopher Broke (2004). Produces game cinematics for major clients including Riot Games and Activision. Created thirteen-time Emmy-winning Netflix series Love, Death + Robots and Prime Video's Secret Level.

name: Hasbro Studios
significance: Hasbro's in-house television production studio, established 2009 in Burbank, California by CEO Brian Goldner to bring content creation in-house. Produced animated series based on Hasbro toy lines including My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic (2010–2019), Transformers: Prime, Littlest Pet Shop, and Pound Puppies. In 2017, rebranded as Allspark Animation as part of Hasbro's reorganization of entertainment assets. The Allspark division encompassed Allspark Animation (TV production) and Allspark Pictures (film). Continued producing Transformers: Cyberverse, Rescue Bots Academy, and the final season of My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic under the Allspark name. In December 2019, Hasbro completed its $3.8 billion acquisition of Entertainment One (eOne) and merged Allspark into eOne Family & Brands, effectively ending the Allspark name by 2020. Content production for Hasbro brands continues under the eOne/Hasbro Entertainment umbrella.

name: Marvel Animation
significance: Marvel's animation division has evolved through multiple eras: Marvel Productions (1980s-1993), New World Animation (1993-1996), Marvel Films Animation (1994-1996, producing Spider-Man: The Animated Series), and currently Marvel Studios Animation (since 2021). The 1990s X-Men: The Animated Series (1992-1997, produced by Saban) ran 76 episodes as the longest Marvel animated series. Current Marvel Studios Animation produces What If...?, X-Men '97, Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man, and I Am Groot for Disney+.

name: Adult Swim
significance: Adult-oriented programming block on Cartoon Network, launched September 2, 2001. Pioneered experimental, transgressive, and surrealist adult animation. Home to Space Ghost Coast to Coast, Aqua Teen Hunger Force, The Venture Bros., Rick and Morty, and many creator-driven series. Known for lo-fi aesthetics born from budget constraints and supporting unique artistic visions.

name: Allspark Animation
significance: Hasbro Studios rebranded as Allspark in 2017 as part of Hasbro's reorganization of entertainment assets. The Allspark division encompassed Allspark Animation (TV production) and Allspark Pictures (film). Continued producing animated series based on Hasbro brands including Transformers: Cyberverse, Rescue Bots Academy, and the final season of My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic. In December 2019, Hasbro completed its $3.8 billion acquisition of Entertainment One (eOne) and merged Allspark into eOne Family & Brands, effectively ending the Allspark name by 2020. See also: Hasbro Studios entry (covers the 2009-2017 period). ⚠️ OVERLAPPING ENTRY — Consider merging with 'Hasbro Studios' as they represent the same entity at different time periods.

name: Scholastic Entertainment
significance: American entertainment company and subsidiary of Scholastic Corporation. Produces family-oriented animated and live-action content based on Scholastic books. Notable productions include Clifford the Big Red Dog for PBS Kids and Amazon Prime, and Peabody and Daytime Emmy Award-winning Stillwater for Apple TV+. Partners with major studios to bring children's literature to screen.

name: Williams Street
significance: Founded in 1994 as Ghost Planet Industries, renamed Williams Street in 1998. In-house production arm of Adult Swim. Created Aqua Teen Hunger Force, The Venture Bros., and Rick and Morty. Pioneered adult animation on cable TV.

name: Legendary Television
significance: Television division of Legendary Entertainment, the American mass media and film production company founded by Thomas Tull in 2000 in Burbank, California. Legendary Television was established in 2011 to develop television productions. The parent company is known for major franchise properties including the MonsterVerse (Godzilla, Kong), Pacific Rim, and Dune. Has co-produced animated and live-action content for major streaming platforms including Netflix and Hulu. Legendary was acquired by China's Wanda Group in 2016; in 2024, Legendary bought out Wanda's stake.

name: Rooster Teeth
significance: Founded in 2003 by Burnie Burns and colleagues in Austin, Texas. Pioneered web-based entertainment and machinima with Red vs. Blue (2003), the longest-running web series in history. Created RWBY (2013), one of the first American anime-style productions. Subsidiary of Warner Bros. Discovery before closure in 2024. Revolutionary in building direct audience relationships through online content.

name: Gaumont Animation
significance: French animation studio owned by Gaumont, founded February 1997 by Christian Davin as Alphanim. Renamed Gaumont Alphanim after Gaumont acquisition in 2007, then Gaumont Animation in 2013. Catalog comprises over 800 half-hours broadcast in 130+ countries. Terry Kalagian promoted to president in 2023. Signed first-look deal with Studio 100.

name: Pumpkin 3D
significance: French CGI animation studio founded in Paris by Pascal Chevé and Louis Viau. Worked on major productions including Oban Star-Racers (TV), Azur et Asmar (2006), and Persepolis (2007). Specializes in computer animation for international co-productions.

name: Take Five
significance: Belgian film production company based in Brussels. Co-produced Flow (2024) with Dream Well and Sacrebleu Productions, which won the Oscar, César, and Golden Globe for Best Animated Feature. Established Carbone 14 animation studio.

name: Doghouse Films
significance: Animation production company founded in 2012 in Luxembourg by Pierre Urbain and David Mouraire, in partnership with Belgian producer Walking The Dog. Combines founders' experience from various animation and fiction production companies. Focuses on high-quality 2D and 3D animation projects, developing original content from new talents. Part of Luxembourg's growing animation industry.

name: Perseprod
significance: French animation production structure created by Marjane Satrapi specifically for Persepolis (2007). Rather than use an existing studio, Satrapi rented space in Paris's 10th arrondissement and hired 100+ animators. Worked alongside Je Suis Bien Content and Pumpkin 3D to create the distinctive black-and-white animation style of the Oscar-nominated film.

name: Dolce Vita Films
significance: French film production company founded in Paris in January 2007 by Marc Irmer. Produces fiction and documentary films with interest in international co-productions. Co-produced Chicken for Linda! (2023), winner of the Cristal Award at Annecy for Best Feature Film. Supports new French directors transitioning from documentaries to features.

name: New Deer
significance: Japanese animation production and distribution company founded by Nobuaki Doi in Tokyo. Specializes in connecting independent animated films from around the world with Japanese audiences and facilitating international co-productions, primarily with France. Doi is also Festival Director of New Chitose Airport International Animation Festival and Producer of Hiroshima Animation Season.

name: Palosanto Films
significance: Italian film production company founded by Pilar Saavedra Perrotta in Rome (originally as Moliwood Films). Produces international co-productions with European and non-European partners. Sister company to Sajama Films. Works primarily with established auteur directors on arthouse features.

name: Ecce Films
significance: French film production company based in Paris, focused on author-driven short and feature films. Produced over 120 films including animated works. Known for supporting emerging filmmakers and diverse genres spanning fiction, documentary, and animation. Works by directors including Momoko Seto and Justine Triet.

name: Cinéma Defacto
significance: French author-driven production company (Cinéma Defacto) founded in 2007 and based in Paris. Has produced around 40 completed features across fiction and animation. Animation credits include Blind Willow, Sleeping Woman (directed by Pierre Földes, based on Haruki Murakami short stories), which premiered at Annecy and screened at major international festivals. Works with international filmmakers across genres. Part of the vibrant Parisian independent film production scene.

name: Le Ciel de Paris
significance: French independent production company based in Aquitaine. Produces commercials with various directors across comedy, beauty, motion design, food content, and animation. Expanded into TV series production with 'Mily Miss Questions' and develops innovative projects for the international market. Also known as Ciel de Paris / Cake Films.

name: Magic Light Pictures
significance: UK-based production company founded in 2008 by Martin Pope and Michael Rose, specializing in high-quality animated specials adapting beloved children's books. Oscar-nominated for The Gruffalo (2009), produced in partnership with Studio Soi. Known for adaptations of Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler books including The Gruffalo's Child (2011), Room on the Broom (2012), Stick Man (2015), Zog (2018), and The Snail and the Whale (2019). BAFTA-winning company celebrating 20+ years of quality animation.

name: Film Four International
significance: Original name of Film4 Productions, the feature film division of Channel 4 Television Corporation. Renamed Channel Four Films in 1995, then FilmFour, now Film4 Productions. Co-finances films from UK and international filmmakers. Productions have won 43 Oscars and 97 BAFTAs since inception.

name: Dog Ears
significance: Award-winning Irish animation studio based in Derry, Northern Ireland. Co-created Emmy-nominated preschool series Puffin Rock with Cartoon Saloon and Penguin Random House—known for its beautiful low-stimulation stories. Co-produced Puffin Rock and the New Friends (2023), the first animated film produced in Northern Ireland. Also created Saturday Club for Hopster. Specializes in pre-production, original IP development, and UK Animation tax break expertise.

name: Lupus Films
significance: London-based studio founded in 2002 by Camilla Deakin and Ruth Fielding. Multi-BAFTA-nominated and Emmy Award-winning producer of high-quality family entertainment. Known for beautifully hand-crafted adaptations including The Snowman and the Snowdog (2012), We're Going on a Bear Hunt (2016), Ethel & Ernest (2016), The Tiger Who Came to Tea (2019), and Kensuke's Kingdom. Specializes in traditional 2D animation with hand-painted backgrounds.

name: Cake Entertainment
significance: British entertainment company specializing in production, distribution, development, and brand development of kids' and family properties. Founded by Genevieve Dexter. Acquired by Zinkia Entertainment in 2011, bought itself back in 2014, and acquired Animation Collective in 2018. Award-winning company with shows broadcast in over 125 countries.

name: Apple Films
significance: Film production division of Apple Corps Ltd, The Beatles' multimedia corporation formally incorporated on January 22, 1968. Produced the groundbreaking animated film Yellow Submarine (1968), a landmark in psychedelic pop-art animation directed by George Dunning at TVC London with art direction by Heinz Edelmann. The film's surreal visual style — combining pop art, psychedelia, Art Nouveau, and op art — influenced generations of animators and designers. Also produced Let It Be (1970), The Beatles Anthology (1995) documentary series, and the restored Yellow Submarine re-release (2012). Apple Corps remains active today managing The Beatles' legacy, music catalogue, and licensing.

name: Glasgow School of Art
significance: Historic Scottish art school founded in 1845. Animation program has produced notable independent animators. Norman McLaren studied at Glasgow before his pioneering work at the GPO Film Unit and NFB. The school continues to train animators in experimental and traditional techniques.

name: Condor Films
significance: Swiss film and TV production company based in Zürich since 1972 at Bellerive Studios. Produces commercials, documentaries, and feature films. Co-produced surrealist animated film Alice (1988) by Jan Švankmajer. In 2020, Hans Syz acquired majority stake to expand into premium features and arthouse projects.

name: Illuminations Films
significance: British independent production company founded in 1982 by Welsh producer Keith Griffiths alongside Channel 4's launch. Specializes in original and imaginative features, shorts, installations and multi-platform projects. Has produced work by innovative directors including the Brothers Quay, Patrick Keiller, Chris Petit, and Czech animator Jan Švankmajer. Also produced Peter Strickland's Berberian Sound Studio (2012). Known for bringing auteur animation and experimental filmmaking to British screens.

name: Yoram Gross Film Studios
significance: Australian animation studio founded by Polish-born Yoram and Sandra Gross in 1968 in Sydney. Pioneered the trademark technique of animating over live-action backgrounds. Known for Dot and the Kangaroo (1977), Blinky Bill, and many beloved Australian animated features. In 2006, EM.Entertainment acquired full ownership and rebranded the studio as Flying Bark Productions, which was later acquired by Studio 100.

name: Nepenthe Productions
significance: British-American production company founded in 1975 by Martin Rosen specifically to produce Watership Down.
