Produced the acclaimed animated adaptations of Richard Adams' novels: Watership Down (1978) and The Plague Dogs (1982), both directed by Rosen. Known for their mature, emotionally complex approach to animated storytelling with unflinching depictions of nature's brutality.

name: Murakami-Wolf Productions
significance: American animation studio founded in 1967 by animators Fred Wolf and Jimmy T. Murakami. Won the Academy Award for Best Animated Short for 'The Box' (1968). Became Murakami-Wolf-Swenson in 1978 when Charles Swenson joined. Produced Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (1987), one of the most successful animated series of its era. Established Dublin studio in 1989, helping launch the Irish animation industry. Renamed Fred Wolf Films in 1992.

name: Ted Nemeth Studios
significance: New York-based studio founded in 1940 by Ted Nemeth (1911-1986), an early animation pioneer and cinematographer. Collaborated with Mary Ellen Bute on pioneering abstract animated films including Spook Sport (1940) and Color Rhapsodie (1948). Made documentaries, commercials, and short subjects, two of which were Academy Award nominees. Nemeth later worked with Jim Henson as cinematographer on Time Piece (1965). Specialized in special effects and experimental animation.

name: Lakeside Animation
significance: Canadian 2D animation studio based in North Bay, Ontario with offices in Toronto. Specializes in developing original content and offering full-spectrum production services. Experienced in international co-production, collaborating with studios worldwide. Recent productions include 'Luz Diabla' (2024, Argentina co-production) and 'Not Safe For Work' adult animated comedy series with Cutting Class Media.

name: Syncopy
significance: British-American film production company founded by director Christopher Nolan and producer Emma Thomas. Based in London and Los Angeles. While primarily live-action, has worked on animated projects. Produced the Dark Knight trilogy, Inception, Interstellar, Dunkirk, Tenet, and Oppenheimer.

name: Square Pictures
significance: Japanese-American CGI animation studio established by Square (now Square Enix) as a subsidiary to produce computer-animated films. Created Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within (2001), the first photorealistic computer-animated feature film, with a budget of $137 million. The film's commercial failure ($85 million box office) led to the studio's closure and absorption into Square's Visual Works division.

name: Korty Films
significance: American independent film production company founded by John Korty (1936-2022) in Mill Valley, California. Korty invented 'Lumage' (Luminous Image), a distinctive cutout animation technique using translucent plastic and felt pieces over backlit light tables. Produced animated inserts for Sesame Street including the Thelma Thumb series. Made Twice Upon a Time (1983) with Lucasfilm, their first animated feature, which employed a young David Fincher on camera and Henry Selick directing sequences. Korty won an Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature.

name: Frogtown Mountain Films
significance: ⚠️ LOW ANIMATION RELEVANCE — Family-owned touring puppetry and theater company based in Bar Harbor, Maine. While puppet-based, this is a live theatrical troupe, not an animation studio or production company. Consider removal from archive.

name: Snoot Entertainment
significance: American film production company founded by producers Keith Calder and Jess Wu Calder. While primarily live-action focused, produced CGI animated feature Battle for Terra (2007) and stop-motion animated feature Anomalisa (2015), the latter receiving an Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Feature. Also produced Adam Wingard films (The Guest, You're Next, Blair Witch).

name: Stout Studio
significance: Belgian animation production company. Co-produced adult animated films with director Picha including The Big Bang (Le Big Bang, 1987), a post-apocalyptic comedy. Part of Belgium's adult animation scene of the 1980s alongside Pils Film and Comedia.

name: Film Boris von Borresholm
significance: German production company founded by Boris von Borresholm (1911-1989), one of the 26 signatories of the historic Oberhausen Manifesto in 1962 that launched New German Cinema. The company produced influential animated shorts by Polish master Jan Lenica including 'A' (1965), 'Die Nashörner/Rhinoceros' (1963, winner of Oberhausen prize), and 'Adam 2' (1968). Also collaborated with Gerhard Fieber on 'Es war einmal' (1957).

name: Trickompany
significance: Founded in 1985 by Michael Schaack. One of Germany's most successful animation studios. Produced Felidae and Pippi Longstocking. Filed for bankruptcy in December 2010.

name: Atmo Media Network
significance: Swedish film production company founded by director Tarik Saleh and producer Kristina Åberg. Produced the dystopian animated feature Metropia (2009), co-produced with Lars von Trier's Zentropa, which premiered at the 66th Venice International Film Festival. Known for unique visual style combining live-action sensibilities with animation.

name: Film i Väst
significance: Scandinavia's leading co-producer and regional film fund based in Trollhättan. Has co-produced over 1,600 films and drama series since 1992. Co-productions have received 18 Oscar nominations since 2017 and been nominated for the Palme d'Or 18 times.

name: Maipo Film
significance: Norwegian production company founded in 2000 by Synnøve Hørsdal. One of Norway's leading production houses for film and drama. Produced the stop-motion puppet animation Solan og Ludvig (Louis & Luca) franchise, beginning with Jul i Flåklypa (Christmas in Pinchcliffe, 2013) — one of the biggest box office hits in Norwegian film history — directed by Rasmus A. Sivertsen. Follow-ups include Solan og Ludvig: Herfra til Flåklypa (2015) and additional sequels. Also produced the 2D animated feature Hocus Pocus, Alfie Atkins (2013), directed by Oscar-winner Torill Kove. Oscar-nominated for Elling (2001, live-action). Over 40 productions since founding. Member of the European Producers Club.

name: Umbrella Entertainment
significance: Australian film production and distribution company founded in 2001. Distributes local and international films on DVD, Blu-ray, and digital platforms. Recently rebranded to Umbrella.

name: Storm Studio
significance: Dutch post-production company based in Amsterdam specializing in VFX, animation, grading, and creative motion for film and advertising. Part of the Netherlands' growing animation and VFX industry.

name: Sasha Svirsky Studio
significance: Berlin-based Russian animator Sasha Svirsky (b. 1980). Known for hand-drawn experimental shorts with absurdist humor. Frequent festival presence at Annecy, Ottawa, and Zagreb.

name: Second Frog Animation Group
significance: Animation collective founded within Pilot studio by Alexander Tatarsky and Valentin Prokhorov. Produced children's series and commercials in post-Soviet Russia.

name: Multtelefilm
significance: Soviet animation division of Studio Ekran, part of the Gosteleradio television network. Served as the creative base for Alexander Tatarsky and Igor Kovalyov, who left to found Pilot, the first private Soviet animation studio, in 1988. Key alumni later emigrated to work at Klasky Csupo in the US, where they created popular series like Rugrats and Aaahh!!! Real Monsters. Ceased operations with the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991.

name: SHAR School-Studio
significance: Russian animation school-studio founded by legendary filmmakers Fyodor Khitruk, Eduard Nazarov, Yuri Norshtein, and Andrey Khrzhanovsky to preserve the 'genetic link between generations' in Russian animation. Provides professional training for directors and animators while producing artistic animated films. Films have won prizes at many international festivals including Annecy. Based in Moscow.

name: Sverdlovsk Film Studio
significance: Major Soviet/Russian regional film studio based in Yekaterinburg (formerly Sverdlovsk), founded during WWII from evacuated filmmakers. Produced over 200 feature films and 500 documentaries. Animation department known for paint-on-glass work by Alexander Petrov (The Cow, 1989) and sand animation by the Petkevich family.

name: Kinemma
significance: Mexican animation studio known as one of the few Mexican anime-influenced studios. Produced works primarily for the domestic market. The studio is no longer in operation.

name: VGIK
significance: The world's oldest film school, founded in 1919. Gerasimov Institute of Cinematography (VGIK) in Moscow. Has an Animation and Multimedia Faculty. Trained generations of Soviet and Russian animators.

name: Rys Studio
significance: Russian animation studio led by artistic director Andrey Murin. Produces auteur animation shorts and has collaborated with veteran animators from the Soyuzmultfilm tradition.

name: Soyuztelefilm
significance: Soviet television film studio founded in 1967. Parent organization of Multtelefilm animation division. Produced TV films and series for Soviet broadcast. Dissolved with the collapse of the USSR in 1991.

name: Pipe Studio
significance: Russian game development studio. Collaborated with animator Ivan Maximov on the point-and-click adventure game Full Pipe (2004), adapting his surrealist animation style into interactive form.

name: Tsuburaya Productions
significance: Founded in 1963 by Eiji Tsuburaya, the 'Father of Tokusatsu.' Created the Ultraman franchise. Pioneered Japanese special effects and tokusatsu genre. Continues producing Ultraman series today.

name: CloverWorks
significance: Japanese anime studio, originally A-1 Pictures' Kōenji Studio, rebranded April 2018 and spun off October 2018 as Aniplex subsidiary. Known for high-quality productions including Spy x Family, Bocchi the Rock!, My Dress-Up Darling, and The Promised Neverland. Co-founded JOEN venture with Wit Studio, Aniplex, and Shueisha in 2022.

name: Studio Tampopo
significance: Japanese independent animation production company founded by producer Sayaka Omodaka. Produced A Night at the Rest Area (2024) directed by Saki Muramoto, which won Zagreb 2025 Special Award, Tribeca 2025 selection, and special jury prizes at Insomnia, Siam International Animation Festival 2025, and Big Cartoon Festival. Works with independent animators on auteur shorts.

name: Studio LICO
significance: South Korean digital content studio, subsidiary of Webtoon/Naver. Creates webtoons, animation, and multimedia content. Known for Return of the Blossoming Blade (Hwasangwihwan) webtoon and Alien Stage animated music video series. Combines illustration, animation, and storytelling across digital platforms.

name: Studio GDS
significance: Swiss independent animation studio founded in 1970 in Geneva by Georges Schwizgebel, Claude Luyet, and Daniel Suter. The studio produced artistic short animations from 'The Flight of Icarus' (1974) to 'Darwin's Notebook' (2020), creating approximately 20 films. Known for Schwizgebel's distinctive painted animation style. Collaborated with the National Film Board of Canada on international co-productions.

name: Studio Dauka
significance: Latvian animation studio founded in 1991 by animator Ansis Bērziņš and director Roze Stiebra in Riga. Latvia's oldest animation studio, best known for the sci-fi series Fantadroms (1985-1995). Built on Soviet-era traditions of Telefilma-Rīga. Focused on hand-drawn animation and narratives from Latvian folklore. Closed in June 2010 due to lack of funding after the National Film Center twice rejected their project applications. Left a significant legacy in Baltic animation with over 125 films.

name: Studio Flying
significance: South Korean animation studio founded in 2006. Part of Korea's extensive network of animation production companies handling subcontracting work for Japanese anime studios as well as original Korean productions.

name: Riblje
significance: Croatian production credit for Fisheye (Riblje oko, 1980), a celebrated animated short by Joško Marušić produced at Zagreb Film. Marušić (born 1952) created this acclaimed work about a monotonous fishing village. Won multiple international awards and represents the Zagreb School's signature 'limited animation' style and focus on films for adults.

name: La Traverse Films
significance: French film production and distribution company. Specializes in both producing and distributing independent and art-house films, with a focus on restored classics. While not exclusively an animation studio, La Traverse has been involved in distributing animated works including films by legendary animators. Based in France, the company also operates a boutique selling DVDs, books, and cinema posters.

name: nutprodukcia
significance: Slovak production company founded by producers Jakub Viktorín, Tomáš Hrubý, and Pavla Janoušková Kubečková. Sister company to Czech-based nutprodukce. Co-produced Agnieszka Holland's Spoor and Sergei Loznitsa's State Funeral. Focuses on synergic Slovak and Czech projects with European market appeal. Active in both fiction and animation, including Tony, Shelly & the Magic Light and Free the Chicken.

name: Pils Film
significance: Belgian animation production company co-founded by director Picha (Jean-Paul Walravens). Produced adult animated comedies including The Missing Link (1980, entered Cannes Film Festival) and The Big Bang (1987). Key studio in Belgian adult animation history.

name: DOK produkcija
significance: One of the few production companies in Montenegro primarily focused on stop-motion animated films. Based in Podgorica. Gathers new generation producers, directors, writers and animators to revive traditional animation techniques. CEO Danilo Vujačić. Produced Uroš (2023), screened at Animafest Zagreb. Part of the emerging animation scene in the Balkans.

name: Lunanime
significance: Belgian animation studio founded in 2008 within the Lumière Group, headquartered in Ghent. Specializes in 2D animation for television series and feature films. In-house animation studio LumièreStudio offers opportunities for young animators. Co-produced acclaimed films including A Cat in Paris (2010, Oscar-nominated), Phantom Boy (2015), and award-winning shorts. Part of the Lumière Benelux group, a strategic partner in financing, co-production, and distribution across the Benelux region.

name: Institut National de l'Audiovisuel
significance: France's national audiovisual institute (INA), founded in 1975, is the world's leading resource for digitized audiovisual content. Its mission is to collect, preserve and share France's radio and television audiovisual heritage. Houses over 20,000 hours of searchable archives online since 2006. While primarily an archive institution rather than a production studio, INA preserves significant French animation history and occasionally supports animation projects.

name: Les Films Outsiders
significance: Canadian film production company based in Montreal. Founded by producers Ginette Petit and Nathalie Bissonnette. Specializes in documentary and dramatic features including And the Birds Rained Down (2019).

name: Studio Zvon
significance: Czech puppet animation studio founded by filmmaker Aurel Klimt in Malešov, continuing traditions established at Studio Jiří Trnka. Focuses on stop-motion and combined techniques. Produced the Czech Lion-winning feature Laika (2017). Also involved in international co-productions including puppet animation for Mozart in China. Capacity of 15 minutes finished animation per year.

name: Parce Que Films
significance: Montreal-based Canadian production company founded around 2004. Produces features and shorts in both animation and fiction. Known for When Adam Changes (Quand Adam change, 2023), directed by Joël Vaudreuil, which won Grand Prize for Best Animated Feature at Ottawa International Animation Festival and was nominated at Annecy.

name: Studio Dadashow
significance: Korean animation studio founded by director Yeon Sang-ho (Train to Busan). Specializes in adult-oriented animation. The King of Pigs (2011) was the first Korean animated film invited to Cannes. Also produced The Fake (2013) and Seoul Station (2016), the animated prequel to Train to Busan.

name: MSV Pictures
significance: Indonesian animation studio based in Yogyakarta, affiliated with AMIKOM University. Produced Battle of Surabaya (2015), a historical animated feature about Indonesia's 1945 independence struggle, which won Best Animation at the 2016 Asia Pacific Screen Awards. One of the largest animation studios in Indonesia.

name: Studio LAN
significance: Chinese animation studio (Shenzhen Lanyinghua Animation Production) founded by animator LAN. One of the top animation studios in China, known for exceptional sakuga and animation direction. Produced Link Click (Shiguang Dailiren), To Be Hero series. Works on both Chinese donghua and subcontracting for Japanese anime including JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, Vinland Saga, and One Punch Man.

name: Chengdu Coco Cartoon
significance: Chinese animation studio originally founded as Dumping Animation Studio. Best known for Ne Zha (2019) and Ne Zha 2 (2025), the latter becoming the highest-grossing animated film of all time and the highest-grossing non-English film ever. Based in Chengdu, Sichuan province. Key studio in the modern Chinese animation renaissance.

name: Kaohsiung Shorts
significance: Program of the Kaohsiung Film Festival in Taiwan, which has been organizing international short film competitions since 2011, becoming the largest international short film platform in Taiwan. Since 2015, the program has expanded internationally, bringing Kaohsiung short films to Hong Kong, France, Japan, South Korea, Vietnam, and other countries. Accepts fiction, documentary, experimental, and animation under 25 minutes. An exhibition and festival platform rather than a production studio.

name: Vega Entertainment
significance: Indian digital content and distribution company founded in 2007 in Hyderabad. Focuses on movie production, digital media, and mobile applications. Works with South Indian, Bollywood, and Hollywood film industries.

name: Ningbo Shuimu Animation
significance: Chinese animation studio branch of Shuimu Animation based in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province. Part of a larger network of Shuimu studios across China including Dongguan Shuimu. One of China's most productive animation studios, ranking among top 10 in national animation output. Produces animation for CCTV and various domestic broadcasters. Named 'key enterprise for cultural export in China.'

name: Studio Eeksaurus
significance: India's premier design-driven animation studio founded by Suresh Eriyat (NID graduate) and Nilima Eriyat. Has produced over 400 films winning 100+ national and international awards. Won the Cristal at Annecy 2015 for Fateline—a first for India. Films Tokri, Fisherwoman, and Tuk-Tuk have won National Film Awards for Best Non-Feature Animation. Known for innovative techniques and cultural storytelling.

name: Illusion Studios
significance: Argentine animation studio founded in 2001 in Buenos Aires. One of Latin America's prominent animation houses specializing in feature-length animated films. Produced Boogie, el aceitoso (2009), an adult-oriented action film that was 'sexist, violent and sadistic' by design—a satirical adaptation of Roberto Fontanarrosa's comic strip. Also produced Gaturro (2010), a $6 million CGI adaptation of a popular Argentine comic strip co-developed with Toonz Animation India. Established a Mexico outpost in 2007.

name: APT Entertainment
significance: Philippine television and film production company founded by Antonio P. Tuviera in 1994 as a subsidiary of TAPE Inc. Best known for producing Eat Bulaga!, the country's longest-running live noontime variety program. Primarily a live-action production house with minimal animation output, limited to A Tad of Christmas Cheer (2007) for LeapFrog and occasional animated segments within its variety programming. Tangential animation relevance.

name: Peninsula Pictures
significance: Indian production company founded January 13, 2015 by Alind Srivastava and Nissar Parvej in Mumbai. Produces television series across fantasy, mythological, drama, thriller, crime, mystery, and romance genres for major channels including Sony SAB, Colors, Zee TV, and Star. Notable shows include 'Aladdin – Naam Toh Suna Hoga', 'Paramavatar Shri Krishna', and 'Vikram Betaal Ki Rahasya Gatha'. In 2017, launched Peninsula Studio division for specialized VFX and computer graphics.

name: Regal Films
significance: One of the largest and oldest surviving film studios in the Philippines, founded by Lily Monteverde on August 19, 1962. Started as a distributor of foreign films before becoming a major producer of Filipino cinema across all genres. While primarily a live-action studio, has co-produced animated features including Dayo (2008), the first Filipino 3D animated feature film.

name: Mundoloco CGI
significance: Argentine CGI animation studio founded by Juan José Campanella (The Secret in Their Eyes director), Gastón Gorali, Roberto Schroder, and Sergio Fernandez. Formerly known as Catmandu Branded Entertainment (2007-2013). Produced Metegol/Underdogs (2013), the largest animated film from Latin America, and Emmy-nominated TV series Mini Beat Power Rockers. One of the top animation studios in Latin America.

name: Citoplasmas Stop Motion
significance: Independent stop-motion animation studio founded in Chile, now based in Barcelona, Spain. Works with diverse materials including clay, paper, sand, latex, and puppets. Currently producing Olivia and the Invisible Earthquake, a stop-motion feature film. Named after their first multi-awarded short film Citoplasmas.

name: Maleza
significance: Chilean stop-motion animation studio and theater company founded by Hugo Covarrubias and Muriel Miranda. Pioneers in mixing theater with animation ('Teatroanimación'). Notable works include short films El almohadón de plumas (The Feather Pillow, 2007), La noche boca arriba (The Night Face Up, 2012), and Bestia (2021), which was nominated for Best Animated Short Film at the 2022 Academy Awards. Influenced by Czech masters Jiří Trnka and Jan Švankmajer.

name: Rocketsheep Studio
significance: Award-winning Philippine boutique animation studio founded by director Avid Liongoren, based in Quezon City. Specializes in illustration, 2D animation, and hybrid live-action/animation. Produced Saving Sally (2016), a decade-long passion project, and Hayop Ka! (You Animal!, 2020) for Netflix. Known for representing Filipino urban landscapes and culture in animation. Alumni include animators who went on to work on Bojack Horseman and Tuca & Bertie.

name: Martin's River Ink
significance: Canadian production company founded by Donald Sutherland. Produced the animated film Pirate's Passage (2015), adapted from William Gilkerson's novel. The film was produced with PiP Animation Services and broadcast on CBC Television. Sutherland also voiced the lead character Captain Johnson in the film.

name: Magic Carpet Studios
significance: Nigerian animation studio founded by Ferdinand 'Ferdy' Adimefe, committed to putting authentic African stories on the global entertainment map. One of Africa's leading animation and game development studios, specializing in 2D, 3D, cutout, and innovative techniques like AR/VR. Currently producing The Passport of Mallam Ilia, a $2 million feature adapted from Cyprian Ekwensi's 1960 novel.

name: Vietnam Animation Studio
significance: State-owned animation studio founded November 9, 1959 in Hanoi. Produced Vietnam's first animated film 'What the Fox Deserves' (1960). Nearly the sole producer of Vietnamese animation for decades.

name: Uzbekfilm
significance: Uzbekistan's largest and oldest film studio, founded July 1, 1925 as Sharq Yulduzi (Eastern Star). Headquartered in Tashkent. Major center of Soviet-era Central Asian animation and filmmaking.

name: Afrikana Digital
significance: Multi award-winning 3D animation studio based in Nairobi, Kenya, founded by Andrew Kaggia with over 12 years of experience in Unreal Engine. Produced feature film TeraStorm (2022). Developed the videogame Nairobi X, Kenya's first 3D FPS game, as part of Black Division Games. Launched YouTube channel Heroes Smashers in 2016. Part of the growing East African creative industry.

name: Tallinnfilm
significance: Estonia's primary state film studio from 1931-1996. Produced acclaimed puppet and drawn animation including works by Priit Pärn. Major center of Soviet-era Estonian animation.

name: Mano Animation Studios
significance: Pakistan's first hand-drawn animation studio, based in Karachi. Co-founded by Usman Riaz (director/composer), Mariam Paracha, and Khizer Riaz. Produced The Glassworker (2024), Pakistan's first hand-drawn animated feature film, which premiered at Annecy International Animation Film Festival and screened at Cannes. The studio's style is influenced by Studio Ghibli and traditional 2D animation techniques.

name: YouNeek Studios
significance: Nigerian multimedia entertainment company founded by Roye Okupe in 2012. Creates graphic novels and animation inspired by African history and mythology. Published by Dark Horse Comics. Produced Iyanu: Child of Wonder animated series.

name: EVCL
significance: Nigerian animation studio founded in 2007 by Adamu Waziri in Abuja. Pioneer in Nigerian animation industry, creating Bino and Fino—the first Nigerian children's animated program to broadcast internationally, described by CNN as 'Africa's answer to Dora the Explorer.' Featured by Voice of America. Produces quality Nigerian and African-inspired animated content for global audiences.

name: Alsahar Animation
significance: Founded in 1992 in Cairo by Saudi producer Abbas Alabbas (also known as Alsahar Animation Co.). One of the largest animation studios in the Arab world. Created The Knight and The Princess (2019), the first animated feature film produced in Egypt and first Arab animated feature shown at Annecy. Produced over 5,000 minutes of content for MBC, Egyptian TV, Saudi TV, and Qatari television. Pioneer of Arab animation industry.

name: Purple Cow Studio Japan
significance: Japanese animation studio established June 5, 2012. Co-produced Yasuhiro Yoshiura's acclaimed sci-fi film Patema Inverted (2013) with Studio Rikka. Also worked on animation production for Yozakura Quartet: Hoshi no Umi OVA and provided photography cooperation for Black Rock Shooter TV series.

name: Academy Productions
significance: Japanese animation studio originally founded as Academy Productions in April 1973 by producer Yoshinobu Nishizaki (1934–2010), who had earlier established Office Academy in 1963 as a music production company. Nishizaki entered anime through Mushi Production in 1970. The studio produced the original Space Battleship Yamato (1974), Space Battleship Yamato 2, Space Battleship Yamato III, Beast King GoLion (adapted as Voltron in the West), and Space Emperor God Sigma. Went through several name changes: Academy Productions (1973–1980), Tokyo Animation (1980), Office Academy (1980), Nishizaki Music & Video Corporation (1980–1983), and finally West Cape Corporation (1983–1997). Declared bankruptcy in August 1997 with debts of 4.8 billion yen.

name: Yamamura Animation
significance: Founded in 1993 by Kōji Yamamura. Mt. Head (2002) was Oscar-nominated and won six Grand Prix including Annecy. First animator to win Grand Prix at all major international animation festivals.

name: Studio Rikka
significance: Japanese animation studio founded by director Yasuhiro Yoshiura. Known for sci-fi works exploring human-AI relationships including Time of Eve and Patema Inverted. Yoshiura handles most creative roles personally, developing a distinct visual style.

name: Studio Mir
significance: South Korean animation studio founded in 2010 by Jae-Myung Yu, former animation director of Avatar: The Last Airbender. Named after Soviet space station Mir for its 'scientific breakthrough and collaborative spirit.' Produced The Legend of Korra, DOTA: Dragon's Blood, and The Witcher: Nightmare of the Wolf. Became publicly listed on KOSDAQ in February 2023.

name: Kawamoto Productions
significance: Production entity of Kihachiro Kawamoto (1925-2010), the master of Japanese stop-motion puppet animation. Kawamoto was Tadahito Mochinaga's apprentice in the 1950s and later studied with Czech puppet master Jiří Trnka in Prague. Drew on Japanese aesthetic traditions including Noh, Kabuki, and Bunraku doll theater. His haunting, poetic films like The Demon (1972) and Dojoji Temple (1976) speak of passion, loss, and worlds of ghosts. President of Japan Animation Association from 1989 until his death, succeeding Osamu Tezuka. Influenced generations of stop-motion animators.

name: Goskinotekhnikum (All-Union Technicum of Cinematography)
significance: First Soviet animation studio, established at the Moscow Film School (later VGIK/Gerasimov Institute of Cinematography). Founded by Vladimir Gardin in 1919. Produced pioneering Soviet animations including Interplanetary Revolution (1924) by Nikolai Khodataev, Zenon Komissarenko, and Yuri Merkulov. Birthplace of Soviet animation tradition that influenced Soyuzmultfilm. Also known as All-Union Technicum of Cinematography.

name: Mingxing Studio
significance: Mingxing Film Company (Star Motion Picture Company), one of the largest film production companies in Republican-era China. Founded in Shanghai by Zhang Shichuan and Zheng Zhengqiu, it produced China's first full sound film Sing-Song Girl Red Peony (1931) and classics like Street Angel (1937). Part of the 'big three' studios alongside Tianyi and Lianhua. Forced to close due to the Second Sino-Japanese War.

name: Northeast Film Studio
significance: Historic Chinese state-owned film studio established October 1, 1946 by the Chinese Communist Party in Changchun, using facilities of the former Manchukuo Film Association. The first film production entity founded under communist control and foundational hub for New China's film industry. Produced China's first puppet animation, science education film, cartoon film, and dubbed foreign films. Merged into Changchun Film Studio in 1955.

name: Fengduan Pictures
significance: Chinese animation production company based in Shanghai. Produced Light Pillar (2026), director Xu Zao's debut feature mixing live action and animation, selected for Berlin Film Festival's Perspectives section. Xu previously won DOK Leipzig's Golden Dove in 2023 for animated documentary short No Changes Have Taken in Our Life.

name: Niceboat Animation
significance: Chinese animation studio (好传动画) headquartered in Tianjin, founded February 13, 2012. Part of the modern donghua renaissance. Has raised $7.31M in funding from investors including GeeCap and Beijing Enlight Media. Produces high-quality 2D animated features and series.

name: Eesti Reklaamfilm
significance: Estonian state-owned advertising agency (Estonian Advertising Film) that produced over 6,000 commercials promoting products in the Soviet Union from 1967-1998. Founded by Peedu Ojamaa after Brezhnev mandated companies spend 1% of revenue on advertising. Notably created ads for non-existent products as propaganda. Pioneering work by cinematographer Harry Egipt.

name: Sofia Animation Studio
significance: Bulgaria's central animation studio, founded when Todor Dinov recruited Donyo Donev. Produced Bulgaria's animated output for decades, nurturing generations of animators including Anri Kulev. Key works include The Apple (1963) and Three Fools (1970).

name: Jadran Film
significance: Yugoslav (now Croatian) film studio founded in 1946 in Zagreb. One of the two main film studios in Yugoslav cinema alongside Avala Film of Belgrade. While primarily a live-action studio known for international co-productions, Jadran Film played a role in Croatian film history alongside animation-focused Zagreb Film. Produced over 70 years of films and remains active today in Zagreb. Not to be confused with Zagreb Film, which is specifically known for animated films and the Zagreb School of Animation.

name: Classica Film Studio
significance: Russian animation studio founded by Alexander Petrov in Yaroslavl after his Academy Award win for The Old Man and the Sea. Known as 'Мастерская Александра Петрова' (Alexander Petrov's Workshop). Continues the labor-intensive oil painting on glass animation technique that Petrov pioneered, producing acclaimed works including The Mermaid (1997) and My Love (2006).

name: DLE
significance: Tokyo-based animation and entertainment company (Dream Link Entertainment) founded by former Sony executive Ryuta Shiiki. Known for flagship Flash animation series Eagle Talon by Frogman (Ryo Ono). Produced DC Super Heroes vs. Eagle Talon (2017), first major crossover with global IP. Pioneer in AI-powered anime and business partners across Asia, Middle East, and North America.

name: 20th Century Fox
significance: Animation division of 20th Century Fox (now 20th Century Studios). Originally formed in 1994, oversaw Fox Animation Studios (1994-2000) and Blue Sky Studios (1999-2021). Produced Anastasia, Titan A.E., and the Ice Age franchise. Rebranded as 20th Century Animation following the 2019 Disney-Fox merger; continues operating as a Walt Disney Studios division.

name: Columbia Pictures
significance: Major Hollywood studio founded in 1924. Distributed animation since 1929, including Krazy Kat and early Mickey Mouse cartoons. Established Screen Gems animation division in 1933 (Scrappy, Fox and Crow). Later distributed UPA shorts. Now part of Sony Pictures, parent of Sony Pictures Animation (founded 2002) which produced Spider-Verse and Hotel Transylvania franchises.

name: Ankama
significance: French transmedia entertainment company founded May 15, 2001 in Roubaix by Anthony Roux, Camille Chafer, and Emmanuel Darras. Name derived from founders' initials. Known for DOFUS MMORPG (85M+ accounts) and Wakfu franchise. Animation division founded 2006; Tokyo studio established 2009. Produced feature film Dofus Book 1: Julith (2016) and collaborated with Studio 4°C on MFKZ (Mutafukaz). Pioneers of Flash-based animation expanding into traditional and CGI techniques.

name: MGM Animation
significance: Animation division of Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer founded in 1992 by Paul Sabella and Jonathan Dern. Produced animated films and TV series based on MGM's library including The Pink Panther (1993), All Dogs Go to Heaven 2 (1996), and Tom and Jerry direct-to-video films. Sabella and Dern left in 1999 to form Sabella Dern Entertainment; the studio went dormant in 2002.

name: Millimages
significance: Major independent French animation production company founded by Roch Lener. Develops, produces, and licenses high-quality family entertainment with a catalogue of over 75 IPs. Known worldwide for Molang (International Emmy Kids nomination 2016), 64 Zoo Lane, Corneil and Bernie, and Pablo the Little Red Fox. Generates 10M+ views daily across the globe.

name: SOLA DIGITAL ARTS
significance: Japanese CGI animation studio founded October 22, 2009 by Joseph Chou, former ADV Films producer, and director Shinji Aramaki. Specializes in technically superior 3DCG animation for films, TV, and video games. Notable works include Ultraman (Netflix), Appleseed Alpha, and contributions to The Animatrix. Became division of Sola Entertainment in 2017.

name: Signal.MD
significance: Japanese animation studio founded October 1, 2014 by IG Port as a subsidiary of Production I.G. Focused on digital innovation and family-oriented content. Produced Platinum End, Hirune Hime, and contributed to various anime projects. Merged into Production I.G in June 2025 but continues as an internal brand.

name: Myung Films
significance: South Korean film production and distribution company founded in 1995 by Jamie Shim (Sim Jae-myung). One of Korea's leading production companies, producing early works by renowned directors Kim Ki-duk (The Isle), Kim Jee-woon (The Quiet Family), Park Chan-wook (Joint Security Area), and Im Sang-soo. Co-produced animated feature Leafie, A Hen into the Wild (2011) with Odolttogi, which became one of Korea's most successful domestic animated films.

name: Artmic
significance: Japanese animation design studio founded in 1978 by Toshimichi Suzuki after leaving Tatsunoko Productions. Name stands for 'Art and Modern Ideology for Creation.' Known for Bubblegum Crisis, Genesis Climber Mospeada, Megazone 23, Gall Force, and Dangaioh. Also designed for Western shows including M.A.S.K. and The Real Ghostbusters. Went bankrupt in 1997; IP acquired by AIC.

name: Kitty Films
significance: Japanese production company founded in 1972 by Hidenori Taga. While not an animation studio itself, Kitty Films commissioned and oversaw some of the most influential anime of the 1980s. Produced the animated adaptations of Rumiko Takahashi's works including Urusei Yatsura (1981-1986), Maison Ikkoku, and Ranma ½. Partnered with Studio Pierrot and Studio Deen for actual animation. Urusei Yatsura director Mamoru Oshii launched his career at Kitty. Now primarily operates as a talent agency.

name: Ashi Productions
significance: Japanese anime studio founded December 20, 1975 by Toshihiko Sato in Suginami, Tokyo. Known for magical girl anime, especially Magical Princess Minky Momo. Also produced mecha series like Machine Blaster and Ginguiser. Operated as Production Reed (2007-2019), then reverted to original name. Owned by Bandai (2001-2005), then Wiz (2005-2010). Actas was a subsidiary from 1986-1998. Remains active today.

name: KAFA
significance: South Korea's national film school (한국영화아카데미, Korean Academy of Film Arts), established in 1984 by the Korean Film Council (KOFIC). Offers highly selective intensive programs in Directing, Cinematography, Producing, Animation, and Sound. The Animation major was added in 1999 with the establishment of the Korean Academy of Animation Arts. Produces approximately seven feature films per year through its Feature Film Program. Has graduated 600+ alumni who serve central roles in Korean cinema. Located in Busan since 2018. Known for field-centered training and portfolio-based selection.

name: Aniplex
significance: Founded in 1995 as Sony Pictures Entertainment Visual Works, renamed Aniplex in 2003. Major anime production and distribution company under Sony Music Entertainment Japan. Parent company of A-1 Pictures and CloverWorks studios. Known for producing Sword Art Online, Demon Slayer, Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood, and the Fate franchise. Also publishes Fate/Grand Order mobile game.

name: Big West
significance: Japanese advertising firm founded September 1, 1973 by Yoshimasa Onishi. Primary sponsor and copyright holder of the Macross franchise, working with Studio Nue, Artland, and Tatsunoko Productions. In 2021, reached landmark agreement with Harmony Gold allowing international distribution of Macross sequels worldwide.

name: Manga Productions
significance: Saudi Arabian anime and manga production company, subsidiary of the Mohammed bin Salman Foundation (Misk). Partners with Toei Animation on projects including The Journey (2021) and Future's Folktales. First major anime studio in the Middle East, focused on developing local talent and creating content inspired by Arabian culture.

name: Seoul Donghwa
significance: Pioneering South Korean animation studio founded by director Kim Cheong-gi in 1975. Produced Robot Taekwon V (1976), considered the first major Korean animated feature and a cultural icon. Kim built the studio with a dream of creating autonomous local Korean animation independent of foreign outsourcing. Still operating today as Seoul Donghwa Pictures.

name: Lammtara Art Production
significance: Dubai-based animation studio founded in 2005 by Mohammed Saeed Harib. Also known as Lammtara Pictures. Created Freej (2006), the UAE's first 3D animated TV series depicting four elderly Emirati women navigating modern Dubai. Freej became a national icon and cultural phenomenon, spawning merchandise, theme park plans, and becoming the first Arab-produced animation dubbed in Japanese (2018). Also produced Mandoos and Siraj. The studio serves as a hub for cultural entertainment inspired by Arabic and Islamic heritage.

name: Les' Copaque Production
significance: Malaysian CGI animation and live-action production company founded in December 2005 by Burhanuddin Md Radzi and his wife Ainon Ariff in Shah Alam, Selangor. Known for the hugely successful Upin & Ipin series (since 2007), which pioneered Malaysian animation and influenced the country's animation industry. Also produced Geng: The Adventure Begins (2009), Pada Zaman Dahulu (since 2011), and feature films. One of the highest-grossing Malay-language film producers.

name: Shemaroo Entertainment
significance: Indian content creator, aggregator and distributor founded by Buddhichand Maroo. Started as a book circulating library and set up India's first video rental business in 1979. Began producing animated films in 2007, including the Bal Ganesh series. Manages an extensive library of over 32,000 hours of content including nearly 3,000 Bollywood film titles.

name: Cairo Cartoon
significance: Egypt's leading animation studio (Cairo Cartoon Studios), founded in 1988 by Dr. Mona Abou el Nasr (also referenced as Mona Abu Nasr). Pioneer of CGI animation in Egypt and the Middle East. Created the beloved Bakkar series (1998) about a Nubian boy, which ran for nine seasons and became a national icon and symbol of Egyptian unity. Has completed over 180 hours of animation production. Provides prime quality 2D and 3D animation services to major production companies globally while also developing original projects. 51-200 employees. Based in Heliopolis, Cairo.

name: Kukua
significance: Kenyan educational entertainment company and animation studio based in Nairobi. Creator of Super Sema (2021), the first African animated superhero franchise, executive produced by Academy Award-winning actress Lupita Nyong'o. The show empowers children through STEAM education and features a young African girl inventor. Animation produced across Kenya, Nigeria, and Italy using Adobe Animate. Super Sema airs on YouTube Originals and major African TV networks. Raised $6 million in 2022 led by Alchimia and Tencent. Represents a new era of African-created children's content.

name: New Theatres
significance: Pioneering Indian film studio founded by Birendranath Sircar in Calcutta on February 10, 1931. Produced India's first animated film released in theatres: The Pea Brothers (1934), directed by Gunamoy Banerjee, a 3-4 minute black and white drawn animation. Also produced On a Moonlight (1934) and Michke Potash (1950). Produced 150 films over 24 years. Management rights were handed to Aurora Film Company in June 1954 amid financial difficulties, and the studio was closed in January 1956. Foundational to Indian animation and cinema history.

name: Phalke Films
significance: Production company of Dadasaheb Phalke, the 'Father of Indian Cinema.' Phalke created India's first feature film Raja Harishchandra (1913) and pioneered early Indian animation experiments using stop-motion and trick photography.

name: Filmax Animation
significance: Spanish animation arm of Filmax International, one of Spain's largest integrated film and television groups based in Barcelona. Filmax Animación was formed in 2001 to handle animation production, services, and distribution. Integrated Bren Entertainment, led by Francisco 'Paco' Rodriguez (founder of PPM Multimedia). Filmax itself was founded in 1953, making it one of Spain's longest-standing audiovisual brands. Produced animated features including Bikes (2019) and Robotia (2024). The parent company Filmax is famous for the REC horror series and the Fantastic Factory genre label created by Brian Yuzna and Julio Fernández.

name: British Film Institute
significance: UK's lead organization for film and moving image, founded 1933. Cultural charity and National Lottery distributor. Houses the BFI National Archive, world's largest film and television archive. Has supported and distributed British animation through touring programs, funding, and preservation since early pioneers like Len Lye and Norman McLaren.

name: National Film and Television School
significance: UK's leading film and television school, established in 1971 at Beaconsfield Studios in Buckinghamshire. Has one of the world's most respected animation departments, producing award-winning short films and training filmmakers who go on to work at major studios worldwide. Alumni have won numerous BAFTA and Academy Awards. Offers specialized programs in animation for film and games.

name: Qvisten Animation
significance: Norway's largest animation studio, founded in 1994 in Oslo by two animators in their early twenties in a small drafty attic ('kvistloft' in Norwegian, hence the name). Today employs 65-80+ talents from around the world. Specializes in stop-motion and CG animation. Produced and co-produced over 20 feature films, many topping Norwegian box office. Created beloved characters including Louis & Luca, Captain Sabertooth, and Two Buddies and a Badger. Adapted stories by iconic Nordic writers Thorbjørn Egner, Astrid Lindgren, and Kjell Aukrust. One of the largest animation studios in all of Scandinavia. Co-owned by director Rasmus A. Sivertsen.

name: nWave Pictures
significance: Belgian CGI animation studio founded in 1994 by Ben Stassen, based in Brussels with an American office in Los Angeles. Pioneer of modern 3D filmmaking and 4D films for theme parks and motion simulators. Features include Fly Me to the Moon (2008), Sammy's Adventures (2010), The House of Magic (2013), The Son of Bigfoot (2017), and Chickenhare and the Hamster of Darkness (2022). In 2018, MZM acquired a majority stake.

name: A. Film A/S
significance: Founded August 1, 1988 by animators Stefan Fjeldmark, Karsten Kiilerich, Jørgen Lerdam, Hans Perk, and producer Anders Mastrup after working on Valhalla (1986). Known for Help! I'm a Fish, Checkered Ninja, Jungledyret Hugo, and Terkel in Trouble. In 1995, Egmont purchased 50% and moved it under Nordisk Film. Many animators trained here later joined Disney and DreamWorks.

name: Bivrost Film
significance: Award-winning Norwegian-Latvian production company and animation studio founded in 1999. Won Emmy for My Body Belongs to Me (2018) with NRK Super. Co-produced My Favorite War (2020) with Latvia's Ego Media, which won Annecy Contrechamp Award—a mixed animation/live-action documentary inspired by Persepolis and Waltz with Bashir. Focuses on high-quality children's content addressing social themes.

name: Escena Animation Studio
significance: Mexican animation studio affiliated with ESCENA animation school in Mexico. Produced Shimmer (Fulgores, 2024), winner of the Ariel Award for Best Animated Short and Oscar-qualified. The studio-school model allows students to work on professional productions alongside faculty.

name: León & Cociña
significance: Chilean animation duo (Cristóbal León and Joaquín Cociña, both born 1980) known for experimental stop-motion films that integrate visual arts, sculpture, drawing, and performance. Both studied at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile; León also studied at UdK Berlin and De Ateliers Amsterdam. Their debut feature The Wolf House (La Casa Lobo, 2018) premiered at Berlin Film Festival and was created as a nomadic work-in-process across 12 exhibitions. Also created Los Huesos and directed music videos for PJ Harvey and The Smile. In 2024, formed León & Cociña Films production company with producer Catalina Vergara.

name: Federico Valle Productions
significance: Production company of Italian-Argentine film pioneer Federico Valle (1880-1960). Valle worked as a cameraman for the Lumière Brothers before emigrating to Argentina. Produced El Apóstol (1917), the world's first feature-length animated film, and Sin dejar rastros (1918), directed by Quirino Cristiani using cutout animation. Also produced Peludópolis (1931), the first animated feature with synchronized sound. A 1926 fire at Valle's studio vaults destroyed all known copies of El Apóstol. Foundational to world animation history.

name: Coala Filmes
significance: Brazilian stop-motion animation studio founded in São Paulo with over 25 years in the audiovisual market. Won Annecy Contrechamp Award and Ottawa Animation Festival Grand Prize for Bob Cuspe - We Do Not Like People (2021), directed by Cesar Cabral—the first Latin American film to receive Ottawa's top honor. Known for award-winning shorts Dossiê Rê Bordosa and Tempestade, screened at Sundance and Hiroshima. Based on Rua Augusta in São Paulo.

name: Bits Produções
significance: Brazilian animation and game production studio founded in São Paulo. Known for Tito and the Birds (2018), directed by Gustavo Steinberg, Gabriel Bitar, and André Catoto, which employed innovative mixed media techniques including oil paintings, digital drawings, and graphic animation. Oscar-longlisted, Annie-nominated for Best Independent Animated Feature, and winner at Anima Mundi, Sitges, and Havana. Also founded BIG Festival, Latin America's largest indie games festival.

name: NDR Filmes
significance: Brazilian animation studio founded by Nello De Rossi. Produced Cassiopeia (1996), recognized as Brazil's first fully CGI animated feature film and one of the earliest CGI features worldwide. Production began in 1992 using 386 and 486 computers, demonstrating that high-quality CGI could be achieved with modest budgets. Pioneering studio in Latin American CGI animation.

name: Fosfenos Media
significance: Colombian animation studio founded in Cali by sisters Maritza and Marcela Rincón, the first animation studio in that city. Specializes in quality educational content for children. Created Guillermina y Candelario, a beloved animated series, and produced El Libro de Lila (Lila's Book), an animated feature that premiered at Cannes. Known for exporting childhood educational content.

name: Patagonik Film Group
significance: Founded in 1996 by Pablo Bossi in Buenos Aires, Patagonik is the leading film production company in Latin America. Part of Clarín Group and Disney partner. Produced over 50 feature films including animated works Patoruzito, Condor Crux, El Ratón Pérez, and El Arca. Known for visual effects, computer animation, and character design.

name: Mauricio de Sousa Produções
significance: Brazil's most successful comic book and animation publisher, founded in 1959 by Mauricio de Sousa. Now known as MSP Estúdios. Created Monica's Gang (Turma da Mônica), Brazil's most popular comic series, based on his childhood friends and children. Described as one of the largest animation studios in Brazil. Spans comics, cartoons, character development, product licensing, and amusement parks.

name: Buriti Filmes
significance: Brazilian film production company founded 1997 in São Paulo by filmmakers Laís Bodanzky and Luiz Bolognesi. Produced Rio 2096: A Story of Love and Fury (2013), which won the Cristal Award at Annecy for Best Feature and African Movie Academy Award—an ambitious adult animated epic spanning 600 years of Brazilian history. Also produced Perlimps (2022). Works across live action, documentary, and animation.

name: Latini Studio
significance: Founded by Anelio Latini Filho (1926-1986), self-taught animator who created Brazil's first feature-length animated film, Sinfonia Amazônica (Amazon Symphony, 1953). Latini worked almost single-handedly for six years, handling animation, character design, backgrounds, and artistic direction. The film wove together seven Amazonian legends. His brother Mario Latini assisted with photography and composed a samba for the score. Earlier, the brothers created the short Azares de Lulu (1940).

name: Disney Television Animation
significance: Division of Walt Disney Television founded December 5, 1984 by Gary Krisel to create original animated content for television. Produced creator-driven series including DuckTales, Darkwing Duck, Gargoyles, Kim Possible, Phineas and Ferb, Gravity Falls, and The Owl House. Revolutionized Disney's presence in TV animation and expanded beyond theatrical releases.

name: SEK Animation Studio
significance: North Korea's state-owned animation studio, officially established September 7, 1957 in Pyongyang. Employs over 1,500 personnel. Produces domestic propaganda content including 'Squirrel and Hedgehog' series. Has subcontracted for international companies including European studios like Mondo TV. Sanctioned by US Treasury Department in 2021.

name: Pennfilm
significance: Sweden's most established animation studio, founded in 1970 by Per Åhlin in Hököpinge. Created five feature films including Dunderklumpen! (1974), Journey to Melonia (1989), and That Boy Emil (2013). Best known for Sagan om Karl-Bertil Jonssons julafton (1975), broadcast every Christmas Eve in Sweden, Norway, and Finland. Åhlin (1931-2020) was one of Sweden's most prominent animators.

name: Bitter Films
significance: Don Hertzfeldt's independent animation studio, self-distributing his films since the 1990s. Produced Oscar-nominated Rejected (2000) and the World of Tomorrow trilogy. Hertzfeldt pioneered minimalist stick-figure animation with existential themes, earning a Palme d'Or nomination at 21 and establishing himself as one of America's most important independent animators.

name: Blinkink
significance: London-based animation and mixed-media production studio, part of the Blink group (founded 1985). BAFTA-winning and Oscar-nominated. Specializes in blending hand-crafted techniques with modern technology. Works across commercials, music videos, and entertainment including Gorillaz visuals.

name: Film Workshop
significance: Hong Kong film production company and distributor founded by director Tsui Hark and producer Nansun Shi. Set endless trends in Asian cinema since the 1980s including A Better Tomorrow series, A Chinese Ghost Story series, Once Upon a Time in China, and Detective Dee series. Produced A Chinese Ghost Story: The Tsui Hark Animation (1997), considered Hong Kong's first animated feature.

name: Revcom
significance: French television production and distribution company (Revcom Télévision/Revcom Production). Produced and co-produced animated features including Gandahar (1988), How Wang-Fo Was Saved (1987), and The Captive (1985). Important partner in René Laloux's later animated films. Also produced international live-action co-productions in Australia and Europe.

name: Lucasfilm Animation
significance: Animation division of Lucasfilm established in 2005, with development beginning on Star Wars: The Clone Wars under supervising director Dave Filoni and executive producer George Lucas. Launched a digital studio in Singapore and partnered with CGCG Inc. in Taiwan. The Clone Wars debuted in 2008 as a feature film and Emmy Award-winning TV series spanning seven seasons. Also produced Star Wars Rebels and Strange Magic (2015). Filoni was promoted in 2016 to oversee all Lucasfilm Animation projects.

name: Kadr Film Unit
significance: Polish film production unit (Studio Filmowe KADR) founded in 1955 by director Jerzy Kawalerowicz. While primarily a live-action studio, KADR was instrumental in establishing Polish cinema as world-class in the late 1950s. Home to legendary director Andrzej Wajda, who made A Generation (1955), Kanał (1956), and Ashes and Diamonds (1958) at the studio. Produced over 600 films. In 2011, absorbed the OKO Film Studio. Now focuses on digital reconstruction of Polish cinematic masterpieces.

name: Panorama Animation Film Studio
significance: Russian animation production company based in Yaroslavl. Collaborated with SHAR School-Studio, DAGO, and Rys Studio on projects featuring paint-on-glass animator Alexander Petrov, including The Mermaid (1996). Part of the independent Russian animation scene that emerged in the 1990s.

name: Beijing Enlight Pictures
significance: Major Chinese film production and distribution company, founded 1998. Established animation subsidiary Coloroom Pictures in 2015, which produced Ne Zha (2019), China's second-highest-grossing film ever. Along with Light Chaser and Fantawild, commands over 50% of Chinese animated film box office.

name: October Media
significance: Founded in 1999 by director Tian Xiaopeng, October Media is one of the earliest 3D animation production companies in China. Produced 'Monkey King: Hero Is Back' (2015), which set a new record for Chinese animation with RMB 956 million box office, and 'Deep Sea' (2023). Recognized as a leading force in the Chinese animation industry.

name: Coloroom Pictures
significance: Animation subsidiary of Beijing Enlight Pictures, established 2015 with the goal of becoming China's Pixar. Produced Ne Zha (2019) and co-produced Ne Zha 2 (2025), the highest-grossing animated film of all time at $2.2B. Also produced Big Fish & Begonia, Deep Sea, and Dahufa. Major distributor of Japanese animation in China including Your Name, Spirited Away, and Weathering with You. Forms one of China's 'Big Three' animation studios alongside Light Chaser and Fantawild, commanding over 50% domestic animated film market share.

name: Gubernia Foundation
significance: Russian nonprofit foundation for social and cultural programs ('Gubernia' means 'Province'). Part of Master-Film Holding led by producer Alexander Gerasimov since 2006. Produces auteur animation including anti-drug educational series Re-animation. Known for independent and artistic short films by acclaimed animators including Ivan Maximov. Works have screened at international festivals.

name: Original Force
significance: Major Chinese digital animation and CG studio founded in 1999 in Nanjing by CEO Harley Zhao. Grew from a 4-person startup to a 2,500+ employee operation across Nanjing, Beijing, Chengdu, Wuhan, Los Angeles, Tokyo, and Bangkok. Initially provided CG animation services for global clients including Disney, DreamWorks Television, Sony, Tencent, Activision, and Electronic Arts. In 2015, opened a Hollywood motion picture division led by former DreamWorks Animation and Sony Pictures Animation executives Sandy Rabins and Penney Finkelman Cox (producers of Shrek, Prince of Egypt, Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs). Now developing original feature film IP alongside service work. One of China's largest animation studios.

name: CCTV Animation
significance: State-owned animation group founded March 13, 2007, wholly invested by China Central Television (CCTV). Reorganized as CCTV Animation Group in 2020 under China Media Group. Produced domestic animation masterpieces including Journey to the West, The Legend of Nezha, The Adventures of Little Carp, Happy Dad and Son, and Panda and Little Mole. Aims to build a Chinese cartoon universe with global influence.

name: Great Wall Film Company
significance: Pioneer Chinese film studio originally founded in New York in 1921 by Chinese-American investors, relocated to Shanghai in 1923. Employed the Wan Brothers who created China's first animation short Uproar in the Studio (1926). Pioneered Chinese animation techniques influenced by Fleischer's Out of the Inkwell series. Laid groundwork for Chinese animation tradition.

name: Argos Films
significance: Historic French film production company founded in 1949 by Anatole Dauman and Philippe Lifchitz. One of the most important independent production companies in post-war French cinema, Argos Films was a key vehicle for the Left Bank filmmakers of the Nouvelle Vague. Produced landmark art films including Alain Resnais' Night and Fog (1956), Hiroshima Mon Amour (1959), and Last Year at Marienbad (1961); Chris Marker's La Jetée (1962); René Laloux's groundbreaking Fantastic Planet (La Planète Sauvage, 1973, winner of the Special Jury Prize at Cannes); Volker Schlöndorff's The Tin Drum (1979 Academy Award for Best Foreign Film); and Wim Wenders' Paris, Texas (1984, Palme d'Or) and Wings of Desire (1987). Anatole Dauman died in April 1998. The Argos Films catalogue (84+ films) is now managed and distributed by Cité Films, founded in 1997 by Raphaël Berdugo.

name: ORTF
significance: Office de Radiodiffusion-Télévision Française (ORTF) was the French national public broadcaster from 1964-1974. Aired and produced animated series including The Magic Roundabout (1964-67), Les Shadoks (1968-72), Barbapapa (1974), and Colargol (1968-74). Dissolved in 1974 into separate entities including TF1 and INA.

name: Mainframe Entertainment
significance: Vancouver-based studio established in 1993 by Christopher Brough and British animation team 'The Hub' (Gavin Blair, Ian Pearson, Phil Mitchell, John Grace). Created ReBoot (1994), the first fully computer-animated television series, after pioneering CGI in music videos like Dire Straits' 'Money for Nothing.' Also produced Beast Wars: Transformers and Barbie films. Rebranded as Rainmaker Animation in 2007, then returned to Mainframe Studios name.

name: CinéGroupe
significance: Canadian animation studio and production company founded in Montreal, Quebec by Jacques Pettigrew and Michel Lemire. Produced over 1,000 half-hours of animation broadcast in 125+ countries. Won Daytime Emmy for Sagwa, the Chinese Siamese Cat. Notable productions include Heavy Metal 2000, What's with Andy?, and Pinocchio 3000. Repurposed as dubbing studio Ciné-Groupe J.P. Inc. in 2008.

name: Embuscade Films
significance: Canadian animation and film production company founded in 2013 by producers Nicolas and Félix Dufour-Laperrière. Produces animated films, creative documentaries and atypical fictions with an artistic approach. Notable productions include Archipel (animated fiction feature), Transatlantique (documentary), and Death Does Not Exist (2025), an animated feature selected for Cannes 2025. Based in Quebec.

name: Sacrebleu Productions
significance: Founded in 1999 by Ron Dyens. Prolific French producer of animated shorts and features with multiple Oscar nominations including Madagascar: A Journey Diary and And Then the Bear. Produced acclaimed features Long Way North (Annecy 2015 Audience Award) and My Sunny Maad (Annecy 2021 Jury Award). Known for supporting auteur animation.

name: Pascal Blais Productions
significance: Pioneering Canadian animation studio (Studio Pascal Blais) co-founded in 1983 in Montreal by Pascal Blais and Bernard Lajoie. Academy Award-winning studio — produced Alexander Petrov's The Old Man and the Sea (1999, Oscar for Best Animated Short). Also worked with Sylvain Chomet (The Old Lady and the Pigeon, 1997) and Cordell Barker. Rebranded as TONIC DNA in 2018 on its 35th anniversary. Specializes in 2D, 3D, CGI, stop-motion, and VFX work. One of the most prominent animation studios in Quebec. Has offices in Toronto and Mexico. Pascal Blais has since left the studio and now works as an independent animation director/producer.

name: Radio-Canada
significance: Animation studio of the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC/SRC) founded and directed by Hubert Tison until 1993. Home to legendary animator Frédéric Back, whose films won two Academy Awards: Crac! (1981) and The Man Who Planted Trees (1987). Also produced works by Graeme Ross and Paul Driessen. Studio ceased animation production in the early 1990s due to budget cuts.

name: Les Gémeaux
significance: France's most significant early animation studio, co-founded by Paul Grimault and André Sarrut in 1936. Was the only functioning animation studio in occupied Europe during WWII, finding a captive audience when American cartoons were banned. Produced France's first feature-length animated film, La Bergère et le Ramoneur (The Shepherdess and the Chimney Sweep), though it bankrupted the studio. Briefly collaborated with Disney on an unmade package film after WWII.

name: Bridgit Folman Film Gang
significance: Israeli animation production company founded by Ari Folman. Produced Waltz with Bashir (2008), the groundbreaking animated documentary about the 1982 Lebanon War and Sabra and Shatila massacre. The film was nominated for Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film and won Golden Globe.

name: J.C. Staff
significance: Japanese animation studio founded in January 1986 by Tomoyuki Miyata, formerly of Tatsunoko Production. Name stands for 'Japan Creative Staff.' Initially specialized in OVAs before transitioning to television with Metal Fighter Miku (1994). Has produced over 200 animated works including Revolutionary Girl Utena, Azumanga Daioh, Toradora!, A Certain Magical Index, Food Wars!, One-Punch Man Season 2, and DanMachi. Based in Musashino, Tokyo, and a member of the Association of Japanese Animations.

name: Servais Films
significance: Production company of legendary Belgian animator Raoul Servais (1928-2023), considered the father and pioneer of animated film in Belgium. Won the Palme d'Or for Best Short Film at Cannes 1979 for 'Harpya' and created 'Chromophobia' (1966). Produced 15 animated short films and one feature ('Taxandria', 1994). In 1963, founded the first animation film school in continental Europe at KASK Ghent. Developed the 'Servaisgraphie' technique combining live action with animation. Also known as Absolon Films.

name: Triangle Staff
significance: Japanese anime studio founded in 1987 by former Madhouse staff including Makoto Bessho. Produced Macross Plus, Serial Experiments Lain, and NieA_7. Known for experimental storytelling and psychological themes. Ceased operations in December 2000; remaining staff formed successor studio A.C.G.T. in 2000.

name: Shaft
significance: Founded September 1, 1975 by Hiroshi Wakao, former Mushi Production employee. Defined by director Akiyuki Shinbo's avant-garde visual style since 2004. Produced iconic series including Bakemonogatari/Monogatari franchise, Puella Magi Madoka Magica, Hidamari Sketch, and March Comes In Like a Lion. Known for distinctive head tilts, text screens, and surreal imagery.

name: Bakshi Productions
significance: Founded in 1973 by Ralph Bakshi and producer Steve Krantz. Pioneered adult-oriented American animation with Fritz the Cat (1972), the first animated film to receive an X rating and the most successful independent animated feature ever. Created Heavy Traffic (1973), Wizards (1977), The Lord of the Rings (1978), American Pop (1981), and Fire and Ice (1983). Bakshi revolutionized animation with gritty urban realism and rotoscope techniques. Continues today as Bakshi Studios.

name: Cinema Fantasma
significance: Stop-motion animation, film, and art studio based in Mexico City, founded by brothers Arturo and Roy Ambriz. Endorsed by Guillermo del Toro. Created Frankelda's Book of Spooks series for Cartoon Network Latin America/HBO Max and I Am Frankelda (2025), Mexico's first stop-motion feature film. Also produced Pan's Labyrinth automata and Rick and Morty IDs for Adult Swim. Known for distinct Mexican aesthetic blending horror, folklore, and humor.

name: Barajoun Entertainment
significance: Leading animation and VFX studio in the MENA region, founded in 2011 by banker-turned-producer Ayman Jamal in Dubai, UAE. First bona-fide animation studio in the Middle East. Produced Bilal: A New Breed of Hero (2018), the first CGI animated feature from the Arab world. Employs 100-250 artists and collaborates with streaming platform Shahid on Arabic-language animation originals to develop regional animation talent.

name: Punkrobot
significance: Chilean animation studio based in Santiago, founded in 2008 by Antonia Herrera, Gabriel Osorio, Mari Soto-Aguilar, and Pato Escala. Made history with Bear Story (Historia de un oso, 2014), which won the Oscar for Best Animated Short Film at the 88th Academy Awards - the first Chilean and first Latin American animation to win an Oscar. Also created an episode for Star Wars: Visions Volume 2 (2023). Currently developing first feature film Brave Cat.

name: Huevocartoon Producciones
significance: Mexican animation studio and multimedia company founded in November 2001 by Gabriel and Rodolfo Riva Palacio Alatriste and Carlos Zepeda Chehaibar. Known for comedic content featuring anthropomorphic eggs. Created viral web series that evolved into six feature films including Una película de huevos (2006), which won the Ariel Award for Best Animated Feature. One of Mexico's most successful animation franchises.

name: Films Division of India
significance: Government of India's official film production and distribution unit under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Established to produce documentaries and newsreels for publicity of government programs. Holds over 8,000 titles in archives. Pioneered Indian animation and documentary filmmaking. Mandatory screenings before feature films made it integral to India's cinema experience for 50+ years.

name: Fox Animation Studios
significance: American animation studio in Phoenix, Arizona, subsidiary of 20th Century Fox Animation. Founded by legendary animators Don Bluth and Gary Goldman. Produced only two films: Anastasia (1997), the studio's most successful film, and Titan A.E. (2000). Shut down June 26, 2000, ten days after Titan A.E. release. Library now owned by Disney.

name: Inkwell Studios
significance: Original name of the Fleischer Brothers' animation studio, founded by Max and Dave Fleischer in a New York City basement in 1921. Pioneered the combination of live action and animation with the Out of the Inkwell series featuring Ko-Ko the Clown. Max Fleischer invented the rotoscope in 1915, enabling lifelike animated movement. Also invented the bouncing ball sing-along technique. Renamed Fleischer Studios in 1929, the company became one of the most influential animation studios of the 20th century, rivaling Disney with Betty Boop, Popeye, and Superman cartoons.

name: Platige Image
significance: Polish studio founded in 1997, specializing in CGI, 3D animation, and digital special effects. Has received over 200 awards including BAFTA, four Best of Show at SIGGRAPH, and nominations for Academy Award, Cannes Golden Palm, and Venice Golden Lion. Created cinematics for CD Projekt RED's The Witcher and Cyberpunk 2077 games. Executive Producer Tomek Bagiński worked on Netflix's The Witcher series. Co-produced Academy Award-nominated Another Day of Life (2018).

name: Anthill Studios
significance: Leading film studio in Nigeria founded in 2010 by Niyi Akinmolayan. Self-described as Africa's biggest animation/production company. In January 2022, signed agreement with Amazon Prime Video to stream films globally. Known for VFX-heavy Nollywood productions including Mikolo, Jagun Jagun, Lisabi, Seven Doors, and League of Orishas. Produces animations, advertisements, trailers, music videos, documentaries, and films.

name: Je Suis Bien Content
significance: One of Europe's most critically acclaimed animation studios, based in Montreuil near Paris. Created animation for Persepolis (2007), which won the Jury Prize at Cannes, and April and the Extraordinary World (2015), which won the Grand Prix at Annecy. Also produced TV series including Boyster for Disney EMEA and the Netflix adult anime Last Man. In 2018, Watch Next acquired a stake in the studio to expand international distribution. Known for distinctive hand-drawn animation style combining artistic vision with commercial viability.

name: Les Films Paul Grimault
significance: Paul Grimault's production company that completed his masterpiece Le Roi et l'oiseau (The King and the Mockingbird, 1980), which took over 30 years to produce. The film is considered a landmark of French animation and was cited by Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata as a major influence on their work. Grimault (1905-1994) had founded the earlier Les Gémeaux studio in 1936.

name: Gobelins
significance: World's premier animation school (full name: Gobelins, l'école de l'image), founded in Paris in 1963 by the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Paris. Consistently ranked #1 globally for animation programs. Notable alumni include Pierre Coffin (Despicable Me), Benjamin Renner (Ernest & Celestine), Bibo Bergeron (Shark Tale), and countless industry leaders across studios worldwide. Student thesis films regularly go viral and win international awards. Trains animators from around the world in 2D, 3D, character animation, stop motion, and experimental techniques. Also known for its interactive design and graphic design programs.

name: GPO Film Unit
significance: Pioneering British documentary film unit established in 1933 by John Grierson at the General Post Office. Became a hotbed for experimental animation, employing Len Lye, Norman McLaren, and Lotte Reiniger. Lye's A Colour Box (1935) and Rainbow Dance (1936) pioneered painting directly on film. McLaren's Love on the Wing (1937) demonstrated radical animation techniques. Transformed into Crown Film Unit in 1940.

name: Belvision
significance: Belgian animation studio founded December 11, 1954 by Raymond Leblanc (founder of Le Lombard publishing). Pioneering European animation studio that first adapted Tintin for television (1957), followed by Asterix, Lucky Luke, The Smurfs, and Pinocchio in Outer Space. Key studio in bringing Franco-Belgian comics to animated form.

name: Bruno Bozzetto Film
significance: Multi-award winning Italian animation studio founded by Bruno Bozzetto in Milan. Created Mr. Rossi character series (1960-1964) and the cult classic Allegro non troppo (1976), often compared to Disney's Fantasia but with satirical approach. Also produced West and Soda (1965) and VIP, My Brother Superman (1968). Bozzetto is one of Italy's most celebrated animators.

name: Bob Godfrey Films
significance: Founded by Bob Godfrey (1921-2013), 'The Godfather of British Animation.' Won Academy Award for Great (1975) about Isambard Kingdom Brunel. Created beloved British TV series Roobarb and Henry's Cat. Known for eclectic mix of techniques including cutout animation that pre-dated Terry Gilliam. Career spanned over 50 years.

name: Miyu Productions
significance: Leading French independent animation production company founded by Emmanuel-Alain Raynal (joined by Pierre Baussaron in 2015). Specializes in short films, series, and features with a sharp artistic editorial line. Studios in Paris, Valence, Angoulême (France) and Brussels (Belgium). Miyu Distribution is the global leader in international sales of animated films with 10 Oscar nominations. Works include 27 by Flora Anna Buda and Linda veut du poulet! La Galerie Miyu bridges contemporary art and animation.

name: Nelvana
significance: Canadian animation studio founded in July 1971 by Michael Hirsh, Patrick Loubert, and Clive A. Smith, named after a 1940s Canadian comic book superheroine. Saved from bankruptcy by The Care Bears Movie (1985), which grossed $23 million. Produced Rock & Rule (1983), Care Bears films and series, Babar, Franklin, and later became known for children's programming. Subsidiary of Corus Entertainment since 2000. Production halted September 2025 amid industry-wide downturn; now focuses on library licensing and distribution only.

name: Bilibili
significance: Chinese online entertainment platform launched 2009-2010 by Xu Yi, named after anime character Mikoto Misaka. Originally focused on anime, comics and gaming content. Acquired Haoliners Animation League in 2021. Major force in Chinese animation production and distribution.

name: Filem Negara Malaysia
significance: Malaysian national film organization (Malayan Film Unit) created by British colonialists in 1946 to produce documentaries and government announcements. Produced Malaysia's first in-country animation Hikayat Sang Kancil (1983), designed by Anandam Xavier. Pioneered Malaysian animation with folklore-based shorts featuring the mouse deer character. Laid groundwork for Malaysia's animation industry.

name: Kantana Animation
significance: Thai animation studio spun off as Kantana Animation Studios Company, Limited in 2007 from Kantana Group. Produced Khan Kluay (2006), Thailand's first CGI animated feature film, which took three years and cost 150 million baht ($3.9 million) to make. Khan Kluay became the top film at the Thailand box office in 2006, earning 91 million baht. Director Kompin Kemgumnird had worked on Disney's Atlantis and Tarzan, and Blue Sky's Ice Age. Also produced Khan Kluay TV series for BBTV Channel 7.

name: Light Chaser Animation
significance: Beijing-based CGI studio founded in March 2013 by Gary Wang, founder and ex-CEO of Chinese video sharing website Tudou.com. Hired former Pixar employees and aims to create world-class animated films with Chinese cultural themes. Breakthrough success with White Snake (2019), followed by Green Snake (2021) and the New Gods series. Rapidly became one of China's leading animation studios.

name: Nippon Animation
significance: Japanese animation studio established June 3, 1975 by Kōichi Motohashi, emerging from Zuiyo Eizo's production staff. Famous for the World Masterpiece Theater series adapting Western literature for young audiences, including A Dog of Flanders (1975), Anne of Green Gables (1979), and Romeo's Blue Skies (1995). Early staff included Hayao Miyazaki and Isao Takahata before they founded Studio Ghibli.

name: Mushi Production
significance: Pioneering Japanese animation studio founded in 1961 by Osamu Tezuka, the 'God of Manga,' out of rivalry with Toei Animation. Officially incorporated as Mushi Production in January 1962. Produced Japan's first weekly TV anime series Astro Boy (1963), which achieved 40.7% peak viewership and established limited animation techniques for television. Also created Kimba the White Lion and Princess Knight. Despite success, went bankrupt in 1973 but was revived in 1977. Spawned influential studios including Madhouse and Group TAC.

name: Boyana Film
significance: Bulgarian state film studio established 1962, now Nu Boyana Film Studios. During communist era produced nearly 600 features plus 400 shorts and animated films annually. Acquired by Nu Image/Millennium Films in 2005. One of largest film production complexes in Eastern Europe with extensive facilities.

name: Athanor
significance: Czech film production company founded in 1991 by surrealist filmmaker Jan Švankmajer and producer Jaromír Kallista. Located in Knovíz, 25km northwest of Prague. Produces Švankmajer's distinctive films combining live-action with animation including Alice (1988), Faust (1994), Conspirators of Pleasure (1996), Little Otik (2000), Lunacy (2005), and Insect (2018). Self-sufficient studio with own equipment.

name: Filmové studio Gottwaldov
significance: Animation studio based in Zlín (renamed Gottwaldov 1949-1990), Czechoslovakia. Followed the film production legacy of the Baťa Company from the 1930s. Home to legendary filmmakers Karel Zeman and Hermína Týrlová, the 'mother of Czech animation.' Zeman's The Fabulous World of Jules Verne is considered the most successful Czech film ever. Known for innovative mixture of animation and live-action. Laid foundations of the world-famous Czech School of Animation. After the Velvet Revolution, renamed to Ateliéry Zlín (1990), then Ateliéry Bonton Zlín (2000), which continues operating today.

name: Jiří Trnka Studio
significance: Founded in 1946 by Jiří Trnka, who had previously co-founded Bratři v triku in 1945. Trnka became the defining master of puppet animation, rivaling Walt Disney in output and international acclaim. His studio helped establish Czech animation predominance alongside Karel Zeman, Hermína Týrlová, and Jan Švankmajer. Trnka's work influenced Tim Burton and the Brothers Quay.
