After Trnka's death in 1969, the studio continued as part of Krátký Film Praha and remains active today under that umbrella, preserving rights to hundreds of classic puppet films.

name: Croatia Film
significance: Croatian film company that produced the country's first animated features during the 1980s-90s, all directed by Milan Blažeković: The Elm-Chanted Forest (1986), The Magician's Hat (1990), and Lapitch the Little Shoemaker (1997). Part of the Zagreb School of Animation tradition. Separate from Zagreb Film studio.

name: Kecskemétfilm
significance: Hungarian animation studio established in 1971 as a regional branch of Pannónia Film Studio in Kecskemét. Became independent as Kecskemétfilm Kft. in 1991 after the end of state funding. Produced beloved Hungarian series including Water-Spider Wonder-Spider, Leo and Fred, Tales of King Mathias, and Hungarian Folk Tales. Contributed animation to Oscar-nominated international productions The Secret of Kells (2009) and Chico and Rita (2010), and César Award-winning Wolfy, the Incredible Secret (2013). Also hosts the Kecskemét Animation Film Festival.

name: Ekran
significance: Soviet/Russian TV film studio founded in 1967 as Creative Association Ekran. Its Multtelefilm division focused on television animation, producing popular series like Leopold the Cat, Adventures of Funtik the Piglet, and Investigation Held by Kolobki. Alexander Tatarsky pioneered clay animation with Plasticine Crow and Last Year's Snow Was Falling. Closed after Ostankino reorganization in 2008.

name: Melnitsa Animation Studio
significance: One of Russia's largest animation studios, founded in 1999 in Saint Petersburg by producer Sergey Selyanov and Aleksandr Boyarsky. Called the 'Walt Disney of Saint Petersburg' by Deutsche Welle. Best known for The Three Bogatyrs franchise based on Russian epic heroes, with the latest sequel grossing over $32 million in Russia. First success came with Little Longnose (2003), the first post-Soviet animated feature. Two-time Oscar nominee Konstantin Bronzit serves as permanent art director.

name: Kievnauchfilm
significance: Soviet/Ukrainian film studio (Kyiv Science Film) founded in 1941 in Kyiv to produce popular science films. In 1959, Irina Gurvich, Ippolit Lazarchuk and Nina Vasilenko opened an animation workshop that became legendary. By 1991, it was the second-largest animation studio in the Soviet Union after Soyuzmultfilm, producing 150-250 minutes of animation annually. Made over 300 animated films. The animation division (Ukranimafilm) was separated after 1991. Ceased operations in 1998 amid Ukraine's economic transition.

name: DEFA
significance: Deutsche Film-Aktiengesellschaft, East German state film studio 1946-1992. Animation department produced distinctive work including silhouette animations by Lotte Reiniger and Bruno J. Böttge.

name: Mosfilm
significance: Major Soviet/Russian film studio founded in 1920. Animation department produced significant works before Soyuzmultfilm was established. Continues as Russia's largest film studio.

name: TVC London
significance: Television Cartoons London, founded in 1957. Produced The Snowman (1982), When the Wind Blows, and Yellow Submarine animation. Major British commercial and theatrical animation studio.

name: Studio Miniatur Filmowych
significance: Major Polish animation studio operating from 1958 to 2019 in Warsaw. Originally formed from the Warsaw branch of Studio Filmów Rysunkowych, it was one of five animation studios in the Polish People's Republic. Produced over 1,500 films including original short films, children's series, and feature films. Home to prominent animators including Piotr Dumała, Jan Lenica, Witold Giersz (Red and Black, Little Western), and Julian Józef Antonisz. Produced the Polish children's series alongside its sister studio SFR in Bielsko-Biała. In October 2019, the studio was incorporated into the Warsaw Documentary Film Studio. A central pillar of Polish animation history.

name: Les Films Armorial
significance: French independent film production company founded c. 1963 by producers Simon Damiani and André Valio-Cavaglione. Best known as the production company behind René Laloux's groundbreaking animated feature Fantastic Planet (La Planète Sauvage, 1973), co-produced with Československý Filmexport and animated at the Jiří Trnka Studio in Prague. Fantastic Planet won the Special Jury Prize at Cannes 1973 and remains one of the most acclaimed animated films ever made. Also produced Peter Foldes' experimental animation Appétit d'oiseau/Awakening (1965), one of the earliest computer-assisted animated films. The company also produced several of Laloux's earlier short films. Distribution was handled by Argos Films.

name: Gaumont
significance: Founded in 1895, one of the oldest film companies in the world. Animation department produced numerous French animated features. Émile Cohl made early animation there.

name: Halas and Batchelor
significance: Founded in 1940 by John Halas (Hungary) and Joy Batchelor (UK), becoming the largest animation studio in Western Europe for over 50 years. Produced over 2,000 films. Created Animal Farm (1954), the first British animated feature for theatrical release (secretly funded by the CIA). Joy Batchelor was only the second woman to direct an animated feature after Lotte Reiniger. Won international acclaim for combining entertainment with educational clarity.

name: Klasky Csupo
significance: American animation studio founded in 1982 by graphic designer Arlene Klasky and Hungarian-born animator Gábor Csupó in a spare bedroom in Hollywood. Animated the first three seasons of The Simpsons (1989-1992) and all 48 Tracey Ullman Show shorts. Created era-defining Nicktoons including Rugrats (1991), Aaahh!!! Real Monsters, The Wild Thornberrys, Rocket Power, and As Told by Ginger. The Rugrats Movie (1998) was the first non-Disney animated feature to gross over $100 million. Won five Emmy Awards. Known for distinctive angular character designs and innovative visual style.

name: Film Roman
significance: American animation studio founded October 26, 1984 by Phil Roman in Los Angeles. Best known for animating The Simpsons (seasons 4-27), King of the Hill, Family Guy, The Critic, and Garfield specials. Sold to IDT Entertainment in 2003. Acquired by Waterman Entertainment in 2015, then forfeited by California and closed in 2018.

name: Cartoon Saloon
significance: Founded in 1999 in Kilkenny. Received Academy Award nominations for all feature films: The Secret of Kells, Song of the Sea, The Breadwinner, and Wolfwalkers. Known for Celtic art influences and hand-drawn style.

name: Blue Sky Studios
significance: American computer animation studio founded February 1987 by Chris Wedge, Michael Ferraro, Carl Ludwig, Alison Brown, David Brown, and Eugene Troubetzkoy in Greenwich, Connecticut. Originally a VFX studio. Acquired by 20th Century Fox in 1997. Academy Award for Best Animated Short (Bunny, 1998). Produced Ice Age franchise (5 films, $3.2 billion worldwide), Robots (2005), Rio (2011), Epic (2013), Ferdinand (2017), and Spies in Disguise (2019). At peak employed 500+ people in Greenwich. Closed April 10, 2021 by Walt Disney Company following the 2019 Disney-Fox merger, despite staff petitions to keep it open. Assets and IPs transferred to Disney.

name: Priit Pärn Studio
significance: Estonian animator Priit Pärn, one of the most influential European animators. Known for absurdist, satirical films challenging Soviet and post-Soviet society. Won numerous festival awards.

name: Studio Ponoc
significance: Founded in 2015 by former Studio Ghibli producer Yoshiaki Nishimura. Continues hand-drawn animation tradition with Mary and the Witch's Flower. Spiritual successor to Ghibli's artistic approach.

name: CoMix Wave Films
significance: Founded in 2007. Home to director Makoto Shinkai, producing worldwide hits Your Name (2016) and Weathering with You (2019). Known for stunning photorealistic backgrounds and emotional storytelling.

name: Film Bilder
significance: Independent German animation studio (Studio FILM BILDER GmbH) founded in 1989 by Thomas Meyer-Hermann in Stuttgart. For over three decades, has produced animation in almost every format: music videos, commercials, short films, feature films, and series. Known for individual design, advanced storytelling, and close connections with internationally renowned animated film directors. Works span both artistic creation and commercial craftsmanship. One of the most prominent animation studios in Germany, closely connected to the Stuttgart animation scene including the Film Academy of Baden-Württemberg. Award-winning studio with a diverse, inventive body of work.

name: Kyoto Animation
significance: Founded in 1981, known for exceptional character animation and attention to everyday moments. Produced K-On!, Violet Evergarden, and A Silent Voice. Renowned for treating animators well and maintaining in-house production quality.

name: TMS Entertainment
significance: Founded in 1946 as one of Japan's oldest animation studios. Produced Lupin III, Detective Conan, and Anpanman. Pioneered anime-Western collaborations and international co-productions.

name: A-1 Pictures
significance: Founded in 2005 as Aniplex subsidiary. Prolific producer of popular anime including Sword Art Online, Your Lie in April, and Kaguya-sama. Known for consistent quality across diverse genres.

name: Bones
significance: Founded in 1998 by former Sunrise staff. Known for fluid action animation and original series. Produced Cowboy Bebop: The Movie, Fullmetal Alchemist, My Hero Academia, and Mob Psycho 100.

name: MAPPA
significance: Japanese animation studio founded June 14, 2011 by Masao Maruyama, co-founder and former producer of Madhouse, at age 70. Name is acronym for 'Maruyama Animation Produce Project Association.' Rapidly became one of the most prominent modern anime studios with high-quality action animation. Notable works include Attack on Titan Final Season, Jujutsu Kaisen, Chainsaw Man, Dororo, and In This Corner of the World (2016). Maruyama left in 2016 to form Studio M2; current CEO is Manabu Otsuka.

name: Walt Disney Animation Studios
significance: Founded by Walt Disney in 1923, pioneered the animated feature film with Snow White (1937). Established the 'Disney style' of character animation that influenced the entire industry. Won numerous Academy Awards and defined American animation for nearly a century.

name: Production I.G
significance: Founded in 1987. Known for Ghost in the Shell (1995), one of the most influential anime films. Produces high-quality theatrical and television animation with detailed realism and philosophical themes.

name: Warner Bros. Animation
significance: Founded in 1933, home to Looney Tunes and Merrie Melodies. Created iconic characters Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and others. Known for irreverent humor, breaking the fourth wall, and directors like Chuck Jones, Tex Avery, and Friz Freleng.

name: Sunrise
significance: Founded in 1972, known as the home of mecha anime. Created Mobile Suit Gundam franchise and Cowboy Bebop. Pioneered the 'real robot' genre that redefined Japanese animation.

name: UPA
significance: United Productions of America, founded in 1943. Revolutionized animation with limited animation technique and modernist design, breaking from Disney realism. Created Mr. Magoo and Gerald McBoing-Boing. Influenced global animation including Zagreb School.

name: Studio Ghibli
significance: Founded in 1985 by Hayao Miyazaki, Isao Takahata, and Toshio Suzuki. Internationally renowned for hand-drawn animated features with rich environmental and humanist themes. Won Academy Award for Spirited Away (2001). Known for meticulous craftsmanship, strong female protagonists, and anti-war messages.

name: Laika
significance: Founded in 2005 in Portland, Oregon, successor to Will Vinton Studios. Pioneered integration of 3D printing into stop-motion production. First stop-motion studio to shoot in stereoscopic 3D (Coraline, 2009). All five features Oscar-nominated for Best Animated Feature. Won Scientific and Technology Oscar (2016) for 3D printing innovation. Known for dark fantasy stories with exceptional craft.

name: Animafilm
significance: Romanian state animation studio founded in Bucharest in 1964, originally a department of the Alexandru Sahia Documentary Film Studio. Catalyzed by Ion Popescu-Gopo's international success — his short film A Brief History won the Short Film Palme d'Or at Cannes in 1957. Gopo's minimalist stick figure character ('Gopo's Little Man') symbolized human evolution and became an icon of Romanian animation. Pioneered Romanian animation and influenced Eastern European graphic animation style. Reorganized as a joint-stock company (Animafilm S.A.) after the fall of communism in 1991. Severely diminished post-1990: only 15 films produced between 1990–2001, reduced to 10 employees by 2004, surviving primarily on commissioned educational shorts. Effectively inactive since approximately 2005; the legal entity (Animafilm S.A.) still technically exists.

name: Se-Ma-For
significance: Founded in Łódź, Poland in 1947 as Studio Małych Form Filmowych (Studio of Small Film Forms). Known as the cradle of Polish animated film, particularly puppet animation. Collaborated with experimental filmmakers including Zbigniew Rybczyński, whose Tango (1980) won the Academy Award. Produced both children's content and avant-garde experimental films.

name: Science SARU
significance: Founded in 2013 by Masaaki Yuasa and Eunyoung Choi during production of Adventure Time episode 'Food Chain.' Known for bold, groundbreaking animation that blends logic and emotion. Produced acclaimed works including Devilman Crybaby (2018), The Night is Short Walk On Girl (2017), and Inu-Oh (2021). First major Japanese animation Kickstarter success with Kick-Heart.

name: ICAIC
significance: Instituto Cubano del Arte e Industria Cinematográficos, founded in 1959 as the first cultural body after the Cuban Revolution. Home to Juan Padrón, father of Caribbean animation, creator of Vampires in Havana (1985) and Elpidio Valdés series. Known for modernist design influenced by mid-century aesthetics. Produced cutting-edge experimental animation rivaling European studios.

name: Pilot
significance: Founded in 1988 by Alexander Tatarsky and Igor Kovalyov, becoming the first private animation studio in the Soviet Union. Known for pioneering mixed techniques including classical hand-drawn, plasticine stop-motion, and CGI integration. Produced Alexander Petrov's Oscar-nominated The Cow (1989). Aimed at both auteur and commercial animation.

name: Pannónia Filmstúdió
significance: Hungary's largest and most important animation studio, formed in 1951 and becoming independent in 1957. Produced over 700 animated films including features Son of the White Mare, Cat City, and Time Masters (co-production). Home to Marcell Jankovics, who created Hungary's first animated feature Johnny Corncob (1973). Won Palme d'Or for The Struggle (1977) and Oscar nomination for Sisyphus (1974). Known for distinctive Eastern European style blending psychedelic imagery with philosophical themes. Alumni include Gábor Csupó (Klasky Csupo co-founder). Produced beloved series Hungarian Folk Tales.

name: Bratři v triku
significance: Founded in 1945 by Jiří Trnka, Eduard Hofman, and Jiří Brdečka, becoming the cradle of Czech animation. The oldest and largest animation studio in Czech Republic, producing over 1,600 titles. Pioneered the 'Czech school' of puppet animation with poetic, artistic sensibility. Produced first Czechoslovak animated feature The Czech Year (1947). Home to masters including Trnka, Zdeněk Miler (Little Mole), and Břetislav Pojar. Believed children deserved the best artists and musicians, avoiding violence in favor of warmth and imagination.

name: Triggerfish Animation Studios
significance: Founded in 1996 in Cape Town, becoming Africa's leading animation studio. Produced South Africa's first CGI features Adventures in Zambezia (2012) and Khumba (2013), both among the country's highest-grossing films. Won Cristal awards at Annecy for Stick Man (2016) and Revolting Rhymes (2017). Oscar-nominated for Best Animated Short. Collaborates with Disney, Netflix, and BBC.

name: Zagreb Film
significance: Founded in 1953, Zagreb Film became the center of the internationally acclaimed Zagreb School of Animation. Known for stylized, anti-naturalistic animation that rejected Disney conventions, emphasizing artist individuality and graphic experimentation. Won the first non-American Oscar for animated short (Surogat, 1961). Produced over 600 animated films and trained generations of Yugoslav animators including Dušan Vukotić, Vatroslav Mimica, and Nedeljko Dragić.

name: Studio 4°C
significance: Founded in 1986 by Kōji Morimoto, Eiko Tanaka, and Yoshiharu Satō (named for the temperature at which water is densest). Known for marrying independent festival animation spirit with mainstream anime aesthetics. Produced groundbreaking films including Memories (1995), Mind Game (2004), and Tekkonkinkreet (2006). Created five segments of The Animatrix (2003). Won Japan Academy Prize for Animation of the Year for Tekkonkinkreet.
